      CU["curated"]
      ED["embedding-derived<br/>classified_as, related, covers_topic"]
      AG["agent-contributed<br/>federation reports"]
    end
    EMB["Embeddings: per-modality model registry<br/>web/models.json"]
    W["Layer 3: working property graph<br/>graph.json (served), RDF export"]
    EMB --> ED
    EMB --> AG
    SUB --> W
    CON --> W

docs.title: The three graph layers of GRAPH_STANDARDS.md
docs.text:
The decision: one RDF graph, three layers, joined by concept IRIs.

The decision record was written for medicine, the domain the atlas started with, and its wording is medical: layer 1 is "the medical concepts and entities" and layer 2 is the "clinical / multi-modal instance layer". The pattern itself is domain-agnostic. Each domain's concepts come from that field's own vocabularies and join the same graph by canonical identifier; the served graph already does this for foods (FoodOn, FoodData Central) and for general concepts (Wikipedia). Backbones and instance models for other domains are not yet written into the standard.

Layer What it is What lives in it today Status 1. Terminology / ontology backbone Concepts and entities with stable identifiers from real vocabularies, SKOS-shaped. For medical concepts MeSH is canonical and the hierarchy comes from MeSH tree numbers 3,390 nodes with a mesh: canonical id (among them 51 curated concepts, 142 MeSH tree expansions and 3,160 FoodAtlas diseases); 3,360 part_of edges from tree numbers; cross-codes; 15 code-system authority nodes; Wikipedia-grounded general concepts. See Controlled vocabularies Built 2. Clinical / multi-modal instance layer Actual records whose codings carry concept IRIs that join layer 1. For medicine, FHIR RDF R4 (ImagingStudy, Observation, Condition, …) The 13 FHIR resource types and 5 NACC record types as nodes; 36 instantiates edges saying which datasets would hold which resource. No instance records Designed 3. Working / evidence property graph What the explorer renders: datasets, measured metadata, modality, embeddings, evaluation items and results. A projection of layers 1 and 2, not a separate source of truth The served graph.json (6,187 nodes, 17,119 edges) and its RDF export in the named graph https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas Built

The join is the reason this is one graph: a FHIR coding a sct:… or a loinc:… lands on the same concept IRI as the backbone and as the mirrored external graphs. The concept IRIs in use are the rdf_iri_stem values of web/codesystems.json (RDF vocabulary).

docs.title: Source of record
docs.text: Since 2026-09-26 every triple lives in exactly one named graph, and that graph is its source of record. panAtlas curates, verifies and exports only https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas. External graphs (the NSF OKN graphs, Wikidata) are mirrored read-only under their publisher's graph IRI and replaced wholesale when their agent syncs a new upstream version. panAtlas never edits an externally maintained node or edge; it only links to it (skos:exactMatch, dataset and document annotations) from its own graph. A dataset maintained elsewhere carries maintained_externally: true and a source_of_record block (Dataset registry).

docs.title: Substrate: identity
docs.text:
The substrate is the set of canonical grounded entities: what a thing is. A node's identity is its canonical_id (mesh:D051436, fhir:Condition, chebi:15377, foodon:…). Two systems that emit the same canonical_id are talking about the same entity, with no reconciliation. Ungrounded items stay in a private namespace and do not enter the shared substrate until they are grounded. The substrate answers only "does this entity exist, and what is it?"

In the served graph 5,013 of 6,187 nodes carry a canonical_id; the prefixes in use are mesh (3,390), foodon (1,558), wikipedia (24), fdc (24) and panatlas (17, internal artifact-type vocabulary). The other 1,174 nodes (datasets, benchmarks, models and other non-concept kinds, plus 118 concepts and 10 diseases) have none; see Graph schema.

docs.title: Connectivity: claims
docs.text:
Edges are attributed claims about how the substrate relates, not identity. Many overlapping connectivity graphs can sit over one substrate, and a connectivity layer can be swapped or re-derived without touching the substrate. LAYERS.md names four origins:

Origin Examples in the served graph Marker on the edge ontology-tree part_of from MeSH tree numbers (3,360); FHIR binds (15) src: mesh_tree curated part_of from curated pages (1,845); prereq (6) src: curated embedding-derived classified_as from the corpus classification (1,749 with n_docs); related (31 with sim); benchmark covers_topic from the judge-gated item mapping (300 with n); covers_topic from arXiv lexical alignment (203) n_docs, sim, n, basis agent-contributed Edges reported over the federation by site agents claims (in agent reports)

Every edge is meant to carry an origin and evidence (for example {model, version, cosine}), so that connectivity merges as claims and conflicts surface instead of being overwritten.

The served graph does not carry origin and evidence

No edge in graph.json has an origin or evidence attribute. Provenance is partial and uses other names (src on 5,715 edges, via on 437, basis on 216); 10,863 edges carry none of the three. The attach process (below) implements the contract as one nested attribute, claims: {origin, model, version, cosine, canonical_id}, on the edges it reports.

docs.title: Embeddings and the attach process
docs.text:
Embeddings are how new items find their place in the connectivity graph. Two rules:

  1. Each modality registers its own models in web/models.json.
  2. An embedding is comparable only within one (modality, model, version) space. Cross-modality relation goes through the substrate (shared canonical_id), never through embedding arithmetic.

A registered model carries its space definition: dimension, pooling, concept anchors (one vector per grounded concept, aligned by slug and canonical_id), the optional centroid taxonomy, and the unknown cutoff. At HEAD only the text model is active (BioClinical-ModernBERT-large, version v3w-2026.07, 1024-d); the imaging entry (RAD-DINO) holds embeddings but no anchors, and genomics and structured data have no registered embedder (Models and curriculum).

The attach process (web/embed_attach.py) runs per agent, locally, in one model's space:

new item + embedding e (in model M's space)
        |  L2-normalise (and whiten with the anchors' mu/sd when present); cosine to M's anchors
        v
   top-k concepts by cosine
        |  >= M's cutoff (the whitened cutoff when whitened)?
        |-- yes -> classified_as edges, claims {origin: embedding, model, version, cosine, canonical_id}
        '-- no  -> UNKNOWN: no edge; the item stays in the agent's private namespace

Its output is connectivity, never substrate. A site's local agent (web/pa_local_agent.py) holds the graph index and embedding cache, runs attach on local embeddings, and emits a structure-only report: grounded nodes (canonical_id, kind, label), edges, and a sha256 content hash, with no documents. The report travels the federation, where entities merge by canonical_id and connectivity accumulates as attributed claims. See Distributed panAtlas and The agent contract.

Imaging model named in LAYERS.md

LAYERS.md says imaging is embedded by the LeJEPA-3D CT encoder. The registry's imaging entry is stock RAD-DINO, with anchors held. LAYERS.md also says the local agent's report is served by a separate plugin; the plugin is outside this repository and was not checked here.

docs.title: Verified, seeded and derived facts
docs.text:
panAtlas's first principle (atlas/CLAUDE.md): sources are evidence, not authority. Citing a source records where a claim was seen; it never makes the claim true. Only panAtlas verification, a human verified_by sign-off, makes a page verified. FHIR records and vocabulary assertions enter the same way, as evidence with provenance, and become panAtlas facts only after curator sign-off.

Three kinds of content therefore sit side by side, and the data marks which is which.

docs.title: Seeded: evidence waiting for verification
docs.text: Content Marker Concept pages seeded from Wikipedia status: draft, confidence: estimated, a pinned wikipedia: {title, oldid, retrieved}, and a needs-verification callout: "Wikipedia saying it does not make it true" Fact pages drafted by an agent status: draft, and the claim tagged "UNVERIFIED (agent-drafted from model knowledge; NOT yet checked against a source)" Datasets taken from the inventory built_by "from the dataset inventory; not yet measured …" (88 nodes); measured: false (116) Contamination labels that were guesses Downgraded to UNCHECKED by hygiene_enrich.py (122 dataset nodes), with the guess kept as contamination_prior Benchmark decontamination not yet run decontam.holdout_status: unchecked (85 of 106 language benchmarks)

docs.title: Derived: computed from other data
docs.text:
Content How it is derived Marker Concept hierarchy (medical concepts) MeSH tree-number prefixes part_of with src: mesh_tree Disease specialty MeSH tree number of the disease built_by: "…specialty by tree number" Corpus → concept Corpus document classification (embedding cells + LLM-judged cell labels) classified_as with n_docs Concept relatedness Cosine between concept anchors, kept at 0.72 or above related with sim Benchmark topics Item → concept mapping (judge-gated) covers_topic with n; node topics_status Benchmark grounding Rule: a benchmark reaches a MeSH-grounded concept through covers_topic, tests or covers grounded_in with via: mesh:<UI> Per-concept accuracy Per-item correctness joined to the item mapping measured_on with acc, n; eval_accuracy with ckpt Artifact type of a benchmark Rule from the task_format facet unless overridden artifact_type_via Composite model score Mean over the fixed 21-benchmark battery overall, battery_n

A derived value is only as good as its inputs, and the inputs are named on the edge or node so the value can be recomputed.

docs.title: Verified: checked, with the check recorded
docs.text:
There are two senses of "verified" in the data, and they must not be confused.

Curator verification is the verified_by sign-off that makes an atlas page status: verified. At HEAD it has not happened for any page: of the 75 typed pages in the repository's markdown atlas, 74 have status: draft and 1 (a fact) has status: in_review; none is verified. 53 carry confidence: estimated and 1 confidence: measured. No node or edge in the served graph has verified_by.

Machine verification is a recorded, repeatable check of a specific fact against its source. This is what the served graph's verified content rests on:

What Check Where recorded MeSH groundings of curated concepts UTS resolver, then one adversarial agent per concept confirming the descriptor with a live UTS call built_by on 51 concept nodes Artifact-type groundings Live NLM MeSH lookup (match=exact) and Wikipedia REST, 2026-08-08; concept-identity judge, 2026-08-09 pipeline/groundings_verified.json; grounding_match, grounding_judge Curriculum facts Every job id, config path and repository must exist in the vault (check_curriculum_vault.py, 61/61 on 2026-10-14) Curriculum verified (date and method) Dataset counts Measured on the cluster, not estimated measured: true (249 dataset nodes) Imaging and pathology results Training and evaluation verified before listing verified on result records; withheld otherwise Mirrored external graphs Fingerprint, upstream slices, independent re-extraction, store round trip PROOF.json; see RDF vocabulary

docs.title: The markdown atlas
docs.text:
The atlas in atlas/ is the git-backed fact graph where verifiable facts are written as typed markdown pages. Page types (atlas/CLAUDE.md):

Layer Page types Pages at HEAD Human-readable concept-, document- 51 concepts, 1 document Machine-readable fact-, entity- 3 facts, 4 entities Evaluation dataset-, item-, model-, result- 1 dataset, 2 items, 0 models, 0 results Registry source- 7 sources Governance dispute-, curator-, domain-, jurisdiction-, strata- 2 domains, 1 jurisdiction, 2 strata Navigation map- (maps of content) 1

Rules the linter enforces (atlas/tools/lint_panatlas.py; CI blocks on error):

  1. Every page has frontmatter with type, slug (equal to the file name), status (draft, in_review, verified, deprecated) and oneliner.
  2. Every wikilink in a frontmatter edge field resolves to an existing page.
  3. prerequisites between concepts stay acyclic.
  4. Every verified fact cites at least one registered source- page (the publish gate).
  5. Every factual bullet carries a provenance tag: src:<slug>@<ver>, conv:YYYY-MM-DD, web:<url>, wikidata:Q<id> or [[document-…]], optionally followed by (confidence: …).
  6. Held-out item answers never live in the public file.

A fact page is a typed triple: fact_type, subject, predicate, object, polarity, confidence, with about, elaborates, stated_in and cites_source edges. The predicate must be legal for the fact type, from atlas/predicates.yaml:

fact_type Predicates mechanism inhibits, activates, agonist_of, antagonist_of, causes, mediated_by association associated_with, risk_factor_for, marker_of dosage dose_is, route_is, max_dose_is contraindication contraindicated_with, avoid_in indication first_line_for, second_line_for, indicated_for diagnostic localizes_to, confirmed_by, elevated_in, seen_on temporal precedes, rises_after, peaks_at epidemiologic prevalence_in, incidence_in definitional is_a, part_of, subtype_of

Edges live on the owning end only: a fact owns its elaborates, about and stated_in edges, and concept, entity and document pages receive them through generated reverse-index blocks that are never hand-edited.

build_layered.py reads the atlas concept pages (atlas/20-concepts/*.md) to build the concept layer of the served graph: the page's concept_kind sets the node kind (map becomes specialty, the Medicine page becomes root, a gate page becomes gate), and its prerequisites become prereq edges. The verified MeSH mapping then supplies the canonical identity and the hierarchy. The 51 concept pages at HEAD are the medical curriculum, so root is the root of that curriculum, not of the atlas: the atlas itself sits under atlas-root, with one domain node per top-level field (Graph schema).

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft: seeded from a source or drafted
    draft --> in_review: grounded against a registered source
    in_review --> verified: curator sign-off (verified_by)
    verified --> deprecated: superseded
    draft --> deprecated

docs.title: The problem panAtlas exists to solve
docs.text:
Multi-modal models are hard to evaluate, and a single general score is the wrong instrument. What "good" means changes with the domain (a dermatology read is nothing like an ECG forecast) and, inside a domain, with the context: geography, culture, population, environment, care setting and equipment. A model that reads skin lesions well on one skin type can fail on another; a triage model tuned on one country's intensive-care data can misfire in a field clinic elsewhere. One leaderboard number hides exactly that variance. The plan's conclusion is that evaluation has to be structured by domain and stratified by context, and that this cannot be done without first mapping the domain (PLAN.md §1).

panAtlas is that map. It is a provenance-first knowledge graph that links the parts of an evaluation to each other:

  • concepts of every field, grounded in that field's own vocabularies (MeSH for medicine, Wikidata and others across fields) and arranged as a curriculum, from foundations up through specialties and subspecialties;
  • datasets, the corpora that models are trained on and the sets they are tested on, each registered once with a global identifier and an audit manifest;
  • models, with what they were trained on (their curriculum) and what they were evaluated on;
  • benchmarks, with what they measure, how to read their metric, and every score the atlas holds for them;
  • the documents behind all of it (about 93 million training, evaluation and reference documents on the 2026-09-24 count), each placed by concept.

panAtlas covers every domain, not one field. Medicine holds the most data today: most of the registered datasets, the MeSH grounding and the specialty curriculum are medical, because that is where the work started. The graph, the identifiers, the dataset managers and the federation are domain-agnostic, and other domains are built the same way medicine was: ground the field's concepts in its own vocabularies, register its datasets, models and benchmarks, and attach them to the same graph. Parts of the metadata layer (competency frameworks, the education ladder, stratification standards) are medicine-shaped today, and each new domain gets its own parallels (PLAN.md §2).

The atlas is meant to evaluate humans and AI against the same points: an expert taking a quiz on a concept and a model graded through a controlled interface. That assessment surface is designed and not deployed (see What panAtlas is not). What runs today is the evaluation of models.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text: Reader What they use Researchers choosing or comparing models The explorer at panatlas.net, the public API, and the Astral agent Engineers extending the atlas The build pipeline, the registries, the repository map Sites that hold data The Cresco federation: a dataset joins where it sits (Distributed) Curators The markdown fact-graph and its verification rules (Architecture) Other agents and language-model clients tools.json from the public API, and the SPARQL store through Astral

docs.title: Provenance first: sources are evidence, not authority
docs.text:
Every factual statement carries a provenance tag that says where it was seen. The markdown fact-graph enforces a tag on every factual bullet (atlas/CLAUDE.md, rule 5), in one of a fixed set of forms (src:<slug>@<ver>, conv:YYYY-MM-DD, web:<url>, wikidata:Q<id>, or a link to a document- page).

Citing a source does not make a claim true. Wikipedia, a clinical guideline, an ontology: each is a registered source, recorded as a source- page with publisher, version strategy and licence, and the plan says plainly that "registration is not endorsement" (PLAN.md §5). A claim becomes verified only through a human curator's sign-off (verified_by). Seeding never verifies anything.

The same rule runs through the generated layers. Contamination labels that were never measured are downgraded to UNCHECKED rather than shown as clean (web/hygiene_enrich.py); a model's curriculum entry records the SLURM jobs, configuration and codebase of each training stage (web/pipeline/model_curriculum.json); a dataset is identified by a URN and audited by a manifest hash (Manifests).

docs.title: Describe once, evaluate many times
docs.text:
The project names this as its evaluation policy: describe once, evaluate many (DOEM) times.

Definition not yet written down

The name and its framing are on record; a formal definition is not. The statements below describe how the current code behaves, which is the closest thing to a definition today. They are not a policy text.

In the code, a thing is described once and then reused by every evaluation that touches it:

  • a dataset is registered once in web/datasets.json (schema panatlas.datasets/1), keyed by URN, and every graph node, manager report and public API record refers to that entry (Dataset registry);
  • a benchmark is a node with its metric, what it measures and how to read it, and every model's score attaches to that node (Benchmarks);
  • every measured score, for every model type, sits in one index (data/evals_index.json, built by web/build_evals_index.py) that the site, the API and its clients all read (Evaluation records).

docs.title: Blanks are tracked as rigorously as facts
docs.text:
An unknown is recorded as an unknown, in the same field that would hold the value, so that it can be counted, compared and closed. Examples from the code and records:

  • curriculum_disclosed: false on external models: "we do not know what this model was trained on" becomes a recorded, comparable property (web/build_curriculum.py, Models and curriculum).
  • The training-provenance gap register (docs/curriculum-gap-register.md) lists every blank that stops a full account of how a model was built, with a severity and a named recovery lead for each.
  • Coverage is stamped honestly: record-level topic joins report the share of documents they cover (55.89 % for one pretraining corpus, 43.35 % for another, 2026-08-08) and list uncovered sources instead of blending them in (web/build_record_level.py).
  • Registered-but-unscored models are listed with the reason they were not run (listed_not_run in the public API), and every evaluation response states what the atlas covers, "so a missed search cannot read as missing data" (docs/public-api.md).

docs.title: Measure, date, and say which it is
docs.text: Counts shown on the site and in these docs are read from the deployed data or the source, not estimated. Every statement of status says whether a thing is designed, built, or measured, and a measured number carries its date. Claims are kept as narrow as the evidence: the exact-match contamination check, for example, is reported as "no verbatim-document matches" and not as freedom from near-duplicate leakage (docs/panatlas-system-and-interface.md §D.3).

docs.title: Wikipedia seeds; it is never the verified layer
docs.text:
Wikipedia is used three ways, none of them as an authority:

  1. Seed. atlas/tools/seed_wikipedia.py writes a concept page pinned to an article revision (oldid), at status: draft, with a CC BY-SA attribution block and a needs-verification callout.
  2. Overlay. MeSH is canonical over Wikipedia. A concept in MeSH has MeSH as its source of record; Wikipedia is at most a human-readable overlay, and is the identity only for genuinely non-MeSH nodes (GRAPH_STANDARDS.md).
  3. Coverage measure. The Wikipedia world-view layer (run 20260901) links every document to one primary article with an evidence class, which lets the atlas say how much of the known world its documents cover and where it holds no evidence at all (Web site, Astral).

docs.title: Experts curate
docs.text: People, not pipelines, decide what is verified. Curators sign in with their ORCID iD. The role model is viewer, domain editor, reviewer and super curator, with capabilities pa_read, pa_suggest, pa_edit, pa_verify and pa_admin (web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/panatlas-explorer.php). Today a proposal is recorded for a curator to act on and never auto-publishes; the target design moves verification to a reviewed and merged pull request (Architecture).

docs.title: Structure travels; data stays
docs.text: A dataset joins the atlas where it sits, under its owner's control. Only structure (identifiers, counts, edges, hashes) crosses the federation; documents, pixels, embeddings and anything carrying protected health information never do. See Distributed.

docs.title: Exact or not at all
docs.text: A mirror or a store counts only when it is proven to recreate its source exactly. Each NSF Open Knowledge Network mirror is proven against its upstream, and each SPARQL store must round-trip every graph exactly before it is switched live (Knowledge store).

docs.title: Licence is a per-document attribute
docs.text: The atlas ingests what it needs and records the licence of each document at ingest; the licence is consulted when documents are shared or put into a training set (web/acquisition/arxiv/arxiv_doc_index.py, web/licence/). Restricted and credentialed datasets are catalogued, never served (Acquisition and licence).

docs.title: What panAtlas is not
docs.text:
It is not Why A single leaderboard Each benchmark keeps its own metric, and values are compared only within one benchmark (docs/public-api.md, rules). Rankings across benchmarks are mean positions, stated as such. A data host Datasets are link-only. The public API lists every record and serves no data. Restricted data is metadata only. An authority by citation A registered source is evidence. Verification is a curator's act. A Wikipedia mirror Wikipedia seeds drafts and measures coverage; MeSH is canonical. An open wiki Viewing the explorer is gated to an allowlist today, and edits go through proposals (see Web site). The assessment platform, yet "Test yourself" quizzes, per-person mastery, gates, disputes and adaptive testing are designed in PLAN.md and not deployed (docs/panatlas-system-and-interface.md, Part A). A finished federation The substrate supports federation and the mesh runs; no external site contributes yet (Distributed).

Scope statements from the plan

"Most extensive reference for multi-modal evaluation" is the long-term aim, not a current claim. The plan describes the defensible novelty at small scale as structural: a provenance-grounded, graph-structured, context-stratified evaluation atlas in which the reference corpus and the evaluation scaffold are the same network (PLAN.md §2).

docs.title: panAtlas is a distributed system
docs.text:
panAtlas runs on Cresco, the hierarchical agent mesh, and that matters more than any other fact about how it is built. Shared infrastructure means shared datasets and one global understanding of them: a dataset joins the atlas where it sits, under its owner's control, and from then on it is known, linked and findable by every participant and every agent on the mesh. The data itself does not move.

This section explains how that works, from the mesh up.

docs.title: The idea in one picture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph SiteA["Site holding data (e.g. the HPC cluster)"]
    D1[(dataset A)] --- M1[manager A<br/>cresco-panatlas]
    D2[(dataset B)] --- M2[manager B<br/>cresco-panatlas]
    M1 & M2 --- AG1[Cresco agent]
  end
  subgraph SiteB["Participating site"]
    D3[(local graph +<br/>embeddings)] --- LA[local agent<br/>pa_local_agent.py] --- M3[cresco-panatlas] --- AG2[Cresco agent]
  end
  subgraph Mesh["Cresco mesh (region panatlas-global)"]
    G[global controller]
  end
  AG1 -- "MsgEvent, mTLS" --> G
  AG2 -- "MsgEvent, mTLS" --> G
  G -- "getgraphinventory<br/>(pycrescolib)" --> HUB
  subgraph Hub["panAtlas hub (web host)"]
    HUB[mesh daemon +<br/>hub merge] --> GJ[graph.json / mesh.json] --> SITE[panatlas.net]
  end

Only structure crosses the mesh: identifiers, counts, edges, model stamps and hashes. Documents, pixels, embeddings and anything carrying protected data (protected health information, for example) or licensed text never do. That rule is enforced in code at three points (the report builder, the Cresco plugin and the hub merge), so a misconfigured source can not leak.

docs.title: What is distributed
docs.text:
Part Where it runs What it does Status Dataset managers One cresco-panatlas plugin instance per dataset, on the Cresco agent at the site that holds the data Serves that dataset's structure-only report (getgraphmanifest, getgraphinventory), stamped with its URN and manifest_hash Built, running. Measured on the mesh: 22 (2026-07-31), 33 (2026-09-17), 65 (2026-09-20) Knowledge-graph agents One agent per mirrored NSF Open Knowledge Network graph (okn_agent.py), each also a registered dataset with its own manager Tracks its upstream graph's version and provenance, syncs it independently, and declares its source of record Built. 42 graphs on 2026-09-26, 43 from 2026-10-02 Participating agents Any Cresco node that joins the region and runs cresco-panatlas, usually with the local agent kit Contributes its own grounded subgraph; trust tier and admin status decide whether it merges Built and documented. No external site contributes yet The hub The web host's Cresco agent + mesh_daemon.py + the site Pulls every manager's report over the control plane, shows datasets per node in the Mesh view, folds permitted contributions into the graph Built. Pull runs every 15 s Supervision systemd units on the HPC cluster login node and the web host Restarts wedged agents, re-adds missing managers, rebuilds manifests hourly Built, with a guard for each of the six recorded outages; see Operations Storage GaiaKeep, the global file system for agents, on the same mesh (storage core release 1.3, 2026-10-01) The intended durable, versioned backend for panAtlas datasets; the panAtlas index estate is among the candidates for GaiaKeep's first real data GaiaKeep built; the panAtlas binding measured and designed, nothing stored yet; see Storage on GaiaKeep

What is built and what is designed

Every claim in this section says which it is. The pull path (hub → global controller → manager, over MsgEvent) is built, deployed and measured. The original HTTP submission endpoint (POST /federate), push change-notifications on the data plane, signed reports and hub-to-hub peering are designed, not built. Federation lists each one.

docs.title: Why Cresco
docs.text:
panAtlas does not build its own transport, identity or trust. Cresco already provides:

  • a global → region → agent hierarchy that rolls inventories up the tree;
  • a certificate-bound identity for every node, admitted by an authenticated discovery exchange (a join secret in the standard profile, the operator's PKI in production), with mutual TLS on every broker connection;
  • end-to-end, recipient-bound message authentication and signed plugin installs, on by default since the Cresco 1.3 hardening;
  • per-tenant isolation in the broker;
  • a control plane (MsgEvent RPC) and a data plane (pub/sub topics);
  • self-describing plugin actions that any client, or any AI agent, can call as tools.

Federation therefore needs only one plugin, cresco-panatlas, plus a hub-side client. The same mesh carries GaiaKeep storage and other workloads, so a site that joins for one purpose can share datasets with the atlas with no new infrastructure. Cresco for panAtlas explains the parts used.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. Cresco for panAtlas: the mesh concepts this design relies on.
  2. Federation model: join keys, trust tiers, merge rules, what crosses the wire.
  3. Dataset managers: one manager per dataset, the hub's pull loop, the Mesh view.
  4. Participating agents: the plugin internals, the local agent kit, and how a new site connects.
  5. Wire contract and schemas: every field of every message and file on the federation path.
  6. Operations: supervision units, failure modes and recovery runbooks.
  7. Storage on GaiaKeep: how the index estate binds to the archive on the same mesh.

docs.title: Participating agents
docs.text:
A participating agent is a Cresco node that runs the cresco-panatlas plugin and contributes its own grounded, structure-only subgraph to panAtlas. The hub's own dataset managers are participating agents of a special kind (one plugin instance per dataset, configured by the hub). This page covers the plugin itself, the local agent kit an outside site uses to build its report, the steps for connecting a new site, and the admin portal that lets it in.

Sources: ThePanAtlas/cresco-panatlas (plugin), ThePanAtlas/agent-deployment (onboarding kit and contract), web/federation/ and web/dgx/pa_local_agent.py in the hub repository.

docs.title: The cresco-panatlas plugin
docs.text:
An OSGi bundle (io.cresco.panatlas, version 0.1-SNAPSHOT) modelled on the Cresco skeleton plugin. Four classes:

Class Role Activator Minimal bundle activator. The service is registered through Declarative Services Plugin @Component with ConfigurationPolicy.REQUIRE and ServiceScope.PROTOTYPE, so every configured instance is a separate plugin. It waits until the agent is active, then logs PanAtlas federation reporter active on <region>_<agent> ExecutorImpl Dispatches EXEC messages by their action parameter. Annotated @CrescoCapabilities(namespace = "panatlas", target = "plugin"), so its actions appear in the mesh capability inventory. All other message types return null GraphReporter Loads the report, enforces the contract, stamps identity and computes the hash

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Action Parameters Returns Use getgraphmanifest none agent_id, node_count, edge_count, content_hash (or error) Cheap change check before a full pull getgraphinventory since_hash (optional) report (compressed JSON) and content_hash. If since_hash equals the current hash: unchanged = "true" and content_hash only. On failure: error Full report pull by the hub

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text:
Key Required Meaning pluginname yes io.cresco.panatlas panatlas_source effectively Path to the report JSON on the agent's filesystem. If it is unset or missing, the plugin logs a warning and reports an empty subgraph panatlas_graph_version no Copied into the report's graph_version. Default unversioned panatlas_dataset_id hub managers The dataset URN (panatlas:dataset:<slug>). The hub finds managers by this key panatlas_modalities hub managers Comma-separated modalities panatlas_model.<modality> hub managers The registered model@version per modality. Non-scalar model descriptions are serialised as compact JSON, because Cresco plugin configuration must be flat scalars panatlas_manifest hub managers Path to the dataset's manifest file persistence_code no 10 asks the agent to restore the instance after a restart. The hub leaves it unset; see Operations

The plugin reads only panatlas_source and panatlas_graph_version. The other keys exist so that an instance describes itself in the controller's plugin listing, where the hub finds its URN.

docs.title: What the reporter does on each call
docs.text:
1. Identity: agent_id = "agent-" + region + "_" + agent from the Cresco plugin builder.
  2. Load panatlas_source if it exists, then walk the whole tree and throw on any forbidden field name (text, body, raw, content, document, excerpt, abstract, case-insensitive) at any depth.
  3. Take nodes and edges (empty arrays if absent).
  4. Build the reply object: agent_id, graph_version, generator = "cresco-panatlas/0.1", nodes, edges.
  5. content_hash = "sha256:" + SHA-256( JSON(nodes) ‖ JSON(edges) ), the two serialisations concatenated.

content_hash is not comparable across implementations

Three components compute a content_hash, and they canonicalise differently:

  • Plugin (Java): SHA-256 of nodes bytes concatenated with edges bytes. Jackson's ORDER_MAP_ENTRIES_BY_KEYS does not reorder the keys of an already-parsed ObjectNode, so key order follows the source file.
  • Validator (pa_agent.py): SHA-256 of {"nodes": …, "edges": …} with sorted keys and compact separators.
  • Local agent (pa_local_agent.py): SHA-256 of the same object with sorted keys and default separators.

Each hash is stable for its own producer, so change detection (since_hash) works. The same subgraph does not hash to the same value across the three, so do not compare hashes between them.

Plugin README status line is out of date

The cresco-panatlas README still says "Not yet run on a live mesh". The bundle has served the hub's dataset managers on the live mesh since 2026-07-31.

docs.title: Build and deploy
docs.text:
# JDK 21, Maven, and io.cresco:library:1.3-SNAPSHOT installed locally (build CrescoEdge/library first)
mvn package bundle:bundle        # -> target/panatlas-0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar

Deploy the bundle to a running agent through the Cresco controller (plugin upload, then add an instance with its configuration). The hub does this with pycrescolib in web/mesh/deploy_managers.py; see Dataset managers. On a Cresco build with the 1.3 secure defaults, an uploaded jar is installed only if it is signed and verifies against the agent's plugin_signing_truststore (Signed plugins). The bundle is not signed today; see Cresco for panAtlas.

docs.title: The local agent kit
docs.text:
A site that is not the hub builds its report with the local agent: pa_local_agent.py, pure NumPy and the standard library. It keeps the site's graph index and embedding cache on the site, and only the structure-only report leaves it.

Store layout (default ~/.panatlas-agent):

config.json                     agent_id, site, model, created
cache/  models.json             the hub's model registry (cached)
        <model>.npz             concept anchors for the site's model
index/  nodes.json              id -> {canonical_id, kind, label, grounding}
        by_canonical.json       canonical_id -> id
        concepts.json           concept -> member ids (from part_of / classified_as / covers edges; 5,000 per concept)
        adjacency.json          id -> [{to, rel, cosine?, model?}]
reports/report.json             the structure-only report for the plugin

Commands:

Command Arguments Does init --agent-id, --site, --model, --models, --anchors, --now Creates the store and caches the model registry and anchors index --graph Indexes the site's graph (nodes and edges in report form) attach --embeddings (.npy [m, d]), --ids, --topk (default 3) Relates new embeddings to concepts through the cached anchors and adds classified_as edges with cosine and model report --version (default local) Writes reports/report.json: grounded nodes only (canonical_id, kind, label), every edge, claims = {origin: "embedding", cosine, model} on attach edges, and a content_hash. Runs the structure-only check status Prints the store, index, cache and report state serve --graph, --version, --interval (default 5 s) Watches the graph file and re-indexes and re-reports when it changes

Attach (embed_attach.py) L2-normalises the embeddings and anchors, computes cosine similarity, keeps the top k concepts at or above the model's cutoff and emits classified_as edges carrying {origin, model, version, cosine, canonical_id}. Anything below the cutoff is reported as unknown, with its best cosine and no edge. build-anchors mints a model's anchors as an .npz (vecs, slug, canonical_id plus model, version, dim): one vector per grounded concept, the mean of its passage embeddings.

The published kit is behind the hub repository

agent-deployment/agent/ holds older copies of pa_local_agent.py, embed_attach.py and models.json. The hub copies (web/dgx/pa_local_agent.py, web/embed_attach.py, web/models.json) add the model-space guard: attach takes the embedding model's identifier and raises MODEL-SPACE MISMATCH if it differs from the anchors' model. The kit's attach checks only the dimension, although CONNECTING.md already describes the guard. The kit's models.json also lists an older imaging model. Sync the kit from the hub before onboarding a site. The kit's Cresco links (crescoedge.github.io/quickstart/…) also return 404; the documentation is now at crescoedge.github.io/docs/. Its examples/cresco.env names the identity keys regionName and agentName; Cresco's parameters are regionname and agentname (Configuration), which is how the panAtlas unit files set them.

docs.title: Connecting a new site
docs.text:
The end-to-end path from agent-deployment/CONNECTING.md:

flowchart LR
  A[1 Register<br/>admin creates profile] --> B[2 Join the mesh<br/>join secret, mTLS]
  B --> C[3 Bind dataset<br/>+ model per modality]
  C --> D[4 Get anchors<br/>for that exact model]
  D --> E[5 Index + attach<br/>local, structure-only]
  E --> F[6 Deploy plugin<br/>panatlas_source]
  F --> G[7 Hub pulls + merges<br/>tier and status gated]
  G --> H[8 Verify + operate]
  1. Register and be permitted. Send the request form (examples/register-request.md): display name, purpose, institution, host, optional URL, owner name and ORCID, a private contact email, the vocabularies your identifiers use, approximate node and edge counts, and the dataset, modalities and registered model per modality. You receive your region and agent names (identity agent-<region>_<agent>), your tenant, your starting tier, your status (pending until an admin permits you) and the discovery join secret for your tier.
  2. Join the mesh. Configure and start a Cresco agent (examples/cresco.env): its region and agent names, regional_controller_host, is_global=false and the join secret for your tier (discovery_secret_agent). Keep the secret in an owner-only file or a CRESCO_<NAME> environment variable, not on the command line (Deployment). The kit also sets broker_security_enabled, broker_require_client_auth and tenant_namespacing to true, with the comment "turn ON for a real medical federation". In Cresco 1.3 those three are already the defaults (Secure defaults) and apply to every federation, whatever its domain. The kit's fourth setting, security_regional_ca=true, is opt-in regional-CA enrollment, available in the standard profile only (Security profiles).
  3. Bind your dataset and models. One plugin instance is one dataset. Declare panatlas_dataset_id, panatlas_modalities and panatlas_model.<modality> for each stream, choosing the most specific registered model that applies.
  4. Get the anchors for the exact model you use, distributed with the registry and versioned with the model. Cache them with init.
  5. Index and attach with the local agent, then report.
  6. Deploy the plugin, pointing panatlas_source at ~/.panatlas-agent/reports/report.json.
  7. The hub pulls and merges: substrate by canonical_id, connectivity per model space, gated by tier and status. A model not registered for its modality is quarantined. See Federation.
  8. Verify and operate. getgraphmanifest returns your identity, counts and hash. Keep serve running so the report follows your graph. When a model version changes, re-embed and re-attach in the new space; old edges are marked superseded. A new dataset is a new plugin instance.

Troubleshooting (from CONNECTING.md):

Symptom Cause and fix Report has 0 edges No embeddings attached yet, or attach refused a model mismatch Edges quarantined at the hub The declared model is not registered for that modality Nothing merges status is not active, or the join or mTLS enrollment failed. Cresco's own refusals and their fixes are in Cresco troubleshooting MODEL-SPACE MISMATCH Embeddings from one model attached to another model's anchors

docs.title: The admin portal
docs.text:
The site's explorer plugin includes a federation admin portal (includes/federation-admin.php): a WordPress admin page plus three REST routes in the panatlas/v1 namespace. The registry it maintains, wp-content/uploads/panatlas/federation/agents.json, is the same file merge_reports.py reads.

Method Route Permission Does GET /federate/agents public The agent directory. The public view drops private{} and reduces token to its prefix. An admin sees full profiles but never the token hash POST /federate/agents/register pa_admin Creates a profile (agent_id must match ^agent-[a-z0-9-]+$; 409 if it exists). Tier defaults to provisional, status is always pending. Mints a token pat_ + 40 characters, stores only its 10-character prefix and SHA-256, and returns the plain token once POST /federate/agents/update pa_admin Sets tier and/or status, or rotate: true to mint a new token (returned once). Stamps updated_at

The admin page lists agents with Permit (set active), Suspend and Revoke. Every register and update is written to the site audit log (panatlas_audit, events fed_register and fed_update).

What the token is for

Tokens were designed for the HTTP submission route (POST /federate), which is not built. On the Cresco path, identity comes from the mesh (the node's certificate, admitted with its join secret and checked by mutual TLS), and the registry's tier and status gate the merge.

docs.title: Wire contract and schemas
docs.text:
Every message and file on the federation path, field by field. Schemas are the files in web/federation/ (copied unchanged into agent-deployment/contract/; the two copies are identical at repo HEAD). Where the code writes something the schema does not describe, this page says so.

Artifact Produced by Consumed by Section Agent report (report.schema.json) Participating agents, pa_local_agent.py, pa_agent.py The plugin, merge_reports.py Agent report Dataset-manager report build_dataset_reports.py The plugin, mesh_daemon.py Dataset-manager report Manager instance configuration build_dataset_reports.py deploy_managers.py, the Cresco agent Instance configuration Plugin MsgEvent replies cresco-panatlas The hub MsgEvent actions Agent profile (agent_profile.schema.json) The admin portal The directory, merge_reports.py Agent profile merged_federation.json merge_reports.py build_layered.py Merge output mesh.json mesh_daemon.py The site's Mesh view Mesh state models.json Hub maintainers Local agents, attach, the hub merge Model registry

docs.title: Agent report
docs.text:
report.schema.json, JSON Schema draft 2020-12, $id https://panatlas.net/federation/report.schema.json. Top-level additionalProperties: false.

Field Type Required Meaning agent_id string, ^agent-[a-z0-9-]+$ yes The reporting agent reported_at string, date-time yes The agent's own clock at report time. pa_agent.py takes it from --reported-at graph_version string yes The agent's version label for this snapshot, e.g. 2026.07.29-1, or a manifest_hash for dataset managers content_hash string, ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ yes Hash of the node and edge set. Snapshots are idempotent by this value. See the hashing caveat generator string no Producer and version: pa_agent/0.1, pa_local_agent/0.1, cresco-panatlas/0.1 nodes array of node yes edges array of edge yes

Node (additionalProperties: false; must have canonical_id or local_id):

Field Type Meaning canonical_id string The grounding join key, e.g. mesh:D051436. Required for the node to merge local_id string Agent-local identifier for an ungrounded node. Namespaced at the hub as fed:<agent_id>:<local_id>; the design text also writes <agent_id>:local:<local_id>. Never enters the MeSH tree label string, max 200 Human-readable name kind string Node kind: disease, concept, cluster, … Free text; the merge defaults to concept grounding enum mesh, mesh_broader, fhir, chebi, foodon, fdc, snomed, loinc, rxnorm, umls, wikipedia, none host string Where the node's data lives claims object of number, integer, string or boolean Counts, enums and flags only (e.g. n_docs, modality, n_subtopics, cos_to_anchor). Never text

Edge (additionalProperties: false):

Field Type Required Meaning from string yes A canonical_id, a base-graph node id, or an agent-namespaced id to string yes Same rel string yes Relation, e.g. part_of, classified_as, covers claims object of scalars no For attach edges: origin: "embedding", model, version, cosine, canonical_id. Only cosine and model survive the merge, as evidence

Forbidden anywhere (schema $comment, enforced in code): text, body, raw, content, document, excerpt, and in code also abstract.

Example (web/federation/agent_report_example.json, abridged):

{
  "agent_id": "agent-site-kos",
  "reported_at": "2026-07-29T18:00:00Z",
  "graph_version": "2026.07.29-1",
  "content_hash": "sha256:…",
  "generator": "pa_agent/0.1",
  "nodes": [
    {"canonical_id": "mesh:D051436", "kind": "disease", "grounding": "mesh",
     "label": "Renal Insufficiency, Chronic", "claims": {"n_docs": 12043, "modality": "text"}},
    {"local_id": "run-2026-07-29-cluster-3187", "kind": "cluster", "grounding": "none",
     "label": "CKD dietary-management cluster", "claims": {"n_docs": 4210, "cos_to_anchor": 0.41}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from": "mesh:D051436", "to": "concept-nephrology", "rel": "part_of", "claims": {}},
    {"from": "agent-site-kos:local:run-2026-07-29-cluster-3187", "to": "mesh:D051436",
     "rel": "classified_as", "claims": {"weight": 0.62}}
  ]
}

Cresco identities do not match the agent_id pattern

The plugin stamps agent_id = "agent-<region>_<agent>", which contains an underscore. Both the schema pattern and the admin portal's registration check (^agent-[a-z0-9-]+$) reject underscores. A Cresco agent therefore cannot be registered under its own mesh identity, and merge_reports.py would treat its reports as coming from an unknown (provisional, pending) agent. One of the two rules has to change before an outside site's reports merge automatically; registering with - in place of _ is the stop-gap.

docs.title: Dataset-manager report
docs.text:
<slug>.report.json, written by web/build_dataset_reports.py. This shape is not report.schema.json. It uses id/type nodes and source/target edges, and the hub reads it directly.

Top-level field Type Meaning urn string The dataset URN, panatlas:dataset:<slug> nodes array The dataset node, then modality, model and vocabulary nodes edges array Structural edges from the dataset node

Nodes:

type id Other fields dataset (one) the URN label (registry name), modality (list), host, access, item_count, file_count, manifest_hash modality modality:<m> label model model:<model> label, modality. Datasets whose model is null (a pending encoder) get no model node vocab vocab:<v> label. <v> is each of mesh, umls, foodatlas, fdc, nacc, v628 found as a substring of the registry's grounding text; ungrounded if none

item_count is the first of these registry scale keys that is present: volumes, studies, entities, foods, worklist_cases, axial_cases, papers. file_count and manifest_hash come from the registry manifest. Field meanings are in Dataset registry and Manifests.

Edges (source, target, rel): has_modality (dataset → modality), embedded_by (dataset → model), grounds_to (dataset → vocab).

An optional <slug>/grounded.json ({nodes: [], edges: []}) layers grounded concept connectivity into the report.

docs.title: Manager instance configuration
docs.text:
<slug>.instance.json, one per dataset. Every value is a flat scalar.

Key Value pluginname io.cresco.panatlas jarfile panatlas-0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar. Dropped at deploy; the uploaded jar's pluginname, md5 and version are merged in instead panatlas_dataset_id panatlas:dataset:<slug> panatlas_modalities Registry modalities, comma-joined panatlas_source <reports dir>/<slug>.report.json panatlas_manifest <reports dir>/<slug>.manifest.json panatlas_graph_version The dataset's manifest_hash at generation time, or unversioned panatlas_model.<modality> The registered model for that modality. Object-valued models are serialised as compact sorted JSON (from 2026-09-20; before then the agent refused six such instances) persistence_code Added only when PANATLAS_PERSIST=1 ("10")

docs.title: MsgEvent actions
docs.text:
Both actions are EXEC MsgEvents addressed to panatlas-global / <agent> / <plugin_id> with parameter action. Neither action declares roles in its @CrescoAction annotation, so on a Cresco build with the 1.3 secure defaults, which callers may run them is Cresco's default for an action without roles (Security in Cresco 1.3).

Action Request params Reply params getgraphmanifest none agent_id, node_count (string integer), edge_count (string integer), content_hash; or error getgraphinventory since_hash (optional) report (compressed string; decode with pycrescolib.utils.decompress_param) and content_hash; or unchanged = "true" and content_hash; or error

The decoded report is the source file's nodes and edges wrapped as {agent_id, graph_version, generator, nodes, edges, content_hash}. A dataset-manager report's own urn key is not carried into the reply; the dataset node's id holds the URN.

docs.title: Agent profile
docs.text:
agent_profile.schema.json. One registered agent, stored in agents.json as {"agents": [ … ]} under the site's uploads directory.

Field Type Visibility Meaning agent_id string, ^agent-[a-z0-9-]+$ public Identity (required) display_name string ≤ 120 public Required purpose string ≤ 500 public What the agent reports and why institution string ≤ 160 public host string public Where it runs url string public Homepage or repository owner_name string ≤ 120 public Required owner_orcid string or null, ORCID pattern public Owner's ORCID iD tier trusted | provisional public Required. See Federation status active | suspended | revoked public Required registered_at date-time public Required updated_at date-time or null public last_report_at string or null public last_content_hash string or null public stats object of integers public Per-agent counters token.prefix string public First 10 characters of the token: an identifier, not a secret token.sha256 64 hex admin-only, never served Hash of the token. The plaintext is shown once and never stored token.rotated_at string or null admin private.contact_email, private.phone, private.notes string or null admin-only Never returned by the public directory

What the portal writes differs from the schema

panatlas_fed_register also stores modalities (a list, not in the schema, which forbids extra properties). It sets status to pending, a value the schema's enum lacks but the portal and merge_reports.py both use. It writes timestamps in MySQL format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), not ISO 8601 date-time. Treat the schema as describing the public fields and the portal as authoritative for stored values.

docs.title: Merge output
docs.text:
web/federation/merged_federation.json, written by merge_reports.py and read by build_layered.py.

Node: id (fed:<canonical_id> or fed:<agent_id>:<local_id>), canonical_id (or null), kind, label, grounding (mesh or null), federation_status (visible | pending), reported_by (list of agent ids), origin (federation).

Edge: from, to, rel, origin (federation), federation_status, reported_by (list), and evidence ({cosine, model}) when the reported edge had those claims.

Run statistics (printed, not stored): reports, rejected_not_active, matched_existing, new_nodes, new_edges, dup_edges, by_tier.

docs.title: Mesh state: mesh.json
docs.text:
Written every 1.5 s by mesh_daemon.py into the explorer plugin's data/ directory and served to the Mesh view.

Field Meaning nodes[] node (region_agent), region, role (global | region | agent), addrs, ageMs (on the injected global node), datasets[] nodes[].datasets[] One per manager answering on that agent: urn, name, modality, item_count, manifest_hash (first 19 characters) edges[] from, to, rtt (ms), cost, conns. A …_parent target is rewritten to the global node routes Reserved, always empty source push (fresh route_lsa link-state advertisements) or poll (getnetworkstate fallback) ok Always true when written counts nodes, agents, globals, links, datasets updated_epoch Unix seconds of the write

The global node is injected by the daemon, because a node's own route view omits itself. A mesh.json with only the global node, no agents and 0 datasets means the daemon is writing but cannot see the mesh.

addrs is served publicly

mesh.json is a static file on the public site, and addrs carries each node's network address and discovery port. Strip or mask addrs in the daemon before the file is written if the mesh topology should not be public.

docs.title: Model registry: models.json
docs.text:
The per-modality embedding-model registry, web/models.json. Its top-level _note states the rule: an embedding is comparable only within one (modality, model, version) space; cross-modality relation goes through shared canonical_id.

Structure: modalities.<modality>.models[] (plus an optional note), and predictors.

Embedding model fields (the union over registered models):

Field Meaning id Registry identifier, used as the plugin's panatlas_model.<modality> value and the anchor cache name family Model family and lineage modality text, imaging-ct, … role general, or a specialised role applies_to Which data the model covers dim Embedding dimension version Space version (e.g. v3w-2026.07: the v3 mean-pool pipeline plus whitening) pooling, max_length, dtype, normalize, similarity How embeddings are produced and compared whitening Background population used to whiten. The calibrated whitened_cutoff travels in the anchor artifact cutoff Raw-space attach cutoff (0.25 for text). null means no attach cutoff_note How cutoff relates to whitened_cutoff location, model_location Where the weights live on the cluster anchors {artifact, source, aligned_by}; for imaging {status: "held", decision, node_linkage}: image embeddings are not linked directly to concept nodes centroids {artifact, n_cells, dim}: the corpus cell centroids embeddings For imaging: cache, per-slice shape, count, materialized, id_scheme, coverage, catalog, role status active, or a descriptive status for retrieval-only spaces hf Hugging Face repository of the stock weights provenance How the weights were verified (e.g. SHA-256 equal to the hub's LFS object) and whether they were fine-tuned in-house training_disclosed Whether the training data is disclosed license Weights licence note Free-text caveats

At repo HEAD: text has one active model (text-bioclinical-modernbert-large, 1024-d, v3w-2026.07, cutoff 0.25). imaging has imaging-rad-dino-ct (768-d, retrieval only, anchors held). genomics and structured have no registered embedder.

Predictors (predictors.models[], 58 at HEAD: 37 time-series and 21 tabular; 45 foundation models and 13 baselines; 46 evaluated and 12 not run). These have no embedding space and are never attached. Fields: id, name, family, kind, role, source, embedding (none), open_weights, runs, status, results (dataset URN → pointer into web/predictor_evals.json), wrapper, and not_run_reason and note where they apply. Evaluation metadata is in Evaluation records.

docs.title: Local agent configuration
docs.text: ~/.panatlas-agent/config.json: agent_id, site, model (a registry id), created. The other store files are listed in Participating agents.

docs.title: Cresco for panAtlas
docs.text: This page covers only the parts of Cresco that panAtlas depends on, and how panAtlas uses each one. The canonical reference is the Cresco documentation; where a statement here and that site differ on how Cresco works, the Cresco site is right. Where panAtlas's own deployment is configured differently from Cresco's defaults, this page says so. Cresco's own summary of panAtlas is on its Projects built on Cresco page.

docs.title: The hierarchy
docs.text:
A Cresco node is a JVM running an OSGi (Apache Felix) host that loads the controller and a set of plugins. Each node runs in one controller mode: AGENT (a leaf), REGION (a regional controller running an embedded ActiveMQ broker, not yet federated to a global), REGION_GLOBAL (a regional controller federated up to a global), GLOBAL (federates regions, and is also its own region and agent), or STANDALONE. Agents are JMS clients of their region's broker. Regions bridge to the global, and globals can bridge to each other (Architecture overview).

The panAtlas fabric is one region, panatlas-global, with a global controller and two agents. Both agents start with is_agent=true and a fixed regional_controller_host pointing at the controller node:

Node Mode Role in panAtlas global controller GLOBAL / region root The rollup point. Inventories roll up here, and the hub's calls to managers on other agents are routed through it HPC cluster agent AGENT Hosts the dataset managers for every dataset stored on the cluster: 194 of the 200 entries in web/datasets.json at repo HEAD web host agent AGENT, wsapi enabled Hosts the hub's client side (mesh_daemon.py, deploy_managers.py); can host managers for datasets stored on the web host

Every node addresses every other by region_agent[_plugin], so a dataset manager is addressed as panatlas-global / <agent> / <plugin_id>.

docs.title: The two planes
docs.text:
Plane Carrier panAtlas uses it for Control plane MsgEvent over ActiveMQ queues Every manager call: getgraphmanifest, getgraphinventory; deploying and removing manager instances; getnetworkstate for the Mesh view Data plane ActiveMQ topics (pub/sub) The live Mesh view subscribes to the route_lsa link-state advertisements that every controller publishes on the GLOBAL topic (Data plane). The designed panatlas.graph change topic is not built (see Federation)

Reports are small. In 2026-07 the full set of structure-only reports was about 40 KB. They ride the control plane as a compressed MsgEvent parameter. The data plane and filerepo are kept for large artifacts. That split is deliberate and was learned the hard way: see Operations.

docs.title: Plugins and self-describing actions
docs.text:
A Cresco plugin is an OSGi bundle. cresco-panatlas (io.cresco.panatlas) is built from the Cresco skeleton plugin. Its executor carries @CrescoCapabilities and its actions @CrescoAction annotations, so they appear in the mesh-wide capability inventory (getcapabilityinventory) with their parameters and return types. That makes every dataset manager callable as a tool by any Cresco client, including an AI agent using Cresco's tool interface (Plugin actions).

A plugin can run as many instances on one agent, each with its own configuration. panAtlas relies on that: one bundle, one instance per dataset, each configured with a different panatlas_dataset_id and panatlas_source.

docs.title: Identity, trust and tenancy
docs.text:
Cresco 1.3 is secure by default: a node started with no security setting runs with mutual TLS, broker authorization, tenant namespacing, end-to-end message authentication and signed plugin installs (Security in Cresco 1.3, Secure defaults). The table maps each panAtlas need to the Cresco mechanism that meets it. What a panAtlas node needs to run under those defaults is in Version and security build.

panAtlas need Cresco mechanism A node's identity Messages address a node as region_agent. The identity itself is the node's X.509 certificate subject, CN=<agent>, OU=<region>, O=<tenant>, verified at every TLS handshake. The plugin stamps reports agent-<region>_<agent> Admission to the mesh An authenticated discovery exchange. In the standard security profile it is keyed by the per-tier join secret (discovery_secret_global, _region, _agent); in the production profile it is signed under the operator's PKI and no join secret is used (Discovery, Security profiles, Operator PKI). panAtlas's agents join with join secrets Authenticated transport Mutual TLS on every broker connection, with the connection bound to the identity its certificate names; optional regional-CA enrollment (security_regional_ca, standard profile only) (Security & Identity) Authenticated messages Every MsgEvent a node originates is authenticated end to end and bound to its recipient (cresco_sig_to), so a manager's reply or a call to a manager is accepted only by the node it names (Message authentication) Trusted plugin code A plugin jar installed over the network must be signed by a signer that chains to plugin_signing_truststore (Signed plugins). See Version and security build Keeping tenants apart Tenant namespacing in the broker (T.<tenant>.*), with the tenant bound into the certificate as O=<tenant> (Multi-tenancy) Who may contribute to the graph panAtlas's own overlay: the agent profile, trust tier and admin status. See Federation

Cresco answers "is this really node X, and may it talk to me?" panAtlas answers "may node X's claims enter the atlas, and are they shown at once or held for a curator?"

docs.title: Clients: the wsapi and pycrescolib
docs.text:
Cresco's external clients connect to the wsapi plugin, a secure WebSocket API on port 8282 (wss://). In Cresco's reference topology the global serves clients; panAtlas's configuration also runs wsapi on the web host agent (enable_wsapi=true), so the hub's Python code connects locally (localhost:8282). It uses pycrescolib with the wsapi service key, the legacy credential that Cresco's standard profile still accepts and its production profile refuses (API authentication):

pycrescolib call Used by For agents.list_plugin_agent(region, agent) mesh_daemon.py, deploy_managers.py List plugin instances; filter pluginname == io.cresco.panatlas messaging.global_plugin_msgevent(True, "EXEC", {"action": "getgraphinventory"}, region, agent, plugin_id) both Pull one manager's report (RPC, waits for the reply) messaging.global_controller_msgevent(True, "EXEC", {"action": "getnetworkstate"}, ...) mesh_daemon.py Nodes and links for the Mesh view (polling fallback) get_dataplane("cresco_msg_type='route_lsa'", cb) mesh_daemon.py Subscribe to pushed link-state advertisements (live path) agents.upload_plugin_agent, add_plugin_agent, remove_plugin_agent deploy_managers.py Ship the bundle, create or remove manager instances utils.decompress_param both Decode the compressed report parameter

docs.title: State: the embedded Derby database
docs.text: Each controller keeps nodes, plugins, edges and health in an embedded Derby database (controller), under cresco-data/ in the node's working directory; Cresco's Deployment page says two nodes must never share that directory. That database sits behind three of the six recorded federation outages: stale lock files after an unclean JVM exit (the cluster agent's working directory is on a shared parallel filesystem), duplicated persisted plugin records, and a second Derby engine started by a second filerepo bundle. Operations covers each one and the guard now in place.

docs.title: Version and security build
docs.text:
Both panAtlas agents run a Cresco 1.3-SNAPSHOT agent jar (agent-1.3-SNAPSHOT.jar) on a Java 21 runtime. The plugin builds against io.cresco:library:1.3-SNAPSHOT with JDK 21 and Maven (mvn package bundle:bundle → target/panatlas-0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar).

Running panAtlas under Cresco 1.3 secure defaults

Under the secure defaults a node refuses an unsigned plugin upload, so the cresco-panatlas bundle must be signed and each agent given a plugin_signing_truststore. Keep every secret in an owner-only file or a CRESCO_<NAME> environment variable rather than a -D property, and give the hub's pycrescolib client the wsapi certificate fingerprint, because current pycrescolib releases verify the wsapi certificate by default. The full procedure is Cresco's Upgrading to 1.3 and API authentication.

docs.title: Dataset managers
docs.text:
Every dataset in the registry is managed by its own cresco-panatlas plugin instance, running on the Cresco agent at the site that hosts the dataset. A manager owns exactly one dataset. It serves that dataset's grounded, structure-only report, stamped with the dataset's URN and manifest_hash, and the hub reaches it over Cresco messaging (Cresco MsgEvents): no cron scrape and no raw HTTP.

This is what "a dataset joins the atlas where it sits" means in practice: the data stays on the cluster, the manager sits next to it, and the atlas knows the dataset through the manager.

docs.title: The life of a manager
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant REG as datasets.json<br/>(HPC cluster)
  participant REF as panatlas-refresh<br/>(hourly, HPC)
  participant FS as cresco/reports/<br/>(HPC cluster)
  participant ENS as ensure-managers<br/>(15 min, web host)
  participant AG as Cresco agent<br/>(HPC cluster)
  participant MGR as manager instance<br/>io.cresco.panatlas
  participant D as mesh_daemon<br/>(web host)
  REF->>REG: dataset_manifest.py build --update-registry
  REF->>FS: build_dataset_reports.py --host (cluster)
  Note over FS: <slug>.report.json<br/><slug>.manifest.json<br/><slug>.instance.json
  ENS->>AG: upload_plugin_agent(panatlas.jar)
  ENS->>MGR: probe getgraphinventory (liveness)
  ENS->>AG: add_plugin_agent(instance.json) for missing or dead ones
  ENS->>MGR: verify every manager answers (exit 3 if not)
  loop every 15 s
    D->>AG: list_plugin_agent(panatlas-global, agent)
    D->>MGR: EXEC getgraphinventory
    MGR->>FS: read panatlas_source, enforce structure-only, hash
    MGR-->>D: report (compressed), content_hash
  end
  D->>D: attach datasets to their node in mesh.json

docs.title: 1. Registry and manifest (hourly, HPC cluster)
docs.text:
panatlas-refresh.timer (15 min after boot, then hourly) runs two steps in the cluster's panAtlas directory:

python3 dataset_manifest.py build --registry datasets.json --root <cluster project storage> \
        --out cresco/manifests --update-registry
python3 build_dataset_reports.py --registry datasets.json --out <cluster project storage>/panatlas/cresco/reports \
        --host <cluster host>

The first rebuilds every dataset's manifest and writes the new manifest_hash into the registry. The second regenerates every cluster-hosted manager's payload.

The hourly job rebuilds, it does not audit

build --update-registry makes whatever is on disk the new baseline. Drift (a moved, grown or edited file) changes manifest_hash silently instead of failing, and nothing on a schedule calls dataset_manifest.py audit (exit 0 match, exit 3 drift). The design documents also say the hub checks a reported manifest_hash against the registry and quarantines on mismatch; merge_reports.py does not. To detect drift, run audit before the rebuild. See Manifests.

A full re-walk of the very large CT corpus runs separately, weekly, as a Slurm job (panatlas-ct-rewalk.timer, Sundays 03:00), and its partitions are re-derived without another walk.

docs.title: 2. The payload triplet
docs.text:
web/build_dataset_reports.py writes three files per dataset, flat, named by slug:

File Content Read by <slug>.report.json The structure-only subgraph: the dataset node, one node per modality, one per model@version, one per grounding vocabulary, and the edges between them The manager, at every call <slug>.manifest.json The dataset's audit manifest, copied from the registry Audit; panatlas_manifest config key <slug>.instance.json The plugin configuration for this dataset's manager deploy_managers.py

The layout is flat rather than one directory per dataset because filerepo catalogued files by basename, and recursive sub-directories collided. The slug in the filename and the URN inside each file keep identity unambiguous. Field-level schemas are in Wire contract.

The report skeleton is deliberately minimal and grounded: which modalities the dataset has, which registered model embeds each, which vocabularies ground it. Grounded concept connectivity (embedding attach in the dataset's model space) is layered in per dataset by dropping a <slug>/grounded.json that is merged into the report. CT-RATE's imaging anchors were planned first.

docs.title: 3. Deployment and self-healing (every 15 min, web host)
docs.text:
panatlas-ensure-managers.timer (10 min after boot, then every 15 min) runs ensure_managers.sh, which runs web/mesh/deploy_managers.py:

  1. Upload the bundle (panatlas.jar) to the cluster agent and read its coordinates (pluginname, md5, version).
  2. List existing managers and map each dataset URN to its plugin_id, by finding panatlas:dataset: in the instance's configparams.
  3. Probe liveness. Send every listed manager getgraphinventory. A manager that is listed but does not answer is removed and re-added. Presence is not liveness: see Operations. PANATLAS_NO_PROBE=1 skips this step for a fast pass.
  4. Add missing managers. For every *.instance.json whose report's dataset host is this agent, add an instance unless one for that URN exists (--replace removes and re-adds). The script merges the uploaded jar's coordinates into the configuration. Persistence (persistence_code=10) is off unless PANATLAS_PERSIST=1. The timer, not the agent, guarantees that managers come back.
  5. Verify. Wait 5 s, re-list, probe every manager this run is responsible for, and exit 3 if any does not answer. The script does not trust add replies: on 2026-09-24 to 09-26 every add returned {}, the script printed "deployed 94" and exited 0 every 15 minutes, and the site showed 0 datasets for two days.
  6. On exit 3, ensure_managers.sh restarts the web host's Cresco agent, retries once and restarts the mesh daemon. A one-hour cooldown stops a fault on the cluster side from turning this into a restart loop.

Running deploy_managers.py by hand is safe at any time. It is idempotent by URN.

docs.title: 4. Serving (on every call)
docs.text:
The manager does no work until it is called. On each getgraphmanifest or getgraphinventory it re-reads panatlas_source, enforces the structure-only contract, recomputes content_hash and replies. A refreshed report is therefore served at the next call without redeploying the manager.

graph_version is fixed at deploy time

The report's graph_version comes from the instance configuration (panatlas_graph_version, set to the dataset's manifest_hash when the instance was created). The dataset node inside the report carries the current manifest_hash from the hourly refresh. After a manifest changes, the two disagree until the manager is redeployed with --replace. Treat the dataset node's manifest_hash as authoritative.

docs.title: 5. The hub's pull loop (web host)
docs.text:
web/mesh/mesh_daemon.py runs as panatlas-mesh.service on the web host and keeps mesh.json current for the site's Mesh view:

Every It does continuously Subscribes to route_lsa link-state advertisements on the data plane (the live path). Advertisements older than 60 s are dropped 3 s Polls the global controller's getnetworkstate (fallback when there are no fresh advertisements) 15 s Lists io.cresco.panatlas instances on each manager-hosting agent, pulls getgraphinventory from each, takes the type == "dataset" node, deduplicates by URN and groups datasets by agent 1.5 s Writes mesh.json atomically (temp file, then rename)

On any connection failure the daemon keeps the last good dataset map, so a short outage does not blank the view. Restarting the daemon resets that map, so a low count just after a restart is expected. A count that stays at 0 is the listed-but-not-answering failure.

docs.title: Scale on the mesh
docs.text:
Date Managers answering Event 2026-07-31 22 (21 on the cluster agent, nacc on the web host) First deployment, MsgEvent pull replaces filerepo 2026-09-12 33 Ten renal and two neuropathology datasets integrated 2026-09-17 33 After the persisted-plugin runaway was fixed.
