At repo HEAD the registry holds 200 entries: 194 hosted on the HPC cluster, 1 on the web host and 5 with no host (not deployable). 46 of them are Open Knowledge Network graphs. See Dataset registry.

docs.title: Knowledge-graph agents
docs.text:
The NSF Open Knowledge Network mirror applies the same idea to external graphs (web/acquisition/okn/okn_agent.py, owner order 2026-09-26). Each connected graph is its own panAtlas agent, with:

  • its own version state (pav:version, pav:lastUpdatedOn, dct:modified and VoID counts from the upstream okn-void graph) and an independent update cycle: tick checks every agent and submits one Slurm sync per changed graph;
  • its own provenance (title, homepage, funding award, licence, endpoints and authoritative namespaces, from the upstream registry);
  • a declared source of record. Every triple from graph G is asserted by okn:G@<version>. Every node is maintained by the graph whose authoritative namespace covers it. panAtlas curates only nodes and edges whose source of record is panAtlas. Mirrored content is read-only and replaced wholesale when its agent syncs a new version;
  • a registry entry (panatlas_entry.json), which makes it a dataset with its own manager on the mesh.

Per-agent state lives under data/sources_staging/okn/agents/<sn>/ (state.json, provenance.json, sor.json, check.json, panatlas_entry.json). See Acquisition and Knowledge store.

docs.title: Federation model
docs.text:
Federation is how independent sites contribute to one canonical panAtlas without giving up their data. The design decisions were locked on 2026-07-29 (FEDERATION.md):

  • Hub-and-spoke topology: one canonical hub (panatlas.net), many agents.
  • Structure and metadata only: no raw documents, no protected health information.
  • Tiered trust: trusted agents are visible on arrival, provisional agents are queued as claims.
  • Cresco as the base framework, with the reporter written as a native Cresco plugin.

docs.title: Join keys: the ontology is the protocol
docs.text:
Every grounded panAtlas node carries a canonical identifier from its field's own vocabulary: mesh:D051436 for a medical concept, a FHIR code, a ChEBI or FoodOn identifier for a chemical or a food, a Wikipedia identity for a general concept. Those identifiers are the join keys of federation, in every domain. Two agents that both emit mesh:D051436 are provably describing the same concept, so their contributions merge with no reconciliation step.

A node with no canonical identifier is ungrounded. It carries a local_id, is namespaced to its agent, and never enters the shared concept hierarchy (for medical concepts, the MeSH tree). See Identifiers and Code systems for the identifier schemes.

docs.title: Substrate and connectivity
docs.text:
Two kinds of contribution are kept apart throughout (LAYERS.md, agent-deployment/CONNECTING.md):

Substrate Connectivity What Entity identity: grounded nodes keyed by canonical_id Relationships: edges between nodes How it merges By identity. An existing entity is deduplicated and never duplicated As attributed claims layered on top, each edge carrying reported_by Conflicts Base identity and label win Conflicting claims are kept side by side, never overwritten

docs.title: The model-space rule
docs.text:
Embeddings are comparable only within one registered (modality, model, version) space. Dimension equality is not enough; the model identifier is the real guard. Relations across models or modalities go through shared grounding (canonical_id), never through cosine similarity across spaces.

  • The hub's model registry (web/models.json) lists the registered model or models per modality, each with its anchors and its cutoff. Fields are in Wire contract.
  • The attach step (web/embed_attach.py) refuses to attach embeddings whose declared model differs from the anchors' model (MODEL-SPACE MISMATCH), and raises on a dimension mismatch.
  • A stream declared with a model the registry does not know for that modality has its edges quarantined at the hub. The grounded identifiers still merge.
  • Each site uses the most specific registered model that applies to a stream (a specialised encoder where one exists, else the modality's general model) and records it.

docs.title: Trust tiers and status
docs.text:
Cresco decides whether a node may join the mesh. panAtlas decides whether its claims may enter the atlas. Two independent fields on the agent profile control that:

Field Values Effect tier trusted Contributions merge into the visible graph immediately, attributed to the agent provisional (default) Contributions land as federation_status: pending: hidden by default, held for a curator. A provisional agent can never add a new node to the concept hierarchy (FEDERATION.md names the MeSH tree) without a valid canonical_id status pending (on registration) Registered but not permitted. Nothing merges active Permitted. Only active agents contribute suspended, revoked Contributions stop merging at once

An agent missing from the registry is treated as provisional and pending, so nothing it sends merges. Admins set tier and status in the federation admin portal on the site (see Participating agents).

docs.title: What crosses the wire
docs.text:
Crosses Never crosses Dataset descriptor (URN, name, modality, item and file counts, manifest_hash, access tier) Documents, report text, abstracts Grounded canonical identifiers and labels (labels capped at 200 characters) Pixels, volumes, signals Edges (from, to, rel) and numeric or enumerated claims Embeddings Model stamps (model@version) and similarity scores on attach edges Anything under a data use agreement, PHI or licence-restricted content content_hash, graph_version, agent_id Credentials (a join secret stays with the site; a token is shown once at minting)

Enforcement, defence in depth. These field names are rejected anywhere in a payload, at any depth: text, body, raw, content, document, excerpt, abstract. The check runs in four places:

  1. web/build_dataset_reports.py refuses to write such a report;
  2. the local agent (pa_local_agent.py) refuses to emit one;
  3. the cresco-panatlas plugin (GraphReporter.assertStructureOnly) refuses to serve one and reports an error;
  4. the validator web/federation/pa_agent.py refuses to submit one.

claims values are restricted to numbers, strings and booleans by report.schema.json.

docs.title: How the hub merges
docs.text:
The hub-side merge is web/federation/merge_reports.py. It reads the current graph.json, a directory of agent reports and the agent registry, and writes merged_federation.json: the new nodes and edges to add, each attributed and tier-gated. web/build_layered.py then folds in the visible ones when it compiles the graph.

flowchart TD
  R[agent report] --> S{agent status<br/>== active?}
  S -- no --> X[rejected_not_active<br/>nothing merges]
  S -- yes --> T{tier}
  T -- trusted --> V[federation_status = visible]
  T -- provisional --> P[federation_status = pending]
  V & P --> N{node canonical_id<br/>already in graph?}
  N -- yes --> E[matched_existing:<br/>no new node, edges attach]
  N -- no, grounded --> F["create fed:<canonical_id>"]
  N -- no, ungrounded --> L["create fed:<agent>:<local_id>"]

The rules, as merge_reports.py implements them:

  1. Gate. A report from an agent whose status is not active contributes nothing (stats.rejected_not_active).
  2. Resolve each identifier in this order: an existing graph node id → that node; an existing canonical_id → the node that carries it; otherwise fed:<agent_id>:<id>, namespaced to the agent.
  3. Nodes. A node whose canonical_id is already in the graph is an existing entity (matched_existing): its edges attach and no duplicate is created. A new grounded node becomes fed:<canonical_id>. A new ungrounded node is namespaced to the agent. New nodes carry federation_status, reported_by: [agent] and origin: "federation". grounding is set to mesh when the identifier starts with mesh:.
  4. Edge endpoints. An endpoint that resolves to a fed: identifier with no node gets a minimal node (kind cluster for local: identifiers, else concept).
  5. Edges are deduplicated on (from, to, rel). An edge already in the base graph is dropped (dup_edges). When several agents report the same new edge, the edge keeps one record and reported_by lists every agent. Only cosine and model survive from an edge's claims, as evidence.
  6. Visibility. build_layered.py adds only federation_status == "visible" nodes and edges to the served graph and records the counts as federation.visible_nodes and federation.visible_edges in the build stats. Pending claims stay in merged_federation.json for curator review.

Design versus code: claims_by_agent

FEDERATION.md §5 says each agent's claims{} attach to the merged node as claims_by_agent[agent_id]. The merge code does not carry node claims. It records attribution (reported_by) and keeps only cosine and model from edge claims. Node-level claims from agents are currently dropped at merge.

docs.title: Two report shapes on the federation path
docs.text:
Two producers emit reports in different shapes. Both pass through the same plugin.

Producer Node keys Edge keys Validates against report.schema.json? Participating agents (pa_local_agent.py, own pipelines) canonical_id or local_id, kind, label, grounding, host, claims from, to, rel, claims Yes, the intended shape. The local agent omits reported_at, which the schema requires, so the validator adds it at submission Dataset managers (build_dataset_reports.py) id, type, label, modality, host, access, item_count, file_count, manifest_hash source, target, rel No. The hub reads these directly (mesh_daemon.py looks for type == "dataset"). They are not passed through merge_reports.py

Wire contract documents both shapes field by field.

docs.title: Designed, not built
docs.text: Item Where designed State at repo HEAD POST /panatlas/v1/federate (HTTP snapshot submission with a bearer token) FEDERATION.md §3, §6; pa_agent.py --submit Not built. The site registers only /federate/agents, /federate/agents/register and /federate/agents/update. Pending claims are held in merged_federation.json Signed reports, delta reports, consume-back, hub-to-hub peering FEDERATION.md Phase 3 Not built Raw-data transfer between trusted nodes cresco-panatlas README Designed as a separate, explicit path over filerepo and the data plane, gated by tenant and tier. Never part of a report. Not built

docs.title: Where this is going
docs.text: The direction (owner, 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-25) is that remote panAtlas instances and computational resources are peers on the same mesh. A dataset registered at any site, through the manager beside it, is known and linked everywhere while it stays at the site under its owner's control. The pieces that exist today, a manager per dataset, a global rollup and attributed merge by canonical identifier, are what that rests on. Peering between hubs is the Phase 3 item above.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: How the two panAtlas Cresco agents are supervised, what has gone wrong, and how to recover. Every guard on this page exists because of a specific outage. Sources: web/mesh/deploy/ (units, scripts, README) and the dated incident records. This page covers panAtlas's own deployment; Cresco's refusals and their fixes (start-up, message-signature, discovery and dataplane problems) are in Cresco troubleshooting, and Cresco's deployment guidance in Deployment.

docs.title: Standing rules
docs.text:
• Nothing heavy runs on the HPC cluster login node. The cluster agent runs there under the user's own systemd, and so does the scheduling (squeue, sacct, sbatch). Everything else, including manifest walks, store builds and queries, runs in a Slurm job. CPU jobs go to a CPU partition so they never hold a GPU node.
  • One filerepo bundle per agent: the system one. Never deploy a second.
  • Persistence off for managers. The ensure timer brings managers back, not the agent.
  • Presence is not liveness. A manager is up only if it answers getgraphinventory.
  • Verify, do not trust replies. An empty add reply proves nothing either way. Re-list and probe.

docs.title: HPC cluster (login node, systemd --user with linger)
docs.text:
The cluster has no root access and cron there was unreliable, so supervision uses user systemd with linger enabled.

Unit Schedule Does panatlas-agent.service always (Restart=always, RestartSec=8) Runs the Cresco agent (-Dis_agent=true -Dregionname=panatlas-global). ExecStartPre deletes stale Derby db.lck and dbex.lck panatlas-agent-watchdog.timer → .service every 5 min dgx-agent-watchdog.sh: restart the agent if its log gained Derby/DBEngine errors in the last 15 min and it was not restarted in the last 30 panatlas-refresh.timer → .service 15 min after boot, then hourly Manifest rebuild (dataset_manifest.py build --update-registry, which overwrites the registry baseline; it does not run audit) and report regeneration (build_dataset_reports.py) panatlas-ct-rewalk.timer → .service Sundays 03:00 Submits the CT corpus full re-walk as a Slurm job (ct_native_manifest.sbatch)

JVM hardening on the agent (also in dgx-start.sh, kept only as a manual-start reference): -Xss512k -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=256m -XX:+UseG1GC, LimitSTACK=8388608 (8 MB) and LimitNOFILE=65536. The login node uses strict memory overcommit. An inherited unlimited stack let a thread leak turn into a fatal native-thread out-of-memory error, and capping per-thread stacks prevents that.

Enable once:

export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u)
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now panatlas-agent.service panatlas-agent-watchdog.timer \
                               panatlas-refresh.timer panatlas-ct-rewalk.timer

docs.title: Web host (system systemd)
docs.text: Unit Schedule Does cresco.service + override.conf always (Restart=on-failure) The web host's Cresco agent with the wsapi enabled. The override adds the same -Xss512k and LimitSTACK hardening panatlas-mesh.service always mesh_daemon.py: writes mesh.json for the Mesh view panatlas-ensure-managers.timer → .service 10 min after boot, then every 15 min ensure_managers.sh → deploy_managers.py: probe, re-add, verify; self-heal on exit 3. Log: ensure-managers.log beside the script

docs.title: Failure modes and their guards
docs.text: Six federation outages are on record. Each one produced a guard that is still in place.

docs.title: A second filerepo bundle
docs.text:
When: 2026-07-31. Symptom: the cluster agent crash-looped and dropped off the mesh, leaving 1 of 22 managers reachable.

Cause: reports were first shipped over a second, patched io.cresco.filerepo bundle beside the agent's system filerepo. That put two Derby engines, in two OSGi class loaders, on the same database. They fought over the boot about 2.7 times a second and leaked a derby.rawStoreDaemon thread each time, reaching about 32,000 threads and OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread. The old watchdog, pgrep -f "agentname=…", matched its own shell wrapper, so it always "found" the dead agent.

Guard: reports moved to MsgEvent pull (getgraphinventory). filerepo is for large artifacts only, through the single system bundle. Supervision moved from cron to systemd.

Recovery if rawStoreDaemon threads climb:

  1. Confirm with cat /proc/<pid>/task/*/comm | grep -c rawStoreD (comm is truncated to derby.rawStoreD).
  2. Remove any non-system io.cresco.filerepo instance or panatlas-reports pipeline.
  3. Restart the agent. Orphaned Derby threads do not die when the plugin is removed.
  4. Managers return through the ensure timer.

docs.title: Stale Derby locks (the wedge)
docs.text:
When: 2026-09-10 and overnight 2026-09-16/17. Symptom: the agent JVM stays alive and its health check keeps printing OK, but the controller database will not boot ("Another instance of Derby may have already booted the database"). The agent drops off the mesh and its managers are not restored (21 of 33 came back on 2026-09-17).

Cause: the controller's Derby database (under cresco-data/ in the agent's working directory) sits on a shared parallel filesystem. After an unclean JVM exit, the next start finds db.lck and dbex.lck and refuses to boot.

Guard: ExecStartPre removes both lock files. systemd runs it only after the previous main process is gone, so no live instance can hold them. The 5-minute watchdog restarts the agent once per 30-minute cooldown when Derby errors reappear, and logs to cresco/watchdog.log.

docs.title: Persisted-plugin runaway
docs.text:
When: found 2026-09-17. Symptom: after a restart the agent began starting 4,971 panAtlas manager instances (33 intended) at about three a second. Threads passed 4,300 and the Mesh view fell to 21 datasets.

Cause: with persistence_code=10, every controller re-initialisation inside the JVM (which happens when the regional connection drops and Derby re-boots) persisted the manager instances again.

Guard: the poisoned database was set aside and the agent started fresh (79 threads, no plugin restore). deploy_managers.py no longer sets persistence_code unless PANATLAS_PERSIST=1. The 15-minute ensure timer re-adds missing managers instead, and it is idempotent by URN. Verified the same day: 33 datasets on the mesh, threads stable at 116, 0 errors.

docs.title: Listed but not answering
docs.text:
When: 2026-09-20. Symptom: after a watchdog restart, the regional controller kept listing all 65 managers while messaging to them was dead (getgraphinventory failed 6 of 6 probes). The Mesh view fell from 33 to 0 datasets, and the ensure timer reported "deployed 0" every 15 minutes, because its idempotency check asked only whether the URN was listed.

Guard: deploy_managers.py probes every listed manager, removes the ones that do not answer, and re-adds them. Verified: 65 re-added, mesh back to 65, zero connection failures.

docs.title: The silent refresh outage
docs.text:
When: 2026-09-20 17:01 to 2026-09-23. Symptom: none visible. The timer stayed active, but every hourly refresh failed, and no registry manifest moved for three days.

Cause: six directories named like manifest files, written by a fold script on 2026-09-18, made the manifest builder raise IsADirectoryError.

Guard: the builder now moves such directories aside and continues. Refresh is back to 95 manifests in 15 s. Watch the refresh log's output, not just whether the timer is active.

docs.title: Adds that silently failed
docs.text:
When: 2026-09-24 to 09-26. Symptom: the site showed 0 datasets for two days while the ensure timer printed "deployed 94" and exited 0 every 15 minutes.

Cause: under a "known connection failure" on the web host agent, every add_plugin_agent returned {}. An empty reply had also accompanied successful adds on 09-23, so it could not be read either way.

Guard: deploy_managers.py ends by re-listing and probing every manager it is responsible for, and exits 3 if any does not answer. On exit 3, ensure_managers.sh restarts the web host agent, retries once and restarts the mesh daemon, with a one-hour cooldown.

docs.title: Runbook: the Mesh view shows 0 datasets
docs.text:
1. Read mesh.json. If it holds only the global node (counts.agents = 0), the daemon is running but sees no agents: check the agents first. If agents are present but datasets = 0, the managers are not answering.
  2. Cluster agent. systemctl --user status panatlas-agent.service; look in cresco/watchdog.log and the agent log for DBEngine or Derby errors; count rawStoreD threads (see above).
  3. Restart it if needed: systemctl --user restart panatlas-agent.service.
  4. Managers: on the web host, run deploy_managers.py from the mesh virtual environment (or wait for the timer). It must end with [verify] N of N managers answer.
  5. View: systemctl restart panatlas-mesh.service. The count rebuilds over the next 15 s pull cycles.

docs.title: Runbook: add a dataset to the mesh
docs.text:
1. Register the dataset in the cluster's datasets.json with its host, locations and embedding_models. See Dataset registry.
  2. Build its manifest (dataset_manifest.py build), or wait for the hourly refresh.
  3. Regenerate the payloads (build_dataset_reports.py --host <cluster host>).
  4. Copy the new <slug>.{report,manifest,instance}.json to the web host's reports directory, where deploy_managers.py reads instance files.
  5. Run deploy_managers.py <slug>, or wait 15 minutes. Confirm the dataset in the Mesh view.

docs.title: Storage on GaiaKeep
docs.text:
GaiaKeep (GaiaKeep GFS) is a global file system built for agents, running over the same Cresco mesh. Its job is to keep versioned datasets durable and to stream any version wherever it is needed. Its durable tier encrypts blocks at the origin and places them across independent sites, on memory, NVMe, disk or tape. Durability is chosen per dataset: erasure coding (ec:2+1, the default for new collections), full replicas, or a single copy for scratch and cache data (Durability and redundancy). A separate live tier near compute holds committed versions as unencrypted native files and never counts toward durability (The live tier). Release 1.3 of its storage core shipped on 2026-10-01 (Status at a glance).

GaiaKeep's first real use is as panAtlas's durable backend, with versioned, append-based ingest: add datasets, append versions, retrieve (question P1 in GaiaKeep's open questions, answered 2026-10-02). GaiaKeep's documentation has a page on this binding, GaiaKeep: panAtlas. This page summarises it from the panAtlas side. GaiaKeep is the authority on how GaiaKeep works.

Status

GaiaKeep's core is built and tested; the panAtlas binding is measured and designed. The panAtlas index has not been stored in GaiaKeep yet. GaiaKeep's answer on its first real data (P2, 2026-10-02) is no single hero dataset: several test fixtures of different sizes and shapes, with the panAtlas index among the candidates. It is a strong candidate because it is small, its sizes are measured, and it exercises identity, versioning and the identifier rules without needing tape.

docs.title: The index is a dataset
docs.text:
Measured on 2026-09-19 on the HPC cluster:

Part Size Share Source-of-record ledgers (five parquet files: doc_ledger_{crosswalk,v4,v5}, master_doc_index, pmc_doc_pmid_map) 11.24 GB 5.7 % Derived labels, edges and nearest neighbours (labels_v53/) 186.80 GB 94.3 % Total 198.04 GB 200,497,968 documents, 988 B each

In archive terms that is 185 one-GiB parcels, 0.66 % of one 30 TB cartridge, and about 13–14 minutes to bring back from cold tape with a single mount (the timing is modelled). "Everything indexed" is affordable as long as the index is stored as an ordinary versioned dataset, not as a per-document index inside the archive's own on-media structures, which would be 254 times larger per cartridge. Document index has the schemas.

docs.title: Identifiers and write-once media
docs.text:
panAtlas identifies documents by doc_uid = blake2b(raw_text, 16 bytes), an unkeyed content hash. That is what makes the 200,497,968 documents of the pretraining-ledger crosswalk traceable across corpus versions and checkable for training contamination (Document index). It also means that anyone holding a candidate document can confirm whether it is in the corpus: in GaiaKeep's terms, the hash is a confirmation oracle.

On write-once media that confirmation would last forever. In GaiaKeep's design of record (§19.3 of its specification), a field on unerasable media is allowed only if an adversary holding a candidate plaintext, and no key, cannot reproduce it. All three panAtlas identifier classes fail that test (doc_uid, manifest_hash, and doc_ids_e8_order.txt, which is 2.54 GB of nothing but content hashes). They are therefore payload only: allowed inside encrypted objects, never in on-media structures. A keyed form, HMAC(K_idx, doc_uid), passes the rule but gives up cross-version joinability.

That rule is not absolute. Under the deduplication model built in GaiaKeep 1.3 it became per-mode policy (GaiaKeep decision log, 2026-09-19, "Becomes policy"): it is mandatory in every dedup mode except GLOBAL, where the plain content hash is the public block id. Public literature, most of today's text corpus, could therefore sit in the GLOBAL mode with plain content hashes; protected clinical data could not (Tenants, collections and deduplication, Decision log).

GaiaKeep mints its own identifiers and dataset namespace. A panAtlas URN is not a GaiaKeep dataset name; the crosswalk from URN and manifest_hash to a GaiaKeep version is a panAtlas service, not a storage-layer dependency (GaiaKeep questions X1 and X6, answered 2026-10-02).

Decide before the imaging overlap job runs

The exact-overlap contamination check has so far run only on text: 16 benchmarks, all text. When the imaging version runs, the same unkeyed hash will be computed over protected health information. GaiaKeep's side is settled: its question X1 was answered on 2026-10-02, and GaiaKeep mints its own identifiers and never relies on external keys. Whether to key doc_uid, which would break the cross-version crosswalk at every key rotation, is panAtlas's decision, and it has to be made before that job runs.

docs.title: Withdrawal
docs.text:
• Parquet ledgers: shard by redaction domain before storage, so that a withdrawal destroys one shard's key and blanks only those rows.
  • Derived arrays (.npz): a row cannot be blanked without rewriting the whole array. The response is invalidate and recompute. That is possible because the recipe is kept (jobs 219233 and 219234, p6_promote.py, lexicon v5.3). The cost of a recompute has not been measured; the exhaustive nearest-neighbour search is the expensive part.

What a redaction domain is for panAtlas data, and whether recompute is affordable, are open (GaiaKeep questions X3 to X5).

docs.title: Why the shared mesh matters here
docs.text: The mesh that carries the dataset managers also carries GaiaKeep. A site that joins Cresco can contribute compute, storage and datasets through one identity, one trust model and one tenancy boundary. The atlas then records where each dataset and each copy lives, by URN and manifest_hash (crosswalked to GaiaKeep's own version names), without moving the data.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: panAtlas is mostly metadata. It describes datasets, documents, models, training stages, benchmarks, results and concepts precisely enough that an evaluation can be placed, compared and audited without moving the underlying data. This section documents every metadata family, field by field: its schema, which script writes it, which script reads it, and what values it holds at the repository commit each page names.

docs.title: The families and how they connect
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  DOC["document<br/>doc_uid"] -. "MeSH labels and weighted edges<br/>(document index, outside the graph)" .-> CON["concept / specialty<br/>canonical_id (mesh:D…, foodon:…, wikipedia:…)"]
  DS["dataset<br/>panatlas:dataset:<slug><br/>manifest_hash"] -. "ledger rows" .-> DOC
  DS -- "classified_as, covers_topic" --> CON
  DS -- test_set_of --> BEN["benchmark /<br/>llm-benchmark"]
  BEN -- grounded_in --> CON
  MOD["model"] -- has_training_stage --> ST["training-stage"]
  ST -- stage_trained_on --> DS
  ST -- "executed_on, built_with" --> SYS["system, codebase"]
  MOD -- "scored (value, metric)" --> BEN
  MOD -- "measured_on (acc)" --> CON
  DS -. "served by" .-> MGR["dataset manager<br/>(Cresco)"]

Solid arrows are edge relations in the served graph (Graph schema lists all 36). Dotted arrows are links held outside the graph: in the document index, or on the mesh.

Family Identity Page Identifiers URNs, slugs, doc_uid, manifest_hash, MeSH slugs, model@version, job ids Identifiers Datasets panatlas:dataset:<slug> Dataset registry Dataset contents manifest_hash over (relpath, size, mtime) Manifests Acquisition, licence, entitlement Per dataset and per document Acquisition and licence Documents doc_uid = blake2b-16(text) Document index Graph nodes and edges Node id, typed edges Graph schema Benchmarks Benchmark node, ontology facets Benchmarks Results Model × benchmark × dataset, with verified date and method Evaluation records Models and training Model record, curriculum stages Models and curriculum Triples Prefixes, classes, predicates, named graphs RDF vocabulary Vocabularies MeSH, Wikidata, FHIR, LOINC and others Code systems Federation messages Reports, profiles, instance configuration, mesh.json, models.json Wire contract

docs.title: Rules every family follows
docs.text:
1. Stable identity. An identifier, once minted, is never reused for something else. Versions are explicit (@v3w, manifest_hash, pav:version), not implied by overwriting.
  2. Provenance on every fact. Records say which script or job produced them, from what input, and when. Slurm job numbers are first-class provenance.
  3. Measured versus declared. A count read from a source's own documentation is kept apart from a count measured on our copy, and the record says which one it is.
  4. Blanks are data. Unknown values are recorded as unknown, with the reason (curriculum_disclosed: false, withheld_reason, the curriculum gap register), so that they can be compared and closed.
  5. Licence per document. Licence and tier are recorded at ingest for every document, and consulted when something is shared or put into a training set. "Not training-eligible" is never a reason to leave data out of the atlas.
  6. Source of record. Every mirrored node and edge names the graph that maintains it. panAtlas curates only what it is the source of record for.
  7. Structure only across sites. The metadata that crosses the mesh is identifiers, counts, edges, model stamps and hashes, never content. See Federation.

docs.title: Acquisition and licence
docs.text:
Status

Built: the registry status field and its transitions, acquisition records, completion summaries, fold-in, the upstream licence table (web/licence/licence_registry.json), dataset-level licence fields, and the per-document licence columns on the estate document index (measured 2026-09-23 over 93,056,465 rows). Designed, not built: the per-user, per-project entitlement layer for restricted data (PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md phases P2 to P6), and any training-set assembler that reads the per-document licence column. Registry counts are at repository HEAD 57505c6 (2026-10-31).

This page covers three kinds of metadata that decide what may be done with a dataset: where it is in its lifecycle (status and acquisition records), what licence governs it (per dataset and per document), and who may see it (access class and, for restricted data, entitlements).

docs.title: The status lifecycle
docs.text:
status on a registry entry has three values at HEAD:

Status Entries Meaning acquiring 46 registered, data not yet held or not yet verified complete; manifest is null building 5 a derived dataset whose rows do not exist yet; locations empty and host null so no manifest, report or manager is produced active 149 data is held; the entry may have a manifest and a manager

There is no acquired or complete top-level status. complete is a value of acquisition.status (below). No code path moves an entry out of active: there is no retired, removed or superseded state, and retired slugs are simply absent from the registry.

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> acquiring: registered before the data is complete
  [*] --> building: derived set registered before its rows exist
  [*] --> active: registered with the data already held
  acquiring --> active: manifest folded with no missing locations
  building --> active: rows produced, locations and host set
  active --> active: re-registration keeps active

How each transition is made:

  • Registration writes the initial status. Fragments for downloads (web/datasets_renal.json, web/datasets_tcga.json) arrive as acquiring; web/register_openh.py writes acquiring with manifest: null and keeps it until the download's DONE marker exists and its manifest is folded; okn_agent.py describe writes active when the graph's agent holds a verified version (state.json current_version), else acquiring.
  • Fold-in (web/fold_manifests.py and its TCGA and renal predecessors) sets status: active only when the folded manifest's missing_locations is empty, and sets acquisition.status: complete. See Manifests.
  • Re-registration never demotes. register_fragment.py and register_tcga.py keep active and the completed acquisition fields when an entry is already active; register_openh.py keeps status once a manifest exists; register_okn.py keeps an existing manifest, linked_nodes and manifest_full_walk.

State combinations in the registry at HEAD:

status acquisition manifest Entries acquiring absent null 46 building absent null 5 active status: complete summary 67 active absent summary 54 active {} summary 6 active {} null 9 active {} absent 6 active object without status absent 5 active status: complete null 1 active free-text status absent 1

The 22 active entries without a manifest are model outputs, derived sets and evaluation suites registered as active without a file walk (listed on Dataset registry).

OKN mirrors: registry says acquiring, the project record says served

All 46 OKN entries are acquiring with source_of_record.held_version: null. The project's dated record states that the local SPARQL store has served 44 OKN graphs, each proven to round-trip exactly, since 2026-10-03. The registry entries were generated by okn_agent.py describe before those copies were held and have not been regenerated and re-merged (register_okn.py) since. Treat the OKN status and held_version fields as stale until describe is re-run.

The served catalog adds three status values that are not part of the registry lifecycle, on catalog-only corpus entries: listed (228), measured (133), on-disk (61). See Dataset registry.

docs.title: Completion records
docs.text:
A completion summary is written by the fetcher or finaliser on the cluster when a download ends, and is the input to fold-in. Three shapes are in use:

=== "Per-dataset manifests (renal)"

`web/acquisition/renal/completion_summary.json` (repository mirror):

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `finished` | finish time |
| `manifests` | `{slug: {file_count, total_bytes, manifest_hash, missing_locations, computed_at}}` |
| `log_tail` | the last fetch-log records: `{name, status, bytes, detail, t}` (80 records; `status` is `ok` 76, `start` 3, `partial` 1) |

Recorded result: 10 manifests, 48,281 files, 6.86 TB, 0 missing locations, finished 2026-09-06 06:09:30.

=== "Per-dataset list (TCGA, default for fold_manifests.py)"

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `finished` | finish time |
| `datasets[]` | `{slug, file_count, total_bytes, missing, hash}` per dataset |

Fold-in refuses a dataset whose manifest hash differs from `hash`.

=== "Whole download (OpenH-RF, openh_fetch.py finish)"

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `repo`, `revision` | upstream repository and pinned revision |
| `files`, `bytes` | files and bytes in the upstream tree |
| `lfs_files_sha256_verified`, `git_files_sha1_verified` | files verified by each hash kind |
| `n_missing_or_unverified`, `missing_or_unverified` | count and first 50 paths |
| `partial_files` | count of `.part` / `.incomplete` files |
| `extra_files` | first 50 files not in the upstream tree |
| `checked` | when the check ran |

`finish` writes a `DONE` marker (the summary plus `"verified": true`) only when nothing is missing,
unverified, partial or extra. `fold_manifests.py` accepts this shape only under the same condition.

The per-file fetch log (manifest.jsonl on the cluster) is append-only JSON lines; the renal fetcher writes {name, status, …, t} records. Its full schema is not in the repository.

docs.title: Verification at acquisition
docs.text:
Content is verified when data is acquired, against the publisher's own checksums, not by the manifest (which does not read content; see Manifests). What each recorded acquisition verified:

Acquisition Verification recorded OpenH-RF (2026-10-11 to 2026-10-15, jobs 231465 to 231468) every one of 19,662 files against the pinned Hugging Face tree: sha256 for LFS files, git blob sha1 otherwise; mismatches deleted and refetched; DONE only at 19,662 of 19,662; 34 manifests, 0 missing locations arXiv corpus acquisition.result: all nine configs, 3,745 Parquet shards, 0 errors; 16.08 TB on disk matches the card CPTAC-LUAD slides md5sum -c against each package's own sums: 508 of 508 and 1,137 of 1,137 (jobs 220431, 220430) TCGA slides GDC data endpoint, md5-verified (source_of_truth) OKN graphs a graph is done only if its line count equals the endpoint's COUNT(*), nothing is malformed and lines are distinct or the repeats are confirmed by the endpoint; PROOF.json records fingerprint, upstream, re-extraction and store round-trip checks (web/acquisition/okn/README.md) UMLS 2026AA (job 237451, 2026-10-16) every zip member CRC, the release's inner md5 files, and all 56 RRF files equal to the release's own file list in rows (392,875,930) and size; the fetch fails if any path is group- or world-readable

docs.title: The rule: licence is recorded per document and applied late
docs.text:
Owner policy of 2026-09-23 (web/licence/licence_registry.py docstring; web/estate_doc_index.py docstring):

  1. Ingest is never gated by licence. Register, manifest, federate and index first.
  2. The licence is a per-document attribute, recorded at ingest on the estate document index.
  3. The licence is applied at two moments only: when documents are shared outward, and when a training set is assembled. Both read the per-document column; neither is decided at ingest.

"Not training-eligible" is therefore never a reason to leave data out of panAtlas. Inclusion and training eligibility are separate questions:

Question Where it is recorded Decided when Is the data in panAtlas? the registry entry and its manifest at registration Did a model train on it? registry used_in_training; the document ledger (doc_uid membership in V4/V5) after training, from the training record May it go into a training set? per-document license_* columns on estate_doc_index.parquet (text); per-case governance columns such as pretrain_eligible and held_out_eval in a corpus's own case manifest (imaging) at training-set assembly May it be shared? the same licence columns, plus the dataset's access class at sharing

No assembler reads the licence column yet

At HEAD no repository script filters a training set or an export by license_status or license_scope. The column is recorded and measured; its use at assembly time is a rule for whoever builds the next mix.

docs.title: Upstream licence table
docs.text:
web/licence/licence_registry.json (built by web/licence/licence_registry.py, checked: 2026-09-23) is the evidence layer. Each upstream records where its licence statement was read:

Field Meaning name upstream name license the licence as the source states it (empty when none is stated) license_id normalised id (SPDX where one exists, custom-…, LicenseRef-…, MIXED, or empty) basis file:<root-relative path> (a card or LICENSE shipped with our copy) or web:<url> (a primary page); several separated by ; status verified · conflicting (primary sources disagree; both recorded) · not-found (no statement where one should be; never guessed) · internal (generated inside the programme) note qualifications scope dataset · document (licence varies per document) · derived (outputs of a model or a mix) · internal checked date read

At HEAD: 67 upstreams; status verified 48, not-found 10, conflicting 8, internal 1; scope dataset 57, document 6, derived 3, internal 1.

The table also routes every estate source to its upstream:

Route table Form Meaning pretrain {source: "fixed:<upstream>" \| "pmc" \| "medrxiv" \| "medlineplus"} one upstream for every document of the source, or a per-document resolver leaf {sft source: upstream} an SFT source whose every row has one upstream label {row label prefix: upstream} upstream for an SFT row's own label; longest prefix wins

Upstream count differs from the project record

The project's licence reference (2026-09-23) reports 66 upstreams (47 verified). The repository file at HEAD has 67 (48 verified). One verified upstream was added after that record; the per-document counts below are from the 2026-09-23 build and predate it.

docs.title: Dataset-level licence fields
docs.text:
Registry entries carry the licence of the dataset as a whole (field-by-field table on Dataset registry). web/licence/apply_registry_licences.py copies the verified upstream record onto the 13 text-dataset entries whose slug maps to exactly one upstream, and writes the PMC entry as license_scope: document with license_id: PMC-OA-groups. The nine document-scope entries at HEAD are PMC, the arXiv corpus, DailyMed and six JK-Decide entries. OKN entries take the licence their publisher declares (license_status: declared-by-publisher) or record not-found; upstream_licence_flag marks three OKN graphs whose declared licence does not cover content they embed (credentialed clinical relations, terminology identifiers, or third-party records).

Registry values at HEAD: license_status verified 46, not-found 25, declared-by-publisher 22, conflicting 2, three free-text values; license_scope dataset 98, document 9.

docs.title: Per-document licence on the estate index
docs.text:
estate_doc_index.parquet (on the cluster, 93,056,465 rows; schema on Document index) carries six licence columns on every row. web/licence/estate_licence_build.py fills them:

Column Meaning tier embedded (from master_doc_index.parquet) or reference (arXiv, never embedded) license the licence text(s) of the resolved upstream(s), joined by \| license_id the upstream id(s), joined by \|; for medRxiv the per-preprint code mapped to CC-BY, CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-ND, CC-BY-NC-ND, CC0, CC0 (medRxiv cc0_ng), no-reuse-licence license_scope the upstream's scope; mixed when a row resolves to more than one upstream; unknown when the status is not-found or nothing resolved license_status the upstream's status; conflicting when more than one upstream; not-found if any resolved upstream is not-found; unresolved when no upstream was found license_upstream upstream key(s), joined by \| license_resolved_by how the upstream was found (table below)

Resolution, in order, per row:

license_resolved_by Applies to Rule source-route pretrain sources with a fixed: route the source's single upstream pmc-record PMC the NLM Open Access group (commercial, non-commercial, other) on the row's stage-3 record medrxiv-api medRxiv the preprint's licence from the medRxiv API, by DOI medlineplus-url MedlinePlus by URL path: encyclopedia and drug-information pages are copyrighted, the rest public domain sft-row-label SFT rows the row's own upstream label sft-duplicate-trail SFT rows the labels or leaf upstreams of every exact-duplicate copy (the dedup dup_of trail); precedence: a specific upstream, then an instruction-following mix, then programme-internal arxiv-metadata arXiv metadata.license per paper; document + verified when present, unknown + not-found when null (empty) anything unresolved unknown / unresolved

Measured 2026-09-23 (web/licence/estate_licence_rollup.json):

Measure Rows Total 93,056,465 (embedded 89,907,669 · reference 3,148,796) license_status verified 85,128,342 · conflicting 3,117,740 · not-found 2,120,877 · internal 1,850,711 · unresolved 838,795 license_scope dataset 58,145,222 · document 27,920,759 · unknown 2,959,672 · derived 2,172,658 · internal 1,850,711 · mixed 7,443 license_resolved_by source-route 54,112,889 · pmc-record 23,585,101 · sft-duplicate-trail 6,585,363 · arxiv-metadata 3,148,796 · sft-row-label 3,140,952 · medrxiv-api 1,643,554 · (empty) 838,710 · medlineplus-url 1,100 Largest license_id values PMC-OA-commercial 16,046,523 · PhysioNet-CHDL-1.5.0 14,968,249 · custom-NLM-PubMed-terms 14,333,458 · ODC-By-1.0 7,906,368 · PMC-OA-noncommercial 6,357,130 · CC-BY-4.0 5,817,067 Largest unknown sources dailymed 1,604,636 · arxiv_complete 452,715 · several SFT mixes (332,401; 293,620; 126,808; …)

A row count is not a document count for chunked sources: PMC's 23,585,101 rows are 7,420,701 articles.

Two builders write estate_doc_index.parquet with different schemas

web/estate_doc_index.py (built 2026-09-23 09:13, per web/estate_doc_rollup.json) writes six columns, doc_id, source, role, tier, license, license_scope, with license_scope in {document, dataset, unrecorded}; it found no registry licence string for any embedded source, so all 89,907,669 embedded rows were unrecorded. web/licence/estate_licence_build.py (built 2026-09-23 21:50) overwrites the same file with the full schema and a different scope vocabulary (dataset, document, unknown, derived, internal, mixed). The second build is the current file. The policy text still describes the first vocabulary. Re-running estate_doc_index.py would silently replace the licence columns with the older, poorer ones.

docs.title: Access classes today
docs.text:
Every registry entry has an access class (values and counts on Dataset registry). Restricted classes at HEAD: restricted 16, credentialed-phi 3, credentialed 2, institutional 2, registered (Kaggle account, competition rules accepted) 1, restricted (in-house training data) 1, mixed (per member) 1.

The rule today is all-or-nothing: restricted datasets are catalogued as metadata only and never served. Their registry metadata is visible; their data is not available through panAtlas at all. The public API (web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/includes/public-api.php) is anonymous and rate-limited per client per minute; its dataset routes return a fixed whitelist of metadata fields for every catalog entry, restricted ones included, with cluster paths and job numbers scrubbed from strings. The Astral assistant attaches a "metadata only" note to every non-public record. The explorer's full graph and catalog views are gated by an identity allowlist (PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md §1, 2026-10-11). No per-user or per-project control exists.

docs.title: The entitlement model (designed)
docs.text:
PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md designs a restricted-data layer, with the UMLS Metathesaurus as its first dataset and the same layer intended for every later restricted dataset. Only the licence-fact and acquisition phases are done.

Phase Work State P0 licence facts done 2026-10-11 P1 acquire the release in a Slurm job, verify it, restrict the directory passed 2026-10-16 (job 237451): release 2026AA P2 load verbatim into a separate restricted SPARQL store, one named graph per source restriction level next; not built P3 entitlement registry, enforcement in the SPARQL client, audit log designed P4 internal relations with provenance; promotion of SRL-0-only edges to the public graph designed P5 explanations for entitled users, with the licence notice designed P6 compliance: acknowledgement with year and version, annual report, notice before distribution designed

The design's metadata, without any restricted content:

Entitlement registry (restricted/entitlements.json, private, on the cluster only, never in the public repository or on the web host):

users:     <identity> -> {name, institution, uts_account: yes/no + date checked, grants: [...]}
projects:  <id>       -> {title, purpose, members: [<identity>], datasets: [urn], allowed_srl: [0,1,2,3], expires}
datasets:  urn        -> {licence, terms_section_refs, notice_text, max_srl_by_institution, us_only: [SAB...]}

Access predicate. A user may read a restricted graph only if all hold: the user is a member of a project; the project lists the dataset; the user's own grant allows that source restriction level; for the most restrictive category, the user belongs to the licensee's institution; for the US-only category, the use is in the US. The default is deny, and every grant carries dates so it can be audited.

Per-fact provenance. Every loaded triple is tagged with its source vocabulary and the source restriction level (SRL) read from the release's own source table, not from a hand-made list, and keeps the release's concept, atom and relation identifiers so the source of every fact can be traced. Relations panAtlas derives go in a separate derived graph and record the identifiers, sources and highest SRL they depend on; only edges derived from SRL-0 sources alone may be promoted to the public graph.

Licensing obligations recorded as metadata: acknowledgement of the source with year and version on every derived record and answer; a notice and source list shown before a user first sees restricted content; an annual usage report; notice to the licensor before any application using the data reaches anyone outside the licensee.

Directory mode differs from the plan

The plan specifies a group of licensed users with mode 0750. The acquisition (P1) made restricted/ mode 0700, readable by the licensee's account only, because the licence is held by one individual and only that individual holds a licensor account. Wider access waits on each additional user holding their own licence.

What never appears in panAtlas outputs

No restricted release content (terms, definitions, synonym strings, relation rows) is published, committed, logged or placed in the public graph or catalog. PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md §7 calls for a regression test asserting that no restricted graph IRI, restricted string or definition text appears in the public graph.json or catalog; that test is designed, not built. There is no registry entry for the restricted release at HEAD.

The codes panAtlas already shows on concepts (concept identifiers and cross-codes obtained through the licensor's lookup service) are covered on Code systems.

Related pages: Dataset registry, Manifests, Document index, Identifiers, Code systems.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: A benchmark in panAtlas is described once, by a registry entry, an ontology classification, a taxonomy placement, a suite-fit verdict and a mapping from its items to concepts. Results attach to it separately (see Evaluation records). This page documents every field of that description. Counts were computed with python3 from the files at repo HEAD 57505c6 on 2026-11-10.

On the graph node the same object also carries holdout_status and holdout_note. The status values on the 106 llm-benchmark nodes are unchecked 85, not_held_out 10, provably_held_out 5, partial 4, proven_trained_on 2.

Decontamination fields differ from the catalog document

docs.title: Audit block (audit)
docs.text:
102 entries carry an audit block with 15 keys. build_eval_map.py writes it by joining benchmark_ontology_facets.json (by name), benchmark_audit.json (by panAtlas id) and the suite-fit buckets of benchmark_suite_fit.json (by name):

Field Values kind Free text: official-published (<citation>) or homegrown what_it_does, how_it_works, the_document Free text executable not-implemented 42, runnable-standard-harness 19, runnable-custom-driver 16, cached-not-run 16, homegrown-scorer 8, gated-unavailable 1 run_on_kos never-run (58) or v4-and-v5 (23), plus annotated variants of each item_concept_linked no 81, yes-mesh; NO per-item correctness 16, yes-mesh; per-item correctness=TRUE 5 n_items Integer item count data_on_disk true 52, false 50 concept_fit partial 35, weak 29, strong 23, none 15 concept_fit_how Free text justification suite exclude 61, suite-core 17, suite-secondary 15, candidate 9 domain Evaluation domain onto The ontology facets for this benchmark, joined by name from benchmark_ontology_facets.json: 18 controlled facets plus subdomain on every entry, n_options on 39; typical_shots, decontam_checkable and panatlas_class are not copied map {x, y}: position on the evaluation map, a UMAP projection of the benchmark's facet vector

The audit block is smaller than documented

docs/evaluation-dimensions-and-metadata.md (section D) lists 23 audit fields, including purpose, used_for, how_to_run, engine, kos_result, reporting, quality_notes, rationale and caveats. None of these is in the served registry at HEAD. purpose, used_for, how_to_run, engine, kos_result and caveats exist in web/benchmark_audit.json (106 records), but build_eval_map.py does not copy them; quality_notes and rationale exist only in the benchmark_suite_fit.json dossiers.

docs.title: The benchmark ontology (facets)
docs.text:
docs/benchmark-ontology.md defines 26 dimensions in seven groups (A to G) and states that no model is run to produce it: it is characterization only. web/benchmark_ontology_facets.json holds one row per benchmark for 106 benchmarks. Each row has 27 keys: benchmark (the name), 22 controlled facets, and four free-text fields (subdomain, the_document, primary_metric, notes).

Three of the documented dimensions are not in the facets file:

The per-benchmark table in the ontology document mislabels a column

In docs/benchmark-ontology.md, the per-benchmark table's column headed "scoring" contains scoring_determinism values (deterministic-programmatic, reference-metric, …), not scoring_method values.

docs.title: Suite fit: benchmark_suite_fit.json
docs.text:
The suite-fit audit decides which benchmarks belong to the concept-relational suite. Its rule, stated in suite.principles, has a decisive first test: a benchmark belongs only if each individual item is a document that maps to a dominant concept grounded in MeSH (clinical and biomedical) or Wikipedia (general). This is judged before and independently of score quality. Reporting prevalence is the second criterion.

Key Content dossiers (106) Per benchmark: benchmark, capability, what_it_does, how_it_works, the_document, concept_fit, concept_fit_how, reporting_prevalence, quality_notes, recommendation, rationale suite.suite_core (17) benchmark, arm, concept_fit, reporting_prevalence, the_document, concept, why_core, open_work suite.suite_secondary (15) Same, with why_secondary suite.diagnostic_or_excluded (73) benchmark, concept_fit, category, reason suite.add_to_fill_gaps (24) name, concept_fit, reporting_prevalence, availability, gap_filled, priority suite.coverage_map, suite.medical_coverage, suite.principles Free-text analysis missing.candidates (29) Benchmarks not in the registry: name, what, how, the_document, concept_fit, reporting_prevalence, fills_gap, availability

The core suite is MedQA (USMLE 4-opt), MedMCQA, MedXpertQA (Text), Medical-MMLU (9-subject), MMLU, MMLU-Pro, ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, OpenBookQA, PubMedQA, MIRAGE, SciFact, AfriMed-QA, TruthfulQA, SimpleQA, GSM8K and MATH. The secondary suite is Medbullets, MedExpQA, CareQA, MedNLI, MEDEC, Med-HALT, CommonsenseQA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ, MedRAG, ASDiv (CoT), MathQA and GPQA.

Three suite-decision tallies disagree

The core (17) and secondary (15) lists agree everywhere. The rest does not: dossiers[].recommendation gives candidate 43, exclude 31; suite.diagnostic_or_excluded lists 73 benchmarks; the registry's audit.suite gives exclude 61, candidate 9 (over 102 audited entries). Treat audit.suite as the value the site reads.

docs.title: Question → concept mapping
docs.text: The mapping gives each benchmark item a concept, so a model's per-item correctness rolls up to per-concept accuracy. It exists in two generations. Item text and answers are not in the repository; only distributions and item-to-concept rows are.

docs.title: First mapping (qconcept)
docs.text:
Designed in web/BENCHMARK-QUESTION-MAPPING.md and implemented in build_question_concept_map.py. Each question is embedded with BioClinical-ModernBERT-large (1024-d, masked mean pool, max_length 1024, L2-normalised), assigned to the nearest of 4,096 corpus cell centroids, and given that cell's dominant concept, the same path the corpus documents use.

Row field (qconcept_<bench>.jsonl) Meaning question_id Source id, else <bench>__<index> (six-digit, zero-padded) doc_uid blake2b hex digest of the question text benchmark bench-<slug> concept Concept node id, or unmapped cell Corpus cell key cosine Cosine to the cell centroid

The repository holds the 21 distribution files ({benchmark, n, distribution}) and qconcept_stats.json (per benchmark: n, n_concepts, top_concept, top_share, entropy_bits, mean_cosine, poor_fit_frac). The row files are on the cluster. The 21 benchmarks are AfriMed-QA, AGIEval LSAT-AR, ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, ASDiv, BoolQ, CommonsenseQA, COPA, GPQA, GSM8K, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, Medical-MMLU, MedMCQA, MedQA, MedXpertQA, MMLU-Pro, MMLU, OpenBookQA, PubMedQA and WinoGrande. This mapping feeds concept_accuracy.json and the measured_on edges (Evaluation records).

The doc_uid in question rows is not the ledger doc_uid

build_question_concept_map.py computes hashlib.blake2b(text).hexdigest() with the default 64-byte digest. The training-ledger identity used for decontamination is blake2b(raw_text, digest_size=16). The two cannot be joined.

docs.title: Judge-gated mapping (qconcept2)
docs.text:
build_concept_remap.py wires a corrected mapping from web/pipeline/qconcept2/. Its rows carry question_id, benchmark, concept and cosine. Over the 20 files there are 48,931 rows, of which 2,925 are unmapped. The method string the script stamps is "judge-gated: BGE-large retrieval + gemma-4-31B concept judge". The script:

  1. creates the Wikipedia-grounded general concepts from general_concept_space.json (homes for math, science and reading items);
  2. rebuilds each benchmark's distribution, stored on the node as topics = {n, unmapped, distribution};
  3. wires the 15 largest concepts per benchmark as covers_topic edges with n = number of items (300 edges at HEAD).

hygiene_enrich.py then derives a grounded_in edge (attribute via: mesh:<UI>) from a benchmark to every MeSH-grounded concept it reaches through covers_topic, tests or covers (239 edges).

Design, graph and served registry disagree on the mapping

BENCHMARK-QUESTION-MAPPING.md requires one embedding space (BioClinical-ModernBERT) and lists MedMCQA (270 questions) as the only benchmark mapped. The served graph's topic edges come from the judge-gated BGE mapping over 20 benchmarks (MedMCQA is not among them). The served benchmarks_llm.json still carries topics on 6 entries and topics_status "pending general concept space" on 15, while the graph nodes carry judge-gated topics on 20. The per-concept accuracies on concept nodes still use the first mapping's concept ids.

docs.title: llm-benchmark (106)
docs.text:
Built from the registry. Fields on every node: id, label, kind, layer (concept), arm, metric, gated, measures, composition, kos_usage, benchmark (always true), modality (always text), testing_type, domain, concept_class (always evaluation), decontam. On some: artifact_types, artifact_type_labels, artifact_type_via (96); tier (29); topics, topics_status (20); grounding, wp_topic, wp_url (7: intrinsic methods given a Wikipedia grounding by hygiene_enrich.py).

artifact_type_via records how the artifact types were assigned: override (34, from benchmark_overrides in artifact_types.json) or facet:<task_format> (from benchmark_task_format_map). Ten nodes have none; representation diagnostics are deliberately untyped.

Edges out of an llm-benchmark: is_type, in_domain, tests, covers_topic, grounded_in, has_artifact_type. Edges into it: scored and evaluated_on from models.

docs.title: Controlled vocabularies
docs.text: panAtlas grounds its nodes in external vocabularies and in a small number of internal ones. This page documents each vocabulary, the fields that carry it on graph nodes, the files that define it, and how a grounding is verified. Counts were computed with python3 from the files at repo HEAD 57505c6 on 2026-11-10. How grounded identity becomes RDF is on RDF vocabulary; identifier syntax is on Identifiers.

docs.title: Roles of the vocabularies
docs.text:
Vocabulary Role in panAtlas Canonical? MeSH (NLM) Identity and hierarchy of medical concepts; the deduplication key Yes, for medical concepts Wikipedia Identity of general, non-medical concepts; readable overlay on MeSH concepts Yes, for general concepts only Wikidata Machine-readable identity behind Wikipedia concepts Registered; not yet carried on nodes SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD-10-CM, ICD-11 Cross-codes on MeSH concepts; terminology bindings of FHIR resources No UMLS Metathesaurus Licensed crosswalk used to obtain cross-codes; internal and entitlement-gated No Gene Ontology Anchors the genomics modality No HL7 FHIR R4 Data model of the clinical instance layer Yes, for instance records NACC Neuropathology Metadata Data model of neuropathology records Yes, for that domain FoodOn, ChEBI, FoodData Central, FNDDS Food and chemical entities Yes, for food nodes Internal vocabularies Artifact types, registers, testing types, capabilities, domains Internal (panatlas: prefix where a canonical id is given)

Each domain is grounded in its own field's vocabularies. Medicine has the most today, because it is where the atlas's holdings run deepest; foods are grounded in FoodOn and FoodData Central, and general knowledge in Wikipedia. A new domain registers its own vocabularies the same way. GRAPH_STANDARDS.md, written for the medical holdings, names MeSH, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, UMLS and ICD as the terminology backbone, with MeSH canonical. web/domains.json lists the full ontology_backbone: onto-mesh, onto-fhir, onto-snomed, onto-loinc, onto-rxnorm, onto-icd11, onto-icd10cm, onto-umls, onto-go, onto-foodon, onto-chebi, onto-fdc, onto-wikidata, onto-nacc, onto-wikipedia.

docs.title: web/codesystems.json
docs.text:
The registry of terminology code systems. Its _note: fhir_system is the URI a FHIR CodeableConcept.coding.system uses; rdf_iri_stem concatenated with a code gives the concept's RDF IRI (per the FHIR RDF specification and HL7 THO). These replaced earlier "decorative" authority nodes with sourced identifiers.

Field Meaning id onto-<system>; also the graph node id of the system label Name authority Publisher fhir_system FHIR coding system URI, or null rdf_iri_stem IRI stem for codes, or null when none is registered rdf_iri_basis Why that stem (dated inventory), where it was contested code_example An example code canonical Whether the system is a canonical identity source anchor The concept node the system anchors, or null note Role statement id Authority fhir_system rdf_iri_stem Canonical onto-mesh US National Library of Medicine https://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/ yes onto-snomed SNOMED International / NLM (US Edition) http://snomed.info/sct http://snomed.info/id/ no onto-loinc Regenstrief Institute http://loinc.org http://loinc.org/rdf/ no onto-rxnorm US National Library of Medicine http://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/rxnorm http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/RXNORM/ no onto-umls US National Library of Medicine http://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls an identifier-only prefix expansion (see below) no onto-icd10cm US CDC / NCHS http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm none no onto-icd11 World Health Organization http://id.who.int/icd/release/11/mms http://id.who.int/icd/entity/ no onto-go Gene Ontology Consortium http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/go.owl http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_ no onto-wikipedia Wikimedia none https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ yes onto-wikidata Wikimedia none http://www.wikidata.org/entity/ no

The MeSH stem is http because NLM mints http IRIs and https only redirects; the OKN graphs that hold MeSH also use http (inventory 2026-09-26). The UMLS stem is the Biolink prefix expansion used by the OKN identifier-mapping graph; codesystems.json records that it is an identifier only and no longer resolves, and that NLM publishes no UMLS RDF.

docs.text:
build_layered.py turns the registered systems into 15 authority nodes (layer: ontology): the ten above plus onto-fhir (from fhir.json), onto-nacc (from web/nacc/), and onto-foodon, onto-chebi, onto-fdc (from nutrition.json). Fields: id, label, kind, layer, modality, canonical, authority_org, source, built_by, note; most also carry fhir_system (14), iri_stem (13) and code_example (10); onto-nacc adds version, n_variables, n_codelists.

Edge Count Meaning authority grounds → concept (specialty, root, concept) 13 The system anchors that concept authority defines → root 1 MeSH defines Medicine authority has_resource → fhir 18 FHIR and NACC own their resource and record types fhir binds → authority 15 A FHIR resource's coded elements bind that code system dataset/kg/food structured_as → authority 1,592 The node's records follow that vocabulary (1,582 foods) authority part_of → domain 15 All systems sit under "Data & Standards"

Stale IRI stems on two authority nodes

In the served graph onto-mesh carries iri_stem: https://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/ and onto-umls carries the former UTS REST URL, while codesystems.json has the corrected stems (changed 2026-09-26). build_rdf.py takes iri_stem, rdf_iri_basis and fhir_system from codesystems.json, so the RDF is correct; consumers of graph.json should read the stems from codesystems.json.

docs.title: Hierarchy from tree numbers
docs.text: A descriptor's parent is the descriptor whose tree number is the immediate prefix, for example Cardiology H02.403.429.163 under Internal Medicine H02.403.429 under Medicine H02.403. Specialties are in the H02 (Health Occupations) tree, diseases in C, techniques in E. In the graph these are part_of edges with src: mesh_tree (3,360). FoodAtlas diseases are attached to a specialty by tree number (2,478 disease part_of specialty edges).

docs.title: How a MeSH grounding is verified
docs.text:
• Curated concepts: resolved through the UMLS UTS API, then adversarially verified, one agent per concept, each confirming the descriptor UI with a live UTS call (GRAPH_STANDARDS.md).
  • Artifact types (2026-08-08): checked against the live NLM MeSH descriptor lookup with match=exact, audit trail web/pipeline/groundings_verified.json; then a concept-identity judge pass (2026-08-09) decided whether the descriptor is the same thing as the record type (see Models and curriculum).
  • Later domain additions record the lookup in built_by, with its date.
  • In the SPARQL store, 3,373 of 3,377 panAtlas MeSH IRIs exist in NLM's MeSH RDF (2026-09-26).

docs.title: Wikipedia and Wikidata
docs.text:
Field Nodes Meaning wiki_title 161 Wikipedia article title wp_url 211 Article URL, with ?oldid= when a revision is pinned wiki_oldid 51 Pinned revision id canonical_id wikipedia:<…> 24 Wikipedia as identity (non-MeSH nodes) grounding: wikipedia 154

Wikipedia is a fallback identity only for genuinely non-medical nodes, and an overlay otherwise. The general concept space, web/general_concept_space.json (proposed 153; final.concepts 120 with name, wikipedia_title, definition, domain, granularity top/mid/leaf, serves, example_item; plus coverage_summary, gaps), gives benchmark items in mathematics, science, reading and similar areas a Wikipedia-grounded concept. build_concept_remap.py writes them as concept nodes with grounding: wikipedia, wiki_title, wp_url, general_domain and granularity (117 nodes at HEAD; 3 already existed).

The markdown fact pages record a pinned revision in frontmatter as wikipedia: {title, oldid, retrieved}, and every claim seeded from Wikipedia carries the revision in its provenance tag. Wikipedia text is evidence, never verification (Knowledge layers).

Wikidata is registered (onto-wikidata, stem http://www.wikidata.org/entity/), but no node in the served graph carries a Wikidata QID. The bridge exists in the SPARQL store: 3,310 panAtlas concepts reach 3,313 Wikidata entities through the OKN identifier-mappings graph (vault, 2026-09-26). See RDF vocabulary.

docs.text:

In the graph each becomes a fhir node (layer: ontology, fhir_group), with binds edges to the code systems. dataset_instantiates rules (match_modality or match_ids → resources) give 36 dataset instantiates → fhir edges: imaging datasets instantiate ImagingStudy and DiagnosticReport, genomics datasets MolecularSequence, clinical-note datasets DocumentReference and Composition, drug-label datasets Medication.

Instance layer: model only

The graph holds the FHIR and NACC resource types and which datasets would instantiate them. It holds no FHIR instance records. Layer 2 of GRAPH_STANDARDS.md (FHIR RDF instances whose codings join the backbone) is designed, not built.

docs.title: Corpus cells to concepts
docs.text: web/cell2concept.json (1,740 records) maps clusters of the training corpus to concepts. Fields: cell_id, topic_cluster, subtopic_cluster, count (documents), slug (concept id, 50 distinct), cos (cosine to the concept anchor), cell_domain (for example basic_science 533, general 498, radiology 113), topic_summary. This is the path by which corpus documents, and in the first question mapping benchmark items, reach a concept. web/concept_similarity.json gives the top related concepts by anchor cosine, written as related edges at 0.72 or above.

docs.title: UMLS
docs.text:
The UMLS Metathesaurus is a licensed vocabulary. In panAtlas it is internal and entitlement-gated:

  • It is used as a lookup service through the UTS API under licence, to resolve MeSH groundings and obtain cross-codes. The cross-code fields listed above come from that lookup.
  • The release files were acquired for the planned restricted store (phase P1 passed 2026-10-16, owner-only access). They are not loaded, and nothing from them is in the served graph.
  • PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md designs per-user, per-project access with restriction levels read from the release itself; it is not built.
  • This documentation contains no UMLS content.

docs.title: Dataset registry
docs.text:
Status

Built and in use. The registry is web/datasets.json (schema panatlas.datasets/1). Every count on this page was computed with python3 over the repository at HEAD 57505c6 (2026-10-31) by walking all web/datasets*.json files and enumerating every key path. Nothing here is projected. Field meanings come from the scripts that write and read each field; where no script defines a value set, the page says so.

The registry is the authoritative list of datasets in the panAtlas federation. One entry describes one dataset, identified by its URN (Identifiers) and audited by its manifest (Manifests). Each entry is also the configuration source for that dataset's manager plugin (Dataset managers).

docs.title: Files and how they merge
docs.text:
There are three kinds of registry file. They share one entry schema.

File Role Entries at HEAD web/datasets.json The registry. Every registered dataset, each once. All tooling reads this file. 200 web/datasets_*.json Fragments. A batch of entries produced by one acquisition or programme, kept beside the registry as the record of what that batch registered. 65 (subset of the 200) web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/datasets.json The served catalog. The registry plus catalog-only entries and catalog-only fields, read by the site's Datasets view, the public API and the Astral assistant. 622

A cluster-side copy of the registry also exists in <cluster project storage>/panatlas/datasets.json. It holds only the entries hosted on the HPC cluster that have managers (22 at first registration, 66 on 2026-09-17 per the project record). The hourly manifest refresh rewrites that copy, not the repository file; see Manifests.

docs.title: Fragments
docs.text:
Every fragment URN is also in web/datasets.json; the union of all nine files is exactly the 200 registry URNs. Fragments are merged by upsert keyed on urn:

  • web/register_fragment.py <fragment.json> (general) and its predecessor web/register_tcga.py. New URNs are appended. For existing URNs the fragment entry replaces the registry entry, except that manifest and linked_nodes are kept from the registry when set, and, if the registry entry is already active, its status stays active and its acquisition.status, acquisition.finished and acquisition.summary are kept. The script then copies the fragment to web/<basename> (it never overwrites another fragment's copy) and asserts no duplicate URN.
  • The fold scripts (web/fold_manifests.py, web/fold_tcga_manifests.py, web/fold_renal_manifests.py) write manifest and status updates into web/datasets.json and into fragments that carry the dataset.
Fragment Entries Status at HEAD With manifest Purpose (from the fragment's meta) web/datasets_bench.json 4 4 active 3 benchmark datasets for the WSI embedding-stack study web/datasets_fm_suite.json 6 6 active 0 predictor (tabular / time-series) evaluation suite, registered 2026-10-28 web/datasets_jkdecide.json 13 8 active, 5 building 0 JK-Decide decision-model programme web/datasets_kos_v6.json 2 2 active 0 V6 model lineage: training input and evaluated outputs web/datasets_renal.json 10 10 active 10 renal-biomarker acquisition, 2026-09-04 web/datasets_stack_embeddings.json 11 11 active 0 tile embeddings derived for the WSI embedding-stack study web/datasets_tcga.json 17 17 active 17 TCGA slide-truth acquisition, 2026-09-17 web/datasets_tcga_slides.json 2 2 active 2 TCGA diagnostic and tissue whole-slide images

Fragments drift from the registry

At HEAD, 48 of 65 fragment entries are identical to their registry entries. The other 17 differ only in fields filled after registration: all 17 lack the acquisition key that the registry carries as {} (6 predictor-suite, 5 JK-Decide and 6 embedding-stack entries), and the 6 embedding-stack entries also have no manifest while the registry has one. Fragments are a historical record of a batch. Read web/datasets.json for current state.

The fragment top-level block is meta with keys schema, description, host_default, root_default, measured, manifest_tool, models_registry, benchmark_field, subset, program, fragment, created, updated, acquisition_driver, acquisition_log, vault (each fragment carries a subset). One fragment, web/datasets_kos_v6.json, uses top-level schema and note instead of meta.

docs.title: Field reference
docs.text: How to read the tables. Present is the number of the 200 registry entries that carry the key (an entry whose value is null counts as present). Required means present in all 200; no JSON Schema enforces it, but every tool assumes it. Writes names repository scripts that set the field; "fragment" means the value arrives in a fragment produced outside this repository (on the cluster, or hand-written) and is merged by register_fragment.py. Reads names consumers. Every field is also copied into the served catalog by web/sync_catalog.py and into the RDF export where noted. public-api.php is web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/includes/public-api.php; its /datasets/{slug} route serves only a fixed whitelist of fields (marked API).

docs.title: Catalog-only entries and fields
docs.text:
web/sync_catalog.py upserts every registry entry into the served catalog by URN. For URNs already in the catalog it replaces the entry with the registry entry but preserves the catalog-only fields listed below. For new URNs it appends the entry with those fields defaulted (desc from modality_detail, stage: dataset, used_in_training: false, dtype: benchmark if benchmark is truthy else source, part_of_corpus from part_of, vault_page from vault). At HEAD the 200 registry entries are identical in the catalog apart from these fields.

Catalog field Present (of 622) Meaning Values desc 616 short description free text stage 622 lifecycle in the training programme dataset 394 · sft 107 · corpus-available 64 · pretrain 57 dtype 622 catalog type source 496 · external 73 · benchmark 49 · model-corpus 4 corpus_status 622 where the source sits in the corpus pipeline items: staging 79 · v5-pretrain 51 · sources 17 · v4-pretrain 14 · incoming 10 tier 620 authority tier from the training manifests 1 21 · 2 32 · 3 3 · null or absent 566 model 622 the in-house model that trained on it null 513 · two model names (109) part_of_corpus 622 parent corpus node vault_page, vault_status 620 knowledge-vault page and its status stable 172 · superseded 110 · draft 11 · null or absent 329 used_in_training 622 preserved from the catalog even when the registry carries the field boolean artifact_types, artifact_type_ids 143 artifact types (names and atype-* ids) topic_concepts 38 concept nodes for the source's topics domain_mix 8 [domain, percent] pairs _corpus_synced, _train_synced 61 / 35 provenance flags set by build_all_datasets.py and build_train_sources.py true

The 422 catalog-only entries are corpus sources and SFT mixes discovered by disk inventory and training manifests (web/build_all_datasets.py, web/build_train_sources.py). Their status values are outside the registry vocabulary: listed 228, measured 133, on-disk 61. measured and on-disk are written by build_all_datasets.py (a measured document count exists, or not); no repository script writes listed. The public stats route counts datasets by status over the catalog, so its totals mix both vocabularies.

used_in_training in two places

used_in_training is a registry field (59 entries) and also in sync_catalog.py's list of catalog-only fields, so the catalog's existing value wins over a later registry change. At HEAD the two agree on all 59 entries.
