docs.title: Document index
docs.text:
Status

Built and measured, on the cluster. The document ledger and its doc_uid crosswalk (2026-08-01), the master document index (2026-07-27, labels remapped 2026-09-07, Wikipedia columns added 2026-09-10), the v5.3 registry labels (2026-09-07), the arXiv reference index and the estate document index (2026-09-23) exist as Parquet, NumPy and JSON files in <cluster project storage>/panatlas/. They are not in the repository. The repository holds the scripts that build them and their small JSON rollups (web/doc_ledger_summary.json, web/master_rollup.json, web/estate_doc_rollup.json, web/licence/estate_licence_rollup.json, web/decontam_exact.json). Numbers below are dated; none are projected.

The document index answers, for any text document panAtlas knows about: which source and role it belongs to, whether a model trained on it, what concept it is about, what Wikipedia article it links to, and under what licence. It is built from several tables that share two keys, doc_id (where a row is) and doc_uid (what text it is); see Identifiers.

Artifact Rows Size Key Built by doc_ledger_v4.parquet 131,739,051 2.88 GB doc_uid document-ledger build, jobs 207724 / 208237 doc_ledger_v5.parquet 178,562,639 4.02 GB doc_uid same doc_ledger_crosswalk.parquet 200,497,968 3.03 GB doc_uid job 208241 master_doc_index.parquet 89,907,669 706,689,139 B before the Wikipedia columns were added doc_id web/dgx/build_master_index.py arxiv_doc_index.parquet 3,148,796 282,794,241 B doc_id web/acquisition/arxiv/arxiv_doc_index.py estate_doc_index.parquet 93,056,465 not re-measured after the licence build doc_id web/licence/estate_licence_build.py pmc_doc_pmid_map.parquet 14,383,878 doc_uid PMC identity recovery, job 212698 labels_v53/ per document, e8 order 186,798,930,278 B e8 row v5.3 promotion, job 219233

Measured 2026-09-19: the whole index estate is 198,036,273,201 B over 200,497,968 documents, about 988 B per document. Of that, 11.24 GB (5.7 %) is the five source-of-record Parquet tables (the three ledger files, master_doc_index, pmc_doc_pmid_map) and 186.80 GB (94.3 %) is the derived labels_v53/ directory.

docs.title: Document ledger and doc_uid crosswalk
docs.text:
The ledger records every document that entered the V4 and V5 pretraining runs, one row per document as it was trained, with its content-addressed id.

Ledger columns (doc_ledger_v4.parquet, doc_ledger_v5.parquet):

Column Meaning doc_uid blake2b(raw_text, digest_size=16) as 32 hex characters version v4 or v5 source training source name file the corpus file the row came from row_idx row index within that file n_chars text length in characters

Crosswalk columns (doc_ledger_crosswalk.parquet): doc_uid, in_v4, in_v5 (booleans). One row per distinct doc_uid in either ledger. It is membership only: it does not carry concepts or positions.

Build: 11,848 input files (V4 610 over 14 sources, V5 11,238 over 56 units), a 500-task CPU array with zero failures. The build gates failed closed on the audited census counts and both passed. It was acceptance-tested by round-tripping a real document: text → doc_uid → exactly one ledger row with the correct file and row_idx → crosswalk in_v4 = true, in_v5 = true.

web/doc_ledger_summary.json holds the summary:

Key V4 V5 Meaning rows_entered 131,739,051 178,562,639 rows that entered training census_entered 131,739,051 178,562,639 the audited census count gate_entered PASS PASS rows equal the census census_trained 131,577,161 178,344,619 rows after the over-length drop dropped_overlength 161,890 218,020 whole documents dropped for length (0.12 % of each) distinct_doc_uid 79,548,810 177,728,829 distinct texts duplicate_rows 52,190,241 833,810 rows beyond the first copy duplicate_pct 39.6164 0.467 duplicate rows as a percentage of rows max_copies_of_one_doc 4,280 1,520 the most-repeated single text crosswalk key Value distinct_v4 79,548,810 distinct_v5 177,728,829 in_both 56,779,671 v4_only 22,769,139 v5_only 120,949,158 union 200,497,968

Owner ruling (2026-08-01): every document in the ledger counts as trained on. The over-length drop is not distinguished per document. Exposure is counted on distinct doc_uid, never on rows.

What the crosswalk revealed

The V4 run was never deduplicated: 39.6 % of its rows are exact duplicates, concentrated in the general web source (54.7 % duplicate) and PMC (22.3 %). V5 is nearly duplicate-free (0.47 %). Only 56.8 M documents are common to both runs; V5 dropped 22.8 M documents V4 trained on and added 120.9 M. These are measurements of the ledger, not estimates.

docs.title: Master document index
docs.text:
master_doc_index.parquet lists every document that was embedded and clustered: the pretraining chunk store and the SFT assignment table. web/dgx/build_master_index.py builds it by joining each document's (topic_cluster, subtopic_cluster) cell to a concept label through cell2concept.json and cell2concept_llm.json.

Column Type Meaning Added doc_id string <source>__<NNNNNNNNN>__c<KKKK> for pretrain chunks; SFT ids end in the source line number build source string source name (136 sources) build topic_cluster integer top-level cluster build subtopic_cluster integer cluster within the topic; with topic_cluster, identifies the cell build role string pretrain or sft build concept string the cell's concept label; remapped to the v5.3 primaries on 2026-09-07 build, remapped wiki_primary_page_id int64 the Wikipedia article this document's primary link points to 2026-09-10 wiki_primary_cos float32 cosine of that link 2026-09-10 wiki_band uint8 link strength: 0 weak · 1 medium · 2 strong · 3 curated bridge · 5 lexical agreement 2026-09-10 wiki_channel uint8 which linking channel produced the link 2026-09-10

The four wiki_* columns were added by the Wikipedia-layer promotion; the schema of record is the cluster file, not the build script (which writes the first six).

Measured: 89,907,669 rows (pretrain 77,327,492 · SFT 12,580,177), 89,907,665 with a concept (4 null); but only 81,372,220 distinct doc_ids (8,535,449 duplicate rows), because the pretrain and SFT frames overlap (measured 2026-09-23). The "89.9 M documents" headline is a row count; for pretrain sources a row is a chunk, not an article. wiki_band distribution over all rows (2026-09-10): strong 0.44 %, medium 4.1 %, lexical agreement 5.04 %, bridge 79.8 %, weak 10.66 %.

web/master_rollup.json (repository copy) holds total_docs, mapped, by_role, n_sources, per_concept (rows per concept) and per_source ({role, docs, concepts: [[concept, percent], …]}, top 8).

Read-only by contract

The Wikipedia chain asserts the master index's row count, so the estate builders read master_doc_index.parquet and never change it (web/estate_doc_index.py docstring). Re-running build_master_index.py would drop the wiki_* columns and revert the v5.3 remap.

docs.title: arXiv reference index
docs.text:
arxiv_doc_index.parquet holds the first reference-tier source: indexed, never embedded, never in a training mix. One row per paper, sorted by paper_id. No text is stored.

Column Meaning doc_id arxiv_complete__<paper_id> source arxiv_complete role reference paper_id arXiv id license per-paper licence from the metadata config (null when arXiv holds none) license_text the same value from the assembled-text config (cross-check; the two agree on all 2,431,445 papers that have both) has_text an assembled text exists n_chars UTF-8 length of the assembled text n_abstract_chars abstract length title, primary_category, categories, doi metadata n_versions, first_version_date, latest_version_date version history text_sha256 sha256 of the assembled text (content hash for decontamination) text_encoding, resolution, n_tex_files, n_files_used, n_unused_files how the text was assembled

Measured 2026-09-23 (web/acquisition/arxiv/arxiv_doc_rollup.json): 3,148,796 rows, 2,856,227 with text, 246,780,951,228 characters in total, 452,715 papers with no licence.

docs.title: Estate document index
docs.text:
estate_doc_index.parquet is the only place the two tiers are unioned: one row per estate document, each with its licence, Wikipedia link and MeSH concept. It is the table the licence policy is applied from.

Column Type Meaning (embedded tier / reference tier) doc_id string from master_doc_index / from arxiv_doc_index source dictionary string source name role dictionary string pretrain, sft / reference tier dictionary string embedded / reference license dictionary string resolved licence text license_id dictionary string resolved licence id license_scope dictionary string dataset, document, derived, internal, mixed, unknown license_status dictionary string verified, conflicting, not-found, internal, unresolved license_upstream dictionary string upstream key(s) in web/licence/licence_registry.json license_resolved_by dictionary string resolution route wiki_primary_page_id int64 Wikipedia primary link wiki_primary_cos float32 its cosine wiki_band uint8 band, as in the master index wiki_channel uint8 channel wiki_basis dictionary string w5-primary-own_hub1 / w5-primary-own_hub1 (arxiv_embed_align) mesh_concept dictionary string the cell concept / the cell concept only for MeSH-appropriate papers in non-boilerplate cells, else null mesh_basis dictionary string cell-v5.3 / cell-v5.3 (arxiv_embed_align; MeSH-appropriate papers only) mesh_appropriate boolean reference tier only: whether MeSH applies to the paper

Strings other than doc_id are dictionary-encoded; the file is zstd-compressed and replaced atomically (written to .tmp, then renamed). If the arXiv embedding alignment is absent, the builder falls back to the lexical alignment and writes wiki_basis = arxiv-lexalign:<basis> and mesh_basis = arxiv-lexalign-v5.3-lexicon.

Rules enforced by the builders: every reference doc_id starts with arxiv_complete__; no embedded doc_id does; no reference id occurs in the embedded tier. Within-tier duplicates are counted and reported, not rejected.

Measured 2026-09-23 (web/licence/estate_licence_rollup.json, web/estate_doc_rollup.json):

Measure Value Rows 93,056,465 (embedded 89,907,669 · reference 3,148,796) Distinct documents 84,521,016 (embedded 81,372,220 · reference 3,148,796) Sources 137 Wikipedia-linked rows embedded 89,907,669 · reference 3,148,796 Rows with a MeSH concept embedded 89,907,665 · reference 194,054 Licence status, scope, resolution see Acquisition and licence

Reference-tier alignment numbers differ between records

The project's licence reference page (2026-09-23) reports 2,562,475 Wikipedia-linked and 213,809 MeSH-labelled arXiv rows: those are the lexical-alignment figures, which the arXiv registry entry's alignment block also records (wiki_linked: 2562475). The estate rollup in the repository, built later the same day with the embedding alignment, reports 3,148,796 and 194,054. The current file follows the rollup. Also see the two-builder warning on Acquisition and licence.

docs.title: Exact decontamination records
docs.text:
web/decontam_exact.json records whether any evaluation item's text is, verbatim, a document a model was trained on. It is produced by web/dgx/decontam_exact.py and is the only contamination claim panAtlas presents as proven.

Method.

  1. For each benchmark, read the first lm-eval samples_*.jsonl file found (items are identical across checkpoints). All mmlu_* subtasks are merged into mmlu.
  2. From each sample's doc, take every candidate string: question, query, ctx, goal, sentence, premise, text, passage, activity_label; each string or joined list under context.<key>; or context itself. A bare string doc is used as is.
  3. Hash each with the ledger recipe, blake2b(text.encode("utf-8", "ignore"), digest_size=16), raw, with no normalisation.
  4. Semi-join the distinct hashes against doc_ledger_crosswalk.parquet (DuckDB, with a row-group scan fallback) to get in_v4 and in_v5.

Structure. A JSON object keyed by benchmark task name; each value:

Field Type Meaning items integer number of samples-file lines read for the benchmark (lines, not distinct hashes) item_doc_uids_matched_v4 integer distinct item hashes found in the V4 ledger matched_v5 integer distinct item hashes found in the V5 ledger matched_either integer distinct item hashes found in either trained_on boolean matched_either > 0 method string blake2b16 doc_uid membership vs doc_ledger_crosswalk

The asymmetric names (item_doc_uids_matched_v4 but matched_v5) are as written by the script.

Values at HEAD. 16 benchmarks, 38,491 items in total, zero matches and trained_on: false for all 16:

Benchmark key Items Benchmark key Items afrimedqa_mcq 3,600 mathqa 2,985 arc_challenge 1,172 medmcqa 4,183 arc_easy 2,376 medqa_4options 1,273 asdiv 2,305 medxpertqa_text 2,450 commonsense_qa 1,221 mmlu 100 gsm8k 2,638 piqa 1,838 hellaswag 10,042 pubmedqa 500 ifeval 541 winogrande 1,267

Where it lands. web/decontam_enrich.py maps task names to benchmark slugs (for example medqa_4options → medqa, arc_challenge → arc-challenge) and writes a decontam block on each benchmark node in the served graph and on each entry of web/benchmarks_llm.json:

Field Meaning holdout_status proven_trained_on, provably_held_out, partial, not_held_out or unchecked, from a hand-maintained list per benchmark (the earlier 13-gram decontamination audit) holdout_note the sentence explaining that status exact_doc_uid.checked true if the benchmark is in decontam_exact.json exact_doc_uid.items, .matched_either copied from decontam_exact.json exact_doc_uid.verdict no verbatim-document match (held out at the exact-document level) or EXACT doc_uid match in training ledger method the recipe in words

At HEAD the served graph has 124 benchmark nodes; 116 carry a decontam block, 16 with exact_doc_uid.checked: true. web/benchmarks_llm.json has 106 blocks, 16 checked. See Benchmarks.

Documented fields differ from the data

docs/evaluation-dimensions-and-metadata.md §G lists exact_doc_uid = {checked, matched_either, matched_v4, matched_v5}. The data and decontam_enrich.py carry {checked, items, matched_either, verdict}; per-run V4/V5 matches are only in decontam_exact.json. The 106 blocks in web/benchmarks_llm.json also lack holdout_status and holdout_note, which the graph's blocks have.

Limits of the exact check

It detects verbatim identity of a whole field with a whole training document. A reformatted, truncated or paraphrased copy, or an item embedded inside a longer training document, does not match. Zero matches means "not trained on verbatim", not "not seen". All 16 benchmarks are text; no imaging benchmark has an exact-overlap record.

docs.title: Registry labels v5.3
docs.text: The v5.3 promotion (job 219233, 2026-09-07, 19 minutes) relabelled the estate's 1,740 cells with MeSH descriptors and wrote per-document label artifacts. An independent job (219234, p6_verify.py) verified every count below. Originals were backed up before the change; a promotion log and a labels manifest record it.

docs.title: Cell tables
docs.text:
cell2concept.json (the v5.3 table on the cluster; the v1 copy is kept beside it):

Field Meaning cell_id cell number topic_cluster, subtopic_cluster the cell's cluster coordinates (join key to master_doc_index) count documents in the cell slug mesh-<primary_dui> for a v5.3 cell; the v1 concept-* slug otherwise cos, cell_domain, topic_summary v1 fields (cosine to the v1 concept, domain, summary sentence) primary_dui, primary_name the v5.3 primary MeSH descriptor enrichment, support and top-8 fields the statistics that chose the primary boilerplate, primary_is_boilerplate boilerplate flags (the estate builder reads these two keys) label_source v5.3 or v1

The repository copy, web/cell2concept.json, is the v1 table: it has only the v1 fields above, and all 1,740 slugs are concept-* (see the warning on Identifiers). The exact key names of the enrichment, support and top-8 fields are recorded only in the cluster file and the labels manifest; they could not be verified from the repository.

cell2concept_llm.json maps cell_id to the concept name used for the concept column.

Measured: 1,740 cells; 1,380 carry a v5.3 primary; 360 cells with fewer than 200 labelled rows keep their v1 label and say so. 114 cells (11,217,630 rows) are flagged boilerplate because their primary is in a fixed set of 28 descriptors; their primaries are flagged, not replaced. In master_doc_index.parquet, the concept column was remapped through the new table: 89,890,687 rows changed, and the verification found the column agrees with the cell table on all 89,907,669 rows (0 mismatches, 4 null concepts).

docs.title: Per-document artifacts (labels_v53/)
docs.text:
All arrays are in e8 row order (the order of the embedding store), not master order. e8_to_master_rowmap.npy maps an e8 row to a master row; e8 lists the SFT rows first, so e8 row 0 is master row 77,327,492. The map is unique, and e8 ids 0 to 2,999 were checked equal to the registry doc_id at the mapped row. The map carries ids only; there is no content join.

Artifact Size Content Measured doc_mesh_labels_v53.npz 8.95 GiB per-row lexical MeSH labels, CSR over e8 rows (estate linker, lexicon v5.3) 83,752,006 labelled rows · 2,066,519,278 pairs doc_mesh_labels_v53_granular.npz 3.08 GiB the most specific labels per row 81,505,814 rows · 501,191,944 pairs doc_mesh_edges_v53_s1.npz, _s2.npz 55.67 GiB each weighted document → descriptor edges for two seeds of a 10 % held-out split; fields share, enr, nlp (fp16), flags (bit 0 lexical, bit 1 neighbour), base rates, hold mask, neighbour count s1: 5,292,977,718 edges over 85,546,517 documents; s2: 5,292,887,159 over 85,547,766; about 58.9 per document, median 13 neighbour edges, no cap knn_exact96/ the exact 96 nearest neighbours of every document: 86 parts of idx (int32) and sim (fp16), plus mean.npy; exhaustive search over the text-encoder vectors, centred on the corpus mean last part 778,709 × 96 doc_ids_e8_order.txt 2.37 GiB the document id of every e8 row cell_boilerplate_flags.json, P4_relabel_report.json small boilerplate flags and the relabel report

The edge build also wrote P5_edges_report_s1.json and P5_edges_report_s2.json, and the lexicon build lexicon_v53.jsonl with lexicon_v53_report.json; the project record names them but not whether they sit inside labels_v53/.

Total labels_v53/: 186,798,930,278 B, re-measured with du -sb on 2026-09-19 (an earlier "140 GB" figure was low).

Derived label arrays cannot be redacted row by row

An .npz is a zip of whole arrays and a CSR row cannot be blanked without rewriting them. Removing one document from labels_v53/ means invalidating and recomputing it from the retained recipe (jobs 219233 and 219234, lexicon v5.3). The cost of that recompute has not been measured. The Parquet tables, by contrast, are row-group structured and can be sharded so that a withdrawal touches only its own rows. doc_ids_e8_order.txt is 89.9 M unkeyed content-derived ids; see the storage rule on Identifiers.

docs.title: PMC identifier map
docs.text:
PMC documents in the V4 and V5 corpora were trained without per-article ids. Their identity was recovered by content anchor (job 212698, 2026-08-16): a 12-word key from each trained document's opening matched against the June-2026 Open Access baseline; a key that maps to two ids in one corpus is dropped as ambiguous (37,854, 0.5 %), never guessed. Result: 7,194,690 of 7,686,832 baseline members matched (93.6 %), giving pmc_doc_pmid_map.parquet with columns doc_uid, pmcid, pmid, in_v4, in_v5, corpus_index, match_offset (14,383,878 rows, V4 and V5 renditions) and a list of 6,978,012 exact trained PMIDs. It is the one table that links a ledger doc_uid to a publisher identifier.

Related pages: Identifiers, Acquisition and licence, Dataset registry, Benchmarks, Evaluation records, Models and curriculum.

docs.title: Evaluation records
docs.text: This page documents how panAtlas records evaluation results: the axes it evaluates along, every field of every result record, the rules that keep a result off a leaderboard, and how one result attaches to a model, a benchmark and a dataset. Benchmark descriptions are on Benchmarks; model and training records are on Models and curriculum. Counts were computed with python3 from the files at repo HEAD 57505c6 on 2026-11-10.

docs.title: Evaluation dimensions
docs.text:
docs/evaluation-dimensions-and-metadata.md defines six axes. panAtlas is a map from evaluation documents (benchmark items) to concepts, so any model that is tested, including one never trained on panAtlas data, can be placed on the concept map.

# Dimension What it relates Where it lives in the data Status 1 Document → concept Each benchmark item → a MeSH or Wikipedia concept qconcept and qconcept2 mappings; covers_topic edges; ontology facet concept_fit Built for 21 (first mapping) and 20 (judge-gated) benchmarks 2 Concept × capability What the item is about × what kind of task Concept nodes × the capability facet and tests edges Built 3 Model × (concept × capability) Per-item correctness rolled up to per-concept accuracy eval_accuracy on concept nodes; measured_on edges Built for 5 model families on 5 medical QA benchmarks 4 Training ↔ evaluation overlap Per-concept training exposure against evaluation accuracy trained_on, sft_trained_on, stage_trained_on edges; concept corpus_docs; stats.type_topic_gap Built for KOS models (training data known) 5 Decontamination Evaluation item ↔ training-ledger membership Benchmark decontam block Checked for 16 of 106 language benchmarks 6 Benchmark characterization The 26-dimension ontology Registry audit and ontology facets Built for 106 benchmarks

docs.title: How a result attaches
docs.text:
A result is always the score of one model on one benchmark (or suite), measured on that benchmark's items or on a dataset. The graph and the evaluation index express this with these structures:

flowchart LR
    M["model node<br/>full_eval · overall · predictor_eval"]
    B["llm-benchmark / benchmark node"]
    D["dataset node<br/>(predictor suites, test sets)"]
    C["concept node<br/>eval_accuracy"]
    M -- "scored {value, metric}" --> B
    M -- "scored {value, metric, mean_rank}" --> D
    M -- "evaluated_on" --> B
    M -- "measured_on {acc, n}" --> C
    B -- "covers_topic {n}" --> C
    D -- "test_set_of" --> B
    D -- "derived_from" --> D2["source dataset"]
Pattern Edges at HEAD Meaning model scored → llm-benchmark 6 A reference score of one model release on one benchmark; carries value, metric, variant model scored → dataset 79 A predictor model's aggregate score on a frozen suite dataset; carries value, metric, mean_rank or ratio_to_published, src: link_predictors model evaluated_on → llm-benchmark 8 The model was evaluated on the benchmark (no score on the edge) model measured_on → concept 104 Accuracy on the items mapped to that concept; carries acc, n dataset test_set_of → benchmark 14 A dataset is the held-out test set of an imaging benchmark dataset derived_from → dataset 3 A suite dataset was built from a source dataset model evaluated_by → eval-suite 2 KOS models belong to the KOS evaluation suite

Most scores are not edges. They are fields on model nodes (full_eval, predictor_eval), entries in the benchmark registry (model_scores, scores), and records in mm_evals.json, predictor_evals.json and evals_index.json, described below.

docs.title: Language-model battery: full_eval.json
docs.text:
full_eval.json is produced on the HPC cluster by pipeline/ingest_full_eval.py, which walks the two harness result roots, maps each result directory to a canonical model (pinning the published KOS-V4 and KOS-V5 checkpoints, excluding unreleased and intermediate checkpoints), and extracts the headline metric per benchmark. Shape:

{
  "_labels": { "<model key>": "<display name>" },
  "<model key>": {
    "<category>": [
      { "benchmark": "MedQA", "metric": "acc", "value": 0.2789, "n": 1273, "higher_better": true }
    ]
  }
}
Row field Rows (of 1,142) Meaning benchmark 1,142 Benchmark or sub-benchmark name as the harness reports it metric 1,142 Metric name value 1,142 Score higher_better 1,142 Direction n 1,104 Number of items scored source 30 Where the value came from, when not the harness summary

At HEAD the file holds 39 models. Categories and the number of models with each: knowledge-qa 39, reasoning 39, general-knowledge 39, biomedical-nlp 39, hallucination 39, calibration 39, radiology 38, safety 20, long-context 19, instruction-following 9, math 3.

docs.title: Fields attach_full_eval.py writes on model nodes
docs.text:
Field Model nodes Meaning full_eval 39 The model's entry from full_eval.json, by category overall 39 Composite score: mean over the canonical battery (below), or null if fewer than 15 of the 21 benchmarks were run cat_scores 39 Mean per category over the higher-is-better rows ece 39 Expected calibration error from the calibration category (lower is better; kept out of overall) battery_n 39 Number of canonical-battery benchmarks the model has params_b 39 Parameter count in billions, from an override table or parsed from the label

The canonical battery (CANON in attach_full_eval.py) is fixed at 21 benchmarks: MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, MedXpertQA, AfriMed-QA; MMLU clinical knowledge, college medicine, college biology, medical genetics, professional medicine, anatomy, nutrition, virology, high school biology; BC5CDR (chem NER), NCBI-Disease (NER), BIOSSES (similarity), HoC (Hallmarks of Cancer); Med-HALT FCT, FQT and NOTA. The composite is a per-benchmark mean, not a per-category mean, so a one-benchmark category cannot weigh as much as an eleven-benchmark one. docs/model-evaluation-system.md section 4 records why: an earlier per-category average ranked KOS-V4 above KOS-V5 because the two had run different tests.

docs.title: Per-concept accuracy: concept_accuracy.json
docs.text:
pipeline/build_concept_accuracy.py joins per-item correctness (samples_*.jsonl, by item index) to the first item-to-concept mapping. Only clean one-to-one, count-matched joins are accepted.

{
  "result": {
    "<family>": {
      "<bench>": {
        "<concept id>": { "n": 1090, "correct": 380.0, "acc": 0.3486 },
        "__ckpt": "<checkpoint that produced the samples>",
        "__n": 1273
      }
    }
  },
  "coverage": [ { "bench": "medqa", "family": "kos-v4", "ckpt": "...", "items": 1273, "overall_acc": 0.282 } ]
}

Families at HEAD: kos-v4, kos-v5, kos-v6, biomedlm, qwen3-4b-instruct.

enrich_graph.py folds this into the graph. It keeps only the five medical QA benchmarks (MedQA, MedXpertQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, AfriMed-QA) and excludes kos-v6 (EXCLUDE_MODELS, marked "unreleased"). For each concept it writes:

"eval_accuracy": {
  "<family>": { "acc": 0.1748, "n": 103,
                "benchmarks": { "medqa": { "n": 24, "acc": 0.2083, "ckpt": "<checkpoint>" } } }
}

and one measured_on edge per (model, concept) with acc and n. At HEAD 26 nodes carry eval_accuracy (6 concept, 18 specialty, the root and the gate), and there are 104 measured_on edges. Every per-benchmark entry records ckpt, the exact checkpoint that produced it.

docs.title: Registry scores: model_scores and scores
docs.text:
Two fields of benchmarks_llm.json carry results (see Benchmarks):

Field Entries Shape Meaning model_scores 23 benchmarks {<model name>: {value, metric}} Battery scores matched from full_eval.json by reconcile_benchmarks.py scores 7 benchmarks {<variant>: {value, metric, model, verified, source}} Verified reference scores of a KOS release (for example V5-Instruct) from the canonical harness verified_published 7 true bool The benchmark has a published reference score the harness is checked against

docs.title: Imaging and multimodal: mm_evals.json
docs.text: web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/mm_evals.json is the generic registry for imaging and multimodal evaluations. It is built on the cluster by pipeline/build_mm_evals.py (radiology) and extended by build_patho_evals.py (pathology). build_mm_evals.py infers each evaluation's eval_type from the structure of its result files, and modality follows from one rule table, so nothing about modality is typed by hand.

mm_evals.json has no modality field on benchmarks

docs/model-evaluation-system.md section 11 gives the shape as {benchmarks:[{id, project, modality, domain, metric, models:[{name, score, ...}]}]}. No benchmark entry carries modality; it is derived from eval_type through eval_type_modality, as build_mm_evals.py states. The shape also omits eval_type, name, withheld, withheld_note, eval_source, measures and caveat.

The pathology harness that feeds the *-eva entries is recorded in the vault (reference-pathology-fm-eval-harness): kaiko-ai eva 0.4.5, frozen-encoder linear probe, a single linear head, balanced accuracy on the official test split averaged over five runs, seed 42. Embargoed in-house encoders are evaluated but not published; they are counted in withheld.

docs.title: Tabular and forecasting: predictor_evals.json
docs.text:
web/predictor_evals.json holds the predictor-model suites (tabular and time-series foundation models with classical baselines). It is generated by web/fm_suite/suite/export_panatlas.py from raw results that are kept on the cluster, not in the repository. Its _note states the protocol: every model sees the same rows, folds and context; open-weight models only, run locally.

Top level: _note, generated (ISO timestamp, 2026-10-31 at HEAD), benchmarks (4 suites).

Suite Fields Model fields fm-suite-tabular-medical dataset, protocol, primary_metric, models, comparison, per_task_primary, per_task_all, task_meta splits, ok, tasks_ok, mean_roc_auc, mean_log_loss, mean_balanced_accuracy, mean_r2, mean_fit_s, failed (17 models) fev-bench dataset, metric, models, per_task_error, task_meta tasks, skill_vs_seasonal_naive, ratio_to_published (28 models) fm-suite-ts-health dataset, metric, models, per_task_error, task_meta tasks, skill_vs_seasonal_naive (29 models) tabarena-v0.1-lite dataset, protocol, rows rows: method, elo, elo_plus, elo_minus, ours Sub-field Meaning dataset The registry URN of the frozen suite dataset, for example panatlas:dataset:fm-suite-tabular-medical protocol Frozen protocol, for example "42 tasks (37 OpenML medical + 5 estate); frozen 5-fold splits, 3 repeats when n < 2500; training context capped at 50,000 rows; … seed 0; no tuning" comparison tasks (tasks in the comparison, 41), dropped (tasks dropped for every model), in_progress, held_out (per model: task → failure reason) task_meta Tabular: kind (binary, multiclass, regression), test_rows, features, metric. Forecasting: horizon, seasonality per_task_primary, per_task_all, per_task_error Task → model → value metric (forecasting) "SQL (scaled quantile loss); skill = 1 - geometric mean of error / seasonal-naive error over the tasks"

The model registry for these models is models.json → predictors.models (58 records: id, name, family, kind, role, source, embedding, open_weights, runs, status, results, wrapper, and for 12 not_run_reason). link_predictors.py puts them in the graph as model-predictor-* nodes (46 at HEAD) with:

Node field Meaning role foundation-model or baseline family, source, open_weights, embedding Identity; embedding states that the model has no fixed embedding space predictor_eval Per suite: tabular (mean_primary, mean_rank, tasks_won, beats_best_baseline, tasks, splits, ok, mean_roc_auc, mean_r2, tasks_ok, held_out_of_comparison), tabular_per_task, fev-bench and fm-suite-ts-health (tasks, skill_vs_seasonal_naive, ratio_to_published) eval_status "evaluated on the frozen predictor suite (web/predictor_evals.json)"

Each predictor model also gets a scored edge to the suite dataset node. The suite dataset gets derived_from edges to the datasets its tasks were built from.

docs.title: The unified index: evals_index.json
docs.text:
web/build_evals_index.py builds web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/evals_index.json, the one evaluation index behind the public API (docs/public-api.md, version 1.1). It reads benchmarks_llm.json, full_eval.json (through the graph), mm_evals.json, predictor_evals.json and models.json, and computes ranks, leaders, baselines and headlines so the API routes only filter and serve. By rule, internal fields, paths, hosts and job numbers are never returned.

Top level: generated, note, types, suites, models, tasks, vocab.

Key Content at HEAD types 5 model types, each with label, evaluated_models, evaluated_baselines, not_run, scored_benchmarks, benchmarks: language 38 models / 26 benchmarks; vision 27 / 13; multimodal 1 / 1; tabular 11 + 6 baselines, 4 not run / 2; forecasting 24 + 5 baselines, 8 not run / 2 suites 142 suites (language 124, vision 13, tabular 2, forecasting 2, multimodal 1); 56 scored, 86 cataloged models 124 model records (language 38, forecasting 37, vision 27, tabular 21, multimodal 1); 112 evaluated, 12 not-run tasks Per-task results of the predictor suites vocab Query vocabulary: type words, domain words, aliases, task words

Suite record fields: id, name, type, domain, task_type, metric, higher_better, rank_by (value, or mean_rank for one suite), what, how_to_read, run_status, kw, n_models, ranking; and on some node, capabilities, cap_ids, headline, part_of, dataset, n_tasks, best_baseline, value_metric, dropped_tasks, held_out.

Model record fields: id, name, type, types, role (model, foundation-model, baseline), scores, n_benchmarks, status; and on some node, family, source, open_weights, runs, published_leaderboard, not_run_reason, note.

Score fields (1,426 scores): suite, value, metric, rank, of; and on some published, verified, ratio_to_published, mean_rank, held_out, tasks, same_tasks_leader. Rows taken from a published leaderboard for methods with no run of ours are kept in published_leaderboard, apart from scores and from every count. Values are compared only within one benchmark.

docs.title: Keeping results honest: verification and withholding
docs.text: Mechanism Where Rule leaderboard_eligible + withheld_reason Curriculum record, copied to model nodes by build_curriculum.py A model with leaderboard_eligible: false is shown for its curriculum only, not ranked. At HEAD: KOS-V6-Instruct ("contamination unchecked; V6 pretrain lineage still in flight"), lesion_lg_cohort_reg_dino ("intermediate checkpoint (iter 170k of 200k), no downstream KOS-run measurement"); KOS-V6 base is true verified (curriculum) model_curriculum.json, copied to model nodes as curriculum_verified (8 nodes) Free text giving a date and a method, for example "2026-08-01 vault audit (two independent token censuses agree to 0.0001%)" verified (result) mm_evals.json result records, evals_index.json scores, registry scores Boolean withheld, withheld_note mm_evals.json benchmarks Count of results evaluated but not listed, and why: in-house models need verified training and evaluation before listing; embargoed models are never published comparison.held_out predictor_evals.json A model that failed some tasks is held out of the cross-model comparison, with the failure reason per task; evals_index.json marks its scores held_out and names the leader on the same tasks not_run_reason models.json predictors, evals_index.json Why a registered model has no result (licence gate, timeout, missing toolkit) Checkpoint pinning eval_accuracy[...].benchmarks[...].ckpt, concept_accuracy.json __ckpt Every per-concept accuracy names the exact checkpoint Exclusions enrich_graph.py EXCLUDE_MODELS = {"kos-v6"}; ingest_full_eval.py Unreleased and intermediate checkpoints stay out of comparisons

docs.title: Strata and context axes
docs.text:
The context axes on which a result can be sliced today are the fields above: concept (topic), capability, testing type, evaluation domain, artifact type, modality (through eval_type), model_stage, arm, harness tier, provenance (official or homegrown), checkpoint and model release (variant).

Population and setting strata are designed but not built for results. ARCHITECTURE.md and PLAN.md define six strata axes as controlled strata- pages (geography, culture, population, environment, care setting, equipment), a dataset page field strata[], and a result- page type with context[] (strata), dataset_slice, score, safety_subscore and a run:<id> provenance tag. The repository's markdown atlas holds two strata pages (strata-geography-us, strata-care-setting-ed, both status: draft) and no result- pages. The one strata field in the served graph (on the KOS-V5 SFT mix node) counts SFT record kinds, not population strata.

docs.title: Graph schema
docs.text:
This page documents every node type and every edge type in the panAtlas served graph, with the property keys each one carries and the script that writes it. Every count on this page was computed with python3 from the served graph file at repo HEAD 57505c6 on 2026-11-10. Nothing here is taken from a summary block or a design document unless the text says so.

The served graph is web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/graph.json. It is the property graph the explorer renders, the input to the RDF export (RDF vocabulary) and the input to the evaluation index behind the public API (Evaluation records). In the terms of GRAPH_STANDARDS.md it is layer 3, the "working / evidence property graph", which is a projection of the terminology backbone and the clinical instance layer. See Knowledge layers for how the layers relate.

The stats block inside graph.json is stale

graph.json carries a stats object, but several scripts rewrite parts of it and enrich_graph.py replaces it wholesale, so it no longer matches the file. At HEAD: stats.edges says 13,869 (the file has 17,119); stats.edges_by_rel has no entry for ten relations that exist (for example has_artifact_type, stage_trained_on, has_register); stats.layers reports concept 203, dataset 174, ontology 43; stats.concept_classes reports 44 model nodes (there are 90); and stats.curriculum.models_curriculum_undisclosed is 1 (36 model nodes carry curriculum_disclosed: false). Compute counts from nodes and edges, never from stats.

docs.title: File format
docs.text:
graph.json is one JSON object with four keys:

Key Type Content stats object Summary counters written by the build scripts (stale, see above) plus measured corpus figures such as footprint, documents_mapped and image_documents roots list ["atlas-root"], the entry node for navigation nodes list 6,187 node objects edges list 17,119 edge objects

docs.title: Node object
docs.text:
Four keys are on every node: id, label, kind, layer. Every other key is optional and depends on the kind. The most widely used optional keys are:

Key Nodes carrying it Meaning source 5,953 Free-text statement of where the node's content came from modality 5,701 text, structured, imaging-ct, imaging-ultrasound-rf, time-series, imaging-wsi, imaging, genomics, or an omics-* value concept_class 5,577 knowledge (5,252), evaluation (195), model (90), artifact-type (35), register (5) built_by 5,543 Free-text statement of the method that produced the node (for example "grounded to MeSH via UMLS UTS (resolver + adversarial audit + live confirmation)") desc 5,500 Description grounding 5,328 Which vocabulary grounds the node; see Controlled vocabularies canonical_id 5,013 Canonical identity, <prefix>:<code>; prefixes in use are mesh (3,390), foodon (1,558), wikipedia (24), fdc (24), panatlas (17) mesh_dui, mesh_name 3,400 MeSH descriptor UI and preferred name

docs.title: Edge object
docs.text:
Every edge has exactly four required keys: from, to, rel, id. Some relations add attributes, listed per relation below.

The edge id is content-addressed:

"e-" + hashlib.blake2b(f"{from}|{to}|{rel}".encode(), digest_size=10).hexdigest()

The same formula appears in enrich_graph.py, hygiene_enrich.py, build_curriculum.py and build_concept_remap.py, so rerunning a script adds no duplicate edges. 16,916 of the 17,119 edges match the formula. The other 203 are the covers_topic edges with basis: arxiv-lexalign, whose ids have the form e-arxiv-<MeSH UI>-<target id>.

docs.title: Standards that govern the graph
docs.text: GRAPH_STANDARDS.md is the decision record, adopted 2026-07-26 and extended 2026-09-26. Its binding rules are summarised here with what the served graph does.

docs.title: Identity and grounding
docs.text:
GRAPH_STANDARDS.md was written for medicine, the domain the atlas started with, so its grounding rules name medical vocabularies. The served graph applies the same idea to other domains with their own vocabularies (FoodOn and FoodData Central for foods, Wikipedia for general concepts; see Code systems). As written:

  • Every node must be tied to a real MeSH descriptor or another core concept (SNOMED CT or a UMLS concept). There are to be no orphan nodes.
  • A concept's canonical identity is its MeSH descriptor UI, for example mesh:D002309 for Cardiology. The MeSH UI is the deduplication key: two nodes with the same UI are the same concept.
  • MeSH is canonical over Wikipedia. Wikipedia is a readable overlay on a MeSH concept (an oldid attribute), never a second node. Wikipedia is the fallback identity only for non-MeSH, non-medical nodes, which may instead carry a Wikidata QID.
  • LAYERS.md restates the same rule as the substrate: identity is canonical_id, and two systems that emit the same canonical_id name the same entity without reconciliation.

1,174 nodes carry no canonical_id

The grounding rule is written for concepts, but it says "every node". At HEAD 1,174 nodes have no canonical_id: all 513 dataset, 172 food-category, 106 llm-benchmark, 90 model, 35 capability, 21 testing-type, 18 fhir, 18 benchmark, 15 authority, 14 training-stage, 13 capability-group, 9 eval-domain, 5 domain, 4 codebase, 3 guideline, 3 gen-category, 2 group, 2 system, 1 kg, 1 atlas-root and 1 eval-suite node, and also 118 concept and 10 disease nodes. The 118 concepts are the 117 Wikipedia-grounded general concepts that build_concept_remap.py creates with wiki_title and wp_url but no canonical_id (where build_layered.py would write wikipedia:<slug>), plus one corpus-classification concept. The 10 diseases are FoodAtlas diseases whose upstream id is OMIM, flagged with grounding: none and a grounding_note.

docs.title: Hierarchy and edge direction
docs.text:
• The medical concept hierarchy comes from MeSH tree numbers. A descriptor's parent is the descriptor whose tree number is the immediate prefix. Specialties live in the MeSH H02 tree, diseases in C, techniques in E. In the served graph this hierarchy is the part_of relation with src: mesh_tree (3,360 edges); hand-curated links carry src: curated (1,845).
  • Backbone edges are SKOS-aligned. The property graph does not use SKOS names. The RDF export declares pa:partOf rdfs:subPropertyOf skos:broader and pa:related rdfs:subPropertyOf skos:related, and writes every code as skos:exactMatch. It writes no skos:narrower.
  • Edges point from the specific or owning node to the general or target node: a child is part_of its parent, a dataset covers a concept, a model is scored against a benchmark, a training stage follows the stage before it.

GRAPH_STANDARDS.md does not state naming rules. The served graph follows these conventions consistently: kind values are lower case with hyphens; rel values are lower case snake case verb phrases; node ids are lower case, prefixed by kind (concept-, bench-, model-, dataset-, atype-, stage-), with MeSH expansion nodes as mesh-D<UI> and FoodAtlas nodes as fa-dis- and fa-food-. Identifier rules are on Identifiers.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
• Sources are evidence, not authority. Only panAtlas verification makes a fact verified, and a curator sign-off is recorded as verified_by.
  • FHIR-derived and vocabulary-derived assertions enter as evidence with provenance. Automatic MeSH groundings are adversarially verified, one agent per concept, each confirming the descriptor with a live UTS call, before they are trusted.
  • Every triple lives in exactly one named graph, and the named graph is its source of record. panAtlas curates only https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas; mirrored graphs are read-only. See RDF vocabulary.
  • A dataset maintained elsewhere carries maintained_externally: true and a source_of_record block with the keys system, graph, agent, upstream_version, upstream_last_updated_on, held_version, endpoint, registry_file, registry_commit, funding, homepage, authoritative_namespaces, authoritative_declared. See Dataset registry.
  • LAYERS.md requires every edge to carry an origin (ontology-tree, curated, embedding-derived, agent-contributed) and evidence (for example {model, version, cosine}), so that connectivity merges as attributed claims.

Edge provenance in the served graph is partial

No edge in the served graph has an origin or an evidence attribute, and no node or edge has a verified_by attribute. Provenance is carried instead by src (5,715 edges), via (437), basis (216) and, for measured edges, n_docs, n, sim and acc. 10,863 edges carry none of src, via or basis. On nodes, provenance is the free-text source and built_by fields. The closest implementation of the contract is in the attach process (embed_attach.py and the local agent report, see Knowledge layers), which writes one nested attribute, claims: {origin: "embedding", model, version, cosine, canonical_id}, on its classified_as edges. Those edges are federation reports and are not in the served graph.
