docs.title: Build order
docs.text:
Each build script reads the served graph.json, changes it in place and writes it back. The ordered entry point is web/build_all.sh. Its stated precondition is that the upstream builders (build_graph.py, build_layered.py, build_all_datasets.py, build_train_sources.py, build_source_topics.py, sft_wiring.py, build_corpus_structure.py, model_wiring.py, build_benchmark_nodes.py, build_concept_remap.py, apply_bench_taxonomy.py) have already run. It then runs, in order:

python3 build_artifact_types.py
python3 build_curriculum.py
python3 build_record_level.py
python3 pipeline/existing_meta/merge_gap.py || true
python3 build_existing_meta.py
python3 build_native_meta.py
python3 build_field_values.py
python3 build_patho_evals.py
python3 build_eval_map.py
python3 pipeline/check_curriculum_vault.py
node pipeline/ui_harness.js

Scripts outside this sequence also write the graph: enrich_graph.py (measured_on, eval_accuracy), hygiene_enrich.py (grounded_in, contamination downgrades), attach_full_eval.py (model evaluation fields), reconcile_benchmarks.py, the link_*.py scripts and register_*.py fragments. No single script rebuilds the whole graph from scratch, so the order in which these were last run determines the file.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
Status

Built and in use. Every scheme on this page exists in the repository data or in the cluster-side artifacts it describes. Counts were computed from the repository at HEAD 57505c6 (2026-10-31) unless a different date is given. Counts for cluster-side artifacts (the document ledger, the estate index, the v5.3 labels) come from dated measurements recorded by the project and are marked as such.

panAtlas follows one rule, stated in web/ID-POLICY.md: every entity and every relationship has a unique, stable id. In practice there are several id families. They differ in how they are minted (assigned by hand, derived from a name, or computed from content) and in what they promise:

Family Form Minted from Promise Dataset URN panatlas:dataset:<slug> the slug, assigned at registration global handle for one dataset; never reassigned Dataset slug [a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)* a name, assigned by the registering script unique in the registry; equals the URN suffix Item namespace id_namespace, e.g. ctrate: assigned at registration scopes item ids inside one dataset (see the collision warning below) Graph node id <prefix>-<slug> per builder unique in graph.json Graph edge id e- + blake2b-10 of from\|to\|rel content of the edge duplicate edges collapse to one id Document uid doc_uid = blake2b-16 of raw text the text itself same text, same id, in every lineage Estate document id doc_id, e.g. <source>__<NNNNNNNNN>__c<KKKK> position in a source unique across estate tiers Manifest hash sha256: + 64 hex the canonical file inventory identical inventory, identical hash Version tag model@version, schema /1, upstream revisions assigned or upstream names one embedding space, schema or release Job id Slurm job number the scheduler provenance pointer to the run that produced a value

The sections below define each one, name the script that mints it, and give the stability and collision rules.

docs.title: Dataset URN
docs.text:
panatlas:dataset:<slug>

The URN is the single global handle for a dataset (PLAN-datasets.md §1). It is the key used by every registry upsert, by the manager plugin configuration (panatlas_dataset_id), by manager reports, and by the cross-references between registry entries (derived_from, part_of, partition_of, members, corpus).

Only one URN kind exists. A search of every JSON, Python, Markdown, Java, JavaScript and PHP file in the repository finds 2,305 occurrences of a panatlas:<kind>: prefix, and all of them are panatlas:dataset:. Models, benchmarks, concepts and other entities are identified by graph node ids, not URNs.

Where URNs Notes web/datasets.json (the registry) 200 all distinct; urn == "panatlas:dataset:" + slug for all 200 Fragment files web/datasets_*.json 65 every fragment URN is also in web/datasets.json Served catalog web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/datasets.json 622 the 200 registry URNs plus 422 catalog-only entries; urn == prefix + slug for all 622

How a URN is minted: the registering script writes urn and slug together. The minting scripts and their slug rules are listed under Dataset slug. Every upsert path asserts URN uniqueness before writing (assert len(urns) == len(set(urns)) in web/register_fragment.py, web/register_tcga.py, web/register_okn.py; sync_catalog.py asserts the same over the catalog).

Dangling URN references

URN cross-references are not checked against the registry. At HEAD, 26 distinct URNs named in derived_from lists do not resolve to a registry entry (for example panatlas:dataset:trialgpt, panatlas:dataset:ultrainteract-sft, several router and tool packs). 16 of the 26 exist in the served catalog as catalog-only entries; 10 exist nowhere. Treat derived_from as a provenance claim, not a foreign key.

docs.title: Dataset slug
docs.text:
Rules, computed over all 200 registry entries at HEAD:

  • Lowercase ASCII letters, digits and single hyphens: every slug matches ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$.
  • Longest slug: 35 characters.
  • slug is the URN suffix, the manifest file stem (web/manifests/<slug>.manifest.json), the manager payload stem (<slug>.report.json, <slug>.instance.json), and (for registry entries that have a graph node) the suffix of the node id dataset-<slug>.

Slugs are assigned by the script that registers the dataset. The rule differs per script:

Script Slug rule Example web/acquisition/okn/okn_agent.py (describe) okn- + the OKN graph short name okn-babel web/register_openh.py openh-rf- + subset name lowercased, runs of non-[a-z0-9] replaced by - openh-rf-oslo web/derive_source_manifests.py (slug_for) ct- + the corpus source directory name with _ replaced by - ct-nlst web/build_all_datasets.py, web/build_train_sources.py (nid) dataset- + source name lowercased, runs of non-[a-z0-9] replaced by -; the slug is the node id without dataset- catalog-only entries web/register_arxiv.py, web/register_neuropath.py, web/renal_sbir_registry.py, fragments written literally in the script or fragment arxiv-complete, kits23

Stability and reuse:

  • web/ID-POLICY.md: "a slug is never reused for a different thing." No code enforces this beyond the duplicate-URN assertion, which only prevents two live entries with one slug.
  • Two retired slugs survive only as manifest files: web/manifests/heartlens-ct.manifest.json and web/manifests/nlst-ct.manifest.json (2026-07-31 manifests from the first registration in PLAN-datasets.md §3). Neither slug is in the registry today; the CT data they named is now registered under heartlens-ct3d-native and its ct-* partitions. Do not mint either slug again.

docs.title: Graph node id for a dataset
docs.text:
A registry entry is represented in the knowledge graph by the node dataset-<slug> (web/ID-POLICY.md). At HEAD the served graph (web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/graph.json, 6,187 nodes) has 513 nodes of kind dataset: 400 with prefix dataset-, 101 with dsft- (SFT mixes) and 12 with ext-. 104 of the 200 registry entries have a dataset-<slug> node; the other 96 are catalogued without a graph node.

Node ids that do not follow the slug

web/multimodal.json keys its ten imaging entries by node ids such as dataset-ctrate-train, while the registry slug for the same dataset is ct-rate. One node with the dataset- prefix (dataset-foodatlas) has kind kg, not dataset. Join registry entries to graph nodes by dataset-<slug> only where that node exists, and do not infer one from the other.

The other graph node prefixes, with their counts in the served graph at HEAD, are listed below for completeness. Their meaning is documented in Graph schema.

Prefix Nodes Prefix Nodes fa- (fa-dis- 3,170, fa-food- 1,582) 4,752 capgroup- 13 dataset- 401 ext- 12 concept- 206 evdomain- 9 fndds- 172 nacc- 5 mesh- 142 domain- 5 bench- 124 register- 5 dsft- 101 codebase- 4 model- 90 doc- 3 cap- 35 gen- 3 atype- 35 group- 2 type- 21 atlas-, suite-, sys-, system- 1 each onto- 15 null (a literal node id) 1 stage- 14 fhir- 13

A node whose id is the string null

The served graph contains one node with id null. web/ID-POLICY.md requires a non-empty id on every node; the string passes that check but is almost certainly a builder writing a missing value. All node ids are otherwise unique (verified at HEAD).

The domain-* / evdomain-* split is the one recorded collision: benchmark domain-* nodes once collided with the knowledge-domain roots and deleted them, so benchmark domains moved to evdomain-* (web/ID-POLICY.md).

docs.title: MeSH-derived ids
docs.text:
MeSH descriptors appear in four forms. DUIs are NLM descriptor unique ids (D followed by six or nine digits).

Form Where Minted by Count mesh:<DUI> canonical_id on concept nodes concept builders per node mesh-<DUI> graph node id for a MeSH descriptor node web/build_layered.py (nid = "mesh-" + dui) 142 nodes in the served graph, all kind concept mesh-<DUI> slug of a v5.3 cell record in the cluster's cell2concept.json the v5.3 label promotion (job 219233, p6_promote.py) 1,380 of 1,740 cells (measured 2026-09-07, verified by job 219234) fa-dis-<DUI> FoodAtlas disease nodes FoodAtlas builders 3,170 nodes

The v5.3 promotion gave every cell with at least 200 labelled rows a primary MeSH descriptor and set its slug to mesh-<primary_dui>; the 360 cells below that floor kept their v1 concept-* slug. The independent verification job checked that every v5.3 cell's slug equals mesh- + its primary_dui. See Document index.

The repository copy of cell2concept.json is the v1 table

web/cell2concept.json in the repository has 1,740 records whose slugs are all concept-* (50 distinct) and has no primary_dui field. It is the pre-v5.3 table from the initial commit. The v5.3 table with mesh-<DUI> slugs exists on the cluster only. Do not derive v5.3 cell ids from the repository copy.

docs.title: Item namespaces and item ids
docs.text:
Each registry entry may carry an id_namespace. Item ids (a volume, a slide, a study, a row) are written inside that namespace so that they are distinguishable from items of other datasets (PLAN-datasets.md §1): ctrate:vol:train_10000_a_1 belongs to panatlas:dataset:ct-rate.

Measured at HEAD: 194 of 200 entries carry id_namespace (the six predictor-suite entries do not). 159 end in :; the 35 OpenH-RF entries use a path-like form openh-rf:<subset>/. Namespaces are partly hierarchical: all 46 OKN entries use okn:<shortname>:, ten JK-Decide components use jkd1:<component>:.

web/multimodal.json records the item-id scheme for ten imaging datasets (unique_id_scheme), for example:

Dataset Namespace Item id scheme CT-RATE ctrate: volume ctrate:vol:<VolumeName>; slice ctrate:slice:<VolumeName>#z<NNNN> MR-RATE mrrate: study mrrate:study:<study_uid> MIMIC-CXR mimic-cxr: study mimic-cxr:study:<study_id> KiTS23 kits23: case kits23:case_<NNNNN> TCIA TCGA-KIRC tcia_tcga_kirc: series tcia_tcga_kirc:<SeriesInstanceUID>

These namespaces are separate from the text estate's doc_id space (web/multimodal.json _note): a radiology report and its paired volume are two documents in two modalities.

Namespaces are not unique per dataset

PLAN-datasets.md says item ids are "globally unique" because each dataset has its own namespace. The data does not guarantee that: gdc: is shared by four entries (gdc-tcga-kidney, gdc-tcga-slides-meta, tcga-diagnostic-slides, tcga-tissue-slides) and a second namespace is shared by the two neuropathology entries. An item id in a shared namespace identifies the upstream object (a GDC file UUID, for example) but not which registry entry holds it. Qualify item ids with the dataset URN when the distinction matters.

docs.title: Graph edge id
docs.text:
edge.id = "e-" + blake2b(f"{from}|{to}|{rel}".encode(), digest_size=10).hexdigest()

web/ID-POLICY.md defines an edge id as content-addressed on its endpoints and relation, so duplicate edges collapse to one. The builders that add edges (web/build_all_datasets.py, web/enrich_graph.py, web/build_curriculum.py, web/model_wiring.py and others) use digest_size=10, giving 20 hex characters. The link_*.py scripts (link_renal.py, link_neuropath.py, link_openh.py, link_predictors.py) read an existing edge id and choose DIGEST = max(4, (len(sample) - 2) // 2) so that they match whatever length the graph already uses.

Verified at HEAD over the served graph (17,119 edges): all edge ids are unique; 16,916 recompute exactly from the formula above; the remaining 203 have the form e-arxiv-<DUI>-<target> truncated to 60 characters, minted by web/fold_arxiv_alignment.py. Those 203 are name-derived, not content-addressed.

docs.title: Document uid (doc_uid)
docs.text:
doc_uid = hashlib.blake2b(raw_text.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=16).hexdigest()   # 32 hex characters

The text is the identity (web/ID-POLICY.md). The same text has the same doc_uid in every lineage (v4_clean, v4_dedup, v5_tier1, v5_clean, pretrain or SFT). It is computed on raw text with no normalisation. It serves four roles:

  • Join key between training exposure and evaluation (doc_uid → concept, doc_uid → (model, score)).
  • Contamination detector: an evaluation item whose doc_uid equals a training document's was trained on (web/dgx/decontam_exact.py; see Document index).
  • De-duplicator: distinct documents are len(set(doc_uid)); exposure is counted on distinct doc_uid.
  • Cross-version tracker: the ledger crosswalk records, per doc_uid, whether V4 and V5 trained on it.

Minted by the document-ledger build (spec-kit feature 017; ledger jobs 207724, merge 208237, crosswalk 208241, 2026-08-01) over every document that entered the V4 and V5 pretraining runs. Measured numbers are on Document index.

The question map does not use the ledger recipe

web/build_question_concept_map.py writes a doc_uid per benchmark question as hashlib.blake2b(text.encode()).hexdigest(), which is blake2b with its default 64-byte digest (128 hex characters). Those values can never equal a ledger doc_uid. web/ID-POLICY.md notes that the parameters "must be reconciled"; at HEAD they are not. The decontamination script (web/dgx/decontam_exact.py) does use digest_size=16, but encodes with errors="ignore", so text with unencodable code points hashes differently from a strict encode.

doc_uid is unkeyed

Anyone holding a candidate document can recompute its doc_uid and confirm whether it is in the estate. On erasable storage that is the feature that makes decontamination possible. On write-once media it is a permanent membership oracle with no key to destroy. The project's storage rule (recorded 2026-09-19) treats doc_uid, manifest_hash and the e8-ordered id list (labels_v53/doc_ids_e8_order.txt, 89.9 M unkeyed content hashes) as payload-only: they may be stored only inside encrypted objects, never in any cleartext index field. A keyed form, HMAC(K, doc_uid), is safe but loses cross-lineage joinability.

docs.title: Estate document id (doc_id)
docs.text:
doc_id is positional, not content-addressed. It names a row in a source as that source was processed:

Tier / role Form Source Embedded, pretrain <source>__<NNNNNNNNN>__c<KKKK> (document index, chunk index) parsed by web/licence/estate_licence_build.py; e.g. pmc__000000000__c0000 Embedded, SFT <source>…<line number> (the suffix is the source file line number, proved for all 53,505,117 stage-0 rows) web/licence/estate_licence_build.py, vault reference on estate licences Reference (arXiv) arxiv_complete__<paper_id> web/acquisition/arxiv/arxiv_doc_index.py Benchmark question question_id = <bench>__<index> docs/evaluation-dimensions-and-metadata.md §E

Rules enforced by web/estate_doc_index.py: every reference-tier id starts with arxiv_complete__; no embedded-tier id may; the reference ids are probed against every embedded chunk and must not collide. Within the embedded tier, duplicates are counted and reported, not rejected (measured 2026-09-23: 89,907,669 rows, 81,372,220 distinct). See Document index.

doc_id and doc_uid are different keys. doc_id locates a row; doc_uid identifies text. The PMC mapping table pmc_doc_pmid_map.parquet is the one recorded artifact that carries both kinds of key for a source (doc_uid, pmcid, pmid, in_v4, in_v5, corpus_index, match_offset).

docs.title: Manifest hash
docs.text:
manifest_hash = "sha256:" + sha256("\n".join(f"{relpath}\t{size}\t{int(mtime)}" for each file, sorted)).hexdigest()

The audit fingerprint of a dataset's files. Minted by web/dataset_manifest.py (and, byte-compatibly, by web/dataset_manifest_parallel.py and web/derive_source_manifests.py). It changes whenever a file is added, removed, moved, resized, or has its modification time changed. It does not hash file content. Full definition, limits and audit procedure: Manifests.

The hash is also used as a version string: the manager plugin's panatlas_graph_version is the dataset's current manifest_hash, or the literal unversioned when the entry has none (web/build_dataset_reports.py).

docs.title: Version tags
docs.text:
Tag Form Where Notes Embedding space <model-id>@<version> registry embedding_models.<modality> the unit of comparability (PLAN-dataset-plugins.md §2). Values at HEAD: imaging-rad-dino-ct@raddino (33 entries), text-bioclinical-modernbert-large@v3w (18), and one value with no @version (text-bioclinical-modernbert-large, on kos-v6-pretrain-corpus). Registry schema panatlas.datasets/1 meta.schema (or top-level schema) of every registry file other schema tags in the repository include panatlas-model-curriculum/1, panatlas-okn-agent/1, panatlas-artifact-types/1, panatlas-record-level/1, panatlas-record-typing/2 Upstream revision git or Hugging Face commit SHA acquisition.revision, provenance.revision, source_of_record.registry_commit pins the exact upstream snapshot acquired OKN graph version upstream_version, held_version source_of_record upstream release vs the copy held; held_version is null until a verified copy exists Restricted release release name, e.g. 2026AA restricted/umls/<version>/ on the cluster see Acquisition and licence Label release v1, v5.3 cell table, lexicon, labels_v53/ see Document index

The registered text version differs from the tag datasets use

web/models.json registers the text model text-bioclinical-modernbert-large with version v3w-2026.07, while 18 registry entries name it @v3w. It also files the imaging model under modality key imaging, while the registry uses imaging-ct. PLAN-datasets.md and PLAN-dataset-plugins.md still name the CT space imaging-v628-ct@v628; no registry entry uses it at HEAD. A consumer that validates model@version strictly against web/models.json will reject every current entry; compare on the model id and treat the version strings as aliases until they are reconciled.

docs.title: Job ids as provenance
docs.text:
Slurm job numbers are recorded as provenance for values that a cluster job produced. They are pointers, not identifiers of the data: a job id says which run computed a manifest, a label table or an evaluation output, so the run's log and script can be found.

Forms found in the registry at HEAD:

Field Form Example provenance.jobs[] job:<n> job:246943 provenance[] (list-valued provenance) job:<n> job:207661 provenance.job <n> 220272 acquisition.jobs[] <n> <purpose> 220405 probe verification.<release>.job <n> 220431 free text in computed, notes, input_convention job <n>, SLURM job <n> refreshed 2026-09-18, job 220280

33 job:<n> tokens occur in the registry, plus free-text references in the other forms above. The public API removes job numbers and cluster paths from every string it serves (panatlas_pub_scrub in web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/includes/public-api.php), so job ids are visible in the repository and to authenticated tools but not in public responses.

docs.title: What is never reused
docs.text:
• A dataset slug or URN, once registered, names that dataset only (web/ID-POLICY.md). Retired slugs stay retired (heartlens-ct, nlst-ct).
  • A graph node id is never given to a different kind of thing (the domain-* → evdomain-* move was made to restore this).
  • doc_uid, edge ids and manifest_hash cannot be reused: they are functions of content, so the same value always means the same text, edge or inventory.
  • doc_id values are positional. They are stable only for a fixed build of a source; a rebuild that reorders a source changes them. Use doc_uid for anything that must survive a rebuild.

Related pages: Dataset registry, Manifests, Document index, Graph schema, Models and curriculum.

docs.title: Manifests
docs.text:
Status

Built and running. The manifest builder and auditor (web/dataset_manifest.py), the parallel walker (web/dataset_manifest_parallel.py), partition derivation (web/derive_source_manifests.py) and the fold into the registry (web/fold_manifests.py and two older variants) are in the repository and run on the HPC cluster: hourly for every hosted dataset, weekly for the large CT corpus. Measured: 127 registry entries carry a manifest at repository HEAD 57505c6 (2026-10-31), covering 993,790 files and 123.4 TB; the CT corpus full walk of 2026-09-17 is the largest single manifest. Designed, not built: content hashing of small or critical files, and hub-side verification of a manager's reported manifest_hash against the registry (see the warnings below).

A dataset is identified by its URN and audited by its manifest (PLAN-datasets.md §2). The manifest is a canonical, sorted inventory of the files that make up the dataset, reduced to one hash. Recomputing it and comparing the hash answers one question cheaply: is this dataset still the set of files we registered, or has something been added, removed, moved, resized or touched?

docs.title: The canonical inventory
docs.text:
For a registry entry, web/dataset_manifest.py builds the inventory like this:

  1. For each path in locations[]: an absolute path is used as is; a relative path is joined to the estate root (--root, or meta.root_default from the registry).
  2. A path that does not exist is recorded in missing_locations and contributes nothing.
  3. A path that is a file contributes itself. A directory contributes every file below it (os.walk, which does not descend into symbolic links to directories).
  4. Each file contributes the tuple (relpath, size, mtime): relpath is relative to the estate root, size is st_size in bytes, mtime is int(st_mtime) (whole seconds). A file whose stat fails is skipped silently.
  5. The tuples are sorted.
  6. The canonical text is one line per file, relpath<TAB>size<TAB>mtime, joined by \n with no trailing newline.
  7. manifest_hash = "sha256:" + sha256(canonical_text as UTF-8).hexdigest().
entries.sort()
canon = "\n".join(f"{rel}\t{size}\t{mtime}" for rel, size, mtime in entries)
manifest_hash = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(canon.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The hash is stable across runs and across machines that mount the data at the same root. File content is not read.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
build writes two files per dataset into --out (on the cluster, <cluster project storage>/panatlas/cresco/manifests/):

File Content <slug>.files.tsv the full inventory, one relpath<TAB>size<TAB>mtime line per file, sorted, each line newline-terminated <slug>.manifest.json the summary (below), indented JSON

The inventory files stay on the cluster. The repository keeps copies of the summaries only, in web/manifests/: 129 <slug>.manifest.json files and 32 <slug>.fullwalk.manifest.json files at HEAD.

docs.title: Manifest summary fields
docs.text:
The summary is what the registry stores in an entry's manifest field and what a manager reports.

Field Type Meaning Example urn string the dataset URN panatlas:dataset:kits23 file_count integer number of inventory lines 6238 total_bytes integer sum of size over the inventory 52537716929 missing_locations list of string locations[] entries that did not exist at build time [] manifest_hash string sha256: + 64 hex characters over the canonical text sha256:7658896b… computed_at integer Unix time, seconds, when the summary was written 1788689368

Partition manifests cut from a full-walk inventory (web/derive_source_manifests.py) add two fields:

Field Type Meaning derived_from string the inventory the partition was cut from partition string the root-relative prefix (or prefixes) the partition covers

docs.title: manifest_full_walk in the registry
docs.text:
33 registry entries also carry manifest_full_walk: the manifest of the full data, kept when the hourly manifest covers something smaller (an inventory file or index files; see Partitioned and inventory-file manifests). It has the summary fields above (computed_at is absent on one entry) plus:

Field Present Meaning locations 33 the locations the full walk covered (the data itself, not the inventory file) computed 33 free text: when, which tool, which job derived_from 31 as above, on the 31 CT partitions partition 31 as above

Each of these entries also carries an audit_scope string that says, in prose, what the hourly manifest covers and why. Read it before relying on an hourly hash.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
# build: compute manifests, write <slug>.files.tsv + <slug>.manifest.json, optionally fold into the registry
python3 web/dataset_manifest.py build --registry datasets.json --root <estate root> \
    --out <manifest dir> [--only slug1,slug2] [--update-registry]

# audit: recompute and compare against the stored baseline
python3 web/dataset_manifest.py audit --registry datasets.json --root <estate root> \
    [--manifests <manifest dir>] [--only slug1,slug2]

build prints one line per dataset (files=, bytes=, hash, and MISSING=[…] if any location is absent). With --update-registry it writes each summary into the entry's manifest field and rewrites the whole registry file (indent=2). Without it the registry is not touched.

If a directory sits where a .files.tsv or .manifest.json should be written, build moves it to <out>/_displaced/<slug>.<timestamp> and continues. This guard was added after six such directories stopped every hourly refresh from 2026-09-20 17:01 until 2026-09-23 (comment in web/dataset_manifest.py).

docs.title: Audit and exit codes
docs.text:
For each selected entry audit takes the baseline from the registry's manifest field, or, if that is empty, from <manifests>/<slug>.manifest.json. It recomputes the manifest and compares only manifest_hash.

Per-dataset line Meaning OK sha256:… recomputed hash equals the baseline DRIFT files±N bytes±N followed by was / now hashes hash differs; the file and byte deltas are reported NO BASELINE (build first) no stored manifest; counted as drift Exit code Meaning 0 every selected dataset matched (all datasets verified) 3 at least one dataset drifted or had no baseline (N dataset(s) drifted or lack a baseline)

Any other non-zero code is an uncaught error (for example an unreadable registry). The audit says that a dataset changed and by how many files and bytes. To find which files changed, diff the old and new <slug>.files.tsv.

docs.title: Where manifests are computed
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  T1[panatlas-refresh.timer<br/>hourly] --> B[dataset_manifest.py build<br/>--update-registry]
  B --> CR[cluster registry copy<br/>manifest fields rewritten]
  CR --> RP[build_dataset_reports.py<br/>manager payloads stamped with manifest_hash]
  T2[panatlas-ct-rewalk.timer<br/>weekly, Sunday 03:00] --> S[ct_native_manifest.sbatch<br/>compute node]
  S --> PW[dataset_manifest_parallel.py<br/>corpus + one subset]
  PW --> DS[derive_source_manifests.py<br/>31 partitions]
  DS --> FW[fullwalk/*.files.tsv, *.manifest.json]
  FW -. inventory files become partition locations .-> B
  CR -. copied at fold time .-> F[fold_manifests.py] --> RR[web/datasets.json + web/manifests/]

Hourly, on the cluster. web/mesh/deploy/panatlas-refresh.timer (15 minutes after boot, then every hour) runs panatlas-refresh.service: dataset_manifest.py build --registry datasets.json --root <estate root> --out cresco/manifests --update-registry against the cluster copy of the registry, then build_dataset_reports.py for the hosted entries. The managers therefore report the hash computed in the last hour.

The hourly job rebuilds; it does not audit

The refresh runs build --update-registry, which overwrites each entry's stored manifest with the new one. A changed dataset gets a new hash and nothing fails. No script or timer in the repository calls dataset_manifest.py audit. Drift is visible only by comparing hashes over time (for example the repository copy in web/manifests/ against the cluster's current value, or a manager's reported hash against an earlier report). If you need a gate, run audit against a pinned baseline directory with --manifests and act on exit code 3.

Registry rewrites race

--update-registry rewrites the whole cluster registry file. An edit to that file made while the hourly build runs is lost when the build finishes. This happened in practice on 2026-09-12 (the project waited out the timer before editing). Stop the timer or edit between runs.

On registration or acquisition, folded into the repository. The repository's web/datasets.json is not updated by the hourly job. Manifests reach it when an acquisition finishes and a fold script copies them in:

Script Input What it writes web/fold_manifests.py <dir> [summary-file] [summary-path] a directory with a completion summary and <slug>.manifest.json files for every matching entry in web/datasets.json and every web/datasets_*.json: manifest (the six summary fields), status: active if missing_locations is empty, acquisition.status: complete, acquisition.finished, acquisition.summary; copies the summary into web/manifests/ web/fold_tcga_manifests.py TCGA completion summary the same, for web/datasets.json and web/datasets_tcga.json web/fold_renal_manifests.py renal completion summary the same, but writes acquisition.completion_summary instead of acquisition.summary, and acquisition.status: incomplete when locations are missing

Checks the fold scripts make before writing: the manifest's urn equals the entry's (assertion); the manifest's hash (and, for the TCGA and renal folds, its file_count) equals the completion summary's (otherwise the fold stops); a whole-download summary with no per-dataset list is accepted only when it reports zero missing, partial and extra files (otherwise nothing is folded). web/test_fold_manifests.py tests the per-dataset form, the whole-download form and the refusal of an incomplete download (python3 -m unittest test_fold_manifests -v).

At HEAD, every one of the 127 registry manifest hashes and 32 manifest_full_walk hashes equals its copy in web/manifests/ (159 comparisons, 0 mismatches). One manifest_full_walk (a neuropathology tile store) has no repository copy. Two files in web/manifests/ (heartlens-ct.manifest.json, nlst-ct.manifest.json) belong to retired slugs and are not referenced by the registry. The summaries were computed between 2026-07-31 and 2026-10-15: the repository holds the value at fold time, not the current hourly value.

docs.title: Partitioned and inventory-file manifests
docs.text: A single-threaded walk is fine for most datasets (CT-RATE: 52,602 files in 10.35 s, measured 2026-09-12). It fails for very large trees. The CT native corpus (296,429 Zarr cases; the parallel walker's docstring estimated "tens of millions" of chunk files, the walk counted 6,883,489) did not finish a login-node walk in 25 minutes, and a 1,387,222-file neuropathology tile store took about 11 minutes, too long to repeat every hour. Three tools handle this.

docs.title: The parallel walker
docs.text:
web/dataset_manifest_parallel.py produces the same canonical inventory and hash as dataset_manifest.py build for the same locations, using a process pool:

  1. For each location, scan directories down to --shard-depth (default 3). Files above that depth are stat'ed in the main process; each directory at that depth becomes a pool task.
  2. --workers processes (default 32) walk the shard directories with os.scandir, never following symbolic links, and return (path, size, int(mtime)).
  3. Paths are made relative to --root, sorted, and hashed in a stream while <slug>.files.tsv is written.
  4. <slug>.manifest.json gets the six summary fields.

Flags: --slug, --urn, --root, --location (repeatable), --out, --workers, --shard-depth, --chunksize (default 64). It prints an EFFECTIVE line with every setting, progress every 5,000 shards, and DONE at the end.

Equivalence was tested on one partition: the cases/cads directory gave the same 80 files, inventory and hash from both tools (recorded 2026-09-17).

Symbolic links make the two walkers disagree

dataset_manifest.py lists a symbolic link to a file as a file and records the target's size and mtime (os.walk plus os.stat). dataset_manifest_parallel.py skips symbolic links entirely (is_file(follow_symlinks=False)). The "byte-for-byte compatible" claim in its docstring holds only for trees without file symlinks. Check for symlinks before mixing the two on one dataset.

docs.title: Weekly full walk and partition derivation
docs.text:
web/mesh/deploy/panatlas-ct-rewalk.timer (Sunday 03:00, persistent) submits web/mesh/deploy/ct_native_manifest.sbatch to a compute node (96 cores, 200 GB, 8-hour limit). It runs:

Step Command Fails with exit 1 parallel walk of the whole corpus, slug heartlens-ct3d-native 2 2 parallel walk of one subset entry over the corpus plus that subset's embedding directory 3 3 derive_source_manifests.py over both inventories 4

and prints CT_MANIFEST_OK on success. Outputs go to <cluster project storage>/panatlas/cresco/manifests/fullwalk/.

web/derive_source_manifests.py uses the corpus layout …/heartlens_ct3d_native/cases/<source>/<case>.zarr/…. Every registered CT sub-collection is exactly one cases/<source> directory, so its manifest is the subset of inventory lines under that prefix, hashed the same way, with no second walk. The slug is ct- + the source name with _ replaced by -. One subset also owns an embedding directory, whose lines are merged in and re-sorted. The script prints unmatched sources (directories with no registry entry) and a reconciliation: shallow files + partition files must equal the inventory total.

Measured on 2026-09-17 (job 220015, 96 workers, 26 minutes):

Measure Value Corpus full walk 6,883,489 files · 25,938,581,260,036 B (25.94 TB) Partitions derived 31 registered ct-* entries Reconciliation 1,838 shallow files + 6,881,651 partition files = 6,883,489 Proof of equivalence the derived ct-cads hash equals a direct walk's hash Not registered cases/ctrate (1,711,569 files), the ingested CT-RATE subset already counted under ct-rate

docs.title: What the hourly manifest covers for these entries
docs.text:
For the 31 partitions and the corpus entry, the registry locations point at the inventory file (panatlas/cresco/manifests/fullwalk/<slug>.files.tsv), not at the data. The hourly manifest of such an entry therefore has file_count: 1 (all 31 partitions at HEAD) and hashes the inventory file's path, size and mtime. The full manifest of the data is kept in manifest_full_walk, and the partition directory in partition_path.

The neuropathology tile store uses the same idea differently: its hourly manifest covers six tile-index CSV files (6 files, 353,437,544 B), which enumerate every tile; the store itself (1,387,222 files, 93.3 GB) was walked once on 2026-09-12 and is kept as manifest_full_walk, with no scheduled re-walk.

What an inventory-file audit can and cannot detect

It detects that the weekly re-walk produced a different inventory (the inventory file changed). It does not detect a change to the data between re-walks, and for the neuropathology store it does not detect a change at all unless the index CSVs change. The audit_scope field on each entry states this.

docs.title: Who consumes the manifest
docs.text:
Consumer Uses web/build_dataset_reports.py stamps the manager's dataset node with manifest_hash and file_count; writes <slug>.manifest.json (the registry summary, or {}) beside the report; sets the plugin's panatlas_graph_version to the hash, or unversioned web/mesh/mesh_daemon.py shows the first 19 characters of each reported hash on the mesh view web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/assets/app.js the "audited" badge and the manifest panel on each dataset card (files, bytes, hash, computed_at date, missing locations); "not audited" when there is no hash web/rdf/build_rdf.py emits manifest_hash, file_count, total_bytes as dataset properties (see RDF vocabulary)

Hub-side verification is designed, not built

PLAN-datasets.md §2 and DATASET-MANAGERS.md say the hub's merge_reports.py verifies each reported manifest_hash against web/datasets.json and quarantines a mismatch. At HEAD, web/federation/merge_reports.py reads an agent registry for tier and status gating only; it does not open web/datasets.json and does not compare hashes. The stamp is carried end to end; the comparison is not made. See Federation contract and Dataset managers.

docs.title: Honest limits
docs.text:
• Content is not hashed. Size and whole-second mtime are the per-file signature. Two files with the same path, size and mtime but different bytes produce the same hash. The manifest proves an inventory, not content, and cannot show that a file in one store is byte-identical to a file in another.
  • Metadata-only changes count as drift. touch, or a copy that does not preserve mtimes, changes the hash with no change to content. Copy with rsync -a or cp -p to keep a hash.
  • The hash depends on the root. relpath is relative to the estate root. Moving the whole estate keeps the hash only if the relative paths are unchanged; moving a dataset within the estate changes it.
  • Empty directories are invisible. Only files are listed.
  • Unreadable files are dropped silently. A file whose stat fails is skipped with no message; a permissions change can shrink the inventory.
  • Overlapping locations double-count. If one location contains another, files under both appear twice.
  • Missing locations do not fail the build. They are listed in missing_locations; the fold scripts keep such an entry out of active, but the hourly build does not.
  • Symbolic links differ between the two walkers (above).
  • The hash is unkeyed. Anyone who knows a dataset's file list can confirm it. See the storage rule on Identifiers.

docs.title: Upgrade path
docs.text:
PLAN-datasets.md §2 names the planned upgrade: keep size and mtime as the cheap signature for bulk files, and add sha256 for small or critical files (labels, splits, index CSVs, manifests of record), so that the audit can prove content where it matters. This is designed, not built: neither walker reads file content.

Content is verified today at a different point, during acquisition, by each fetcher against the publisher's own checksums, and recorded in the acquisition record rather than the manifest (see Acquisition and licence). Examples: every OpenH-RF file against its Hugging Face tree hash (sha256 for LFS files, git blob sha1 otherwise); CPTAC packages by md5sum -c against the packages' own sums; the UMLS release by zip CRC and the release's own row counts. A content column in <slug>.files.tsv for selected files would join the two.

Related pages: Identifiers, Dataset registry, Acquisition and licence, Dataset managers.

docs.title: Models and curriculum
docs.text: This page documents how panAtlas describes models and how they were trained: the artifact-type vocabulary that types training and evaluation data on the same axis, the model records, the per-modality embedding-model registry, the training-curriculum record, and the register of training-provenance gaps. Evaluation results are on Evaluation records. Counts were computed with python3 from the files at repo HEAD 57505c6 on 2026-11-10.

docs.title: Artifact types
docs.text: An artifact type says what kind of record a training or evaluation document is (a QA pair, a discharge summary, a reasoning trace, a whole-slide image). It is the second axis next to the topic (what the record is about, a concept node). Both axes apply to training sources and to benchmarks, so training exposure and evaluation coverage can be compared cell by cell. The layer was added 2026-08-08 (docs/artifact-types-and-model-curriculum.md).

Type count and SFT map size differ from the layer document

docs/artifact-types-and-model-curriculum.md says 33 types and 16 SFT type values. The file has 35 types (the adversarial review added atype-text-transformation and atype-cloze-continuation) and 19 sft_type_map keys.

docs.title: Artifact-type nodes and their grounding
docs.text:
build_artifact_types.py writes one artifact-type node per type (concept_class: artifact-type). Every node carries canonical_id, grounding, wiki_title, grounding_match, grounding_reason and grounding_judge; some carry wp_url, related_wikipedia, related_mesh, related_mesh_name, grounding_note, mesh_dui, mesh_name, mesh_url.

The 2026-08-08 pass grounded 24 types to a MeSH descriptor. A later concept-identity check (grounding_judge: "gemma-4-31B concept-identity judge (2026-08-09)") asked whether the public concept is the same thing as the record type, and recorded the answer in grounding_match (yes 17, no 17, partial 1) with a grounding_reason. In the served graph:

grounding Nodes canonical_id internal-vocabulary 17 panatlas:atype-<slug>; the near public concept is kept as related_wikipedia / related_mesh wikipedia 16 wikipedia:<title> mesh+wikipedia 2 mesh:D063886 (discharge summary), mesh:D008499 (diagnostic report)

So the vocabulary file lists 24 MeSH descriptors, but only two types use one as identity; the others keep it as related_mesh.

docs.title: Where artifact types attach
docs.text:
Structure Count at HEAD dataset has_artifact_type → artifact-type 684 llm-benchmark has_artifact_type → artifact-type 113 benchmark has_artifact_type → artifact-type 19 llm-benchmark nodes with artifact_type_via (override or facet:<task_format>) 96

Measured rollups (tokens per type and topic per pretraining corpus, records per type per SFT mix) are written to web/pipeline/corpus_type_profile.json. Types are not mutually exclusive, so shares can sum past 100 %.

Record-level typing (added 2026-08-08, second pass) types documents individually rather than per source. Pretraining coverage is stamped honestly (V4 55.89 % of manifest documents, V5 43.35 %); uncovered sources are excluded, not guessed. Every SFT record of the V5 (736,990) and V4 (825,504) mixes is typed by deterministic rules in a record-typing script under web/pipeline/record_level/. Results land on corpus and mix nodes as record_level_type_topic, record_level_type_register, record_level_coverage, record_level_records, record_level_method, record_level_judge_audit, and on SFT source nodes as record_topics, record_registers, record_register_atypes, record_topic_concepts.

The register (tone) of a record is a third small vocabulary: five register nodes written by build_existing_meta.py (Academic writing, Technical writing, Medical writing, Plain language, Colloquialism), each grounded to a Wikipedia article, with 162 dataset has_register → register edges.

docs.title: Embedding-model registry: web/models.json
docs.text:
models.json is the per-modality registry of embedding models that place new items in the connectivity graph (Knowledge layers). Its rule: an embedding is comparable only within one (modality, model, version) space; cross-modality relation goes through shared canonical_id, never through embedding arithmetic.

Modality Registered model Status text text-bioclinical-modernbert-large, version v3w-2026.07: stock BioClinical-ModernBERT-large weights (SHA-256 verified 2026-08-08 to equal the published weights; not fine-tuned in-house), 1024-d, masked mean pool, max_length 1024, L2, cosine, raw cutoff 0.25 with a whitened cutoff in the anchor artifact active imaging imaging-rad-dino-ct, version raddino: stock RAD-DINO (768-d) Embeddings are a retrieval asset; concept anchors are held (image embeddings are not linked directly to concept nodes) genomics none "no registered embedder yet" structured none "no registered embedder yet"

Entry fields: id, family, modality, role, applies_to, dim, version, normalize, similarity, cutoff, anchors, status, provenance; text adds pooling, max_length, dtype, whitening, cutoff_note, location, centroids (artifact, n_cells 4,096, dim 1,024), hf, training_disclosed, license; imaging adds model_location, note, embeddings.

The vault page concept-panatlas-text-embedding-space-v3w records that @v3w tags the embedding space, not the weights: v3 is the third concept-embedding pipeline (embed_concepts_v3.py), w the per-dimension whitening (x − mu) / sd stored with the 201 concept anchors.

models.json also holds predictors (58 tabular and forecasting model records), documented on Evaluation records.

Imaging model differs from LAYERS.md

LAYERS.md says imaging is embedded "by the LeJEPA-3D CT encoder". The registry's only imaging entry is stock RAD-DINO, and its anchors are held.

docs.title: The curriculum record: panatlas-model-curriculum/1
docs.text: web/pipeline/model_curriculum.json records, for any model, the ordered training stages that produced it. Each stage answers five questions: (a) what data, (b) when, (c) on what system, (d) with what configuration, (e) from what codebase. The record is model-agnostic: an external model that does not disclose its curriculum reports curriculum_disclosed: false with no stages, through the same fields.

docs.text: Key Type Content _schema string panatlas-model-curriculum/1 note string Purpose and sourcing: in-house facts come from the vault's verified audits models list One record per model (6 at HEAD)

Host-specific values

system.cluster, system.nodelist, codebase.path, codebase.repo and some provenance tags hold host names, cluster paths and account names. They are needed to resolve a fact against the vault, and this documentation does not reproduce them. The public API does not return paths, hosts or job numbers (docs/public-api.md).

training-stage nodes (14, layer: process) carry id, label (stage name), kind, layer, stage_type, order, model, data (without inline_datasets), when, system, config, codebase, results, provenance and source. The script also stamps model nodes with curriculum_disclosed, leaderboard_eligible and withheld_reason (when set), curriculum_verified, curriculum_stages, curriculum_summary, and curriculum_note for models without stages. Any model node still lacking curriculum_disclosed when the script runs gets false and the note "no published stage-level curriculum (data-by-stage, schedule, system, config, codebase)". Edge ids are content-hashed, so reruns add no edges.

Not every model node carries curriculum_disclosed

The layer document and the vault say every model node carries curriculum_disclosed. At HEAD 44 of 90 do (8 true, 36 false). The 46 predictor models were added by link_predictors.py after build_curriculum.py last ran and have no value. The stale stats.curriculum block reports 1 undisclosed model.

docs.title: Verification gate
docs.text: pipeline/check_curriculum_vault.py checks that every hard fact in the curriculum (each scheduler job id other than n/a, each config file path, each codebase repository other than a container) appears in at least one page of the knowledge vault, and exits 1 on any miss. It runs in build_all.sh. The vault records 39/39 facts found on 2026-08-08 and 61/61 after the KOS-V6 record was added on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: The training-provenance gap register
docs.text:
docs/curriculum-gap-register.md lists every blank that prevents a complete "look at the model, see exactly how it was trained" record, compiled 2026-08-08 from a sweep of the vault and the curriculum layer. Blanks are tracked with the same rigour as facts.

Format:

  • Legend. Each gap names the missing curriculum field by its letter: (a) data, (b) when/jobs, (c) system, (d) config, (e) codebase.
  • Sections. CRITICAL (zero or deleted records), HIGH (partial records), KNOWN DEFECTS (measured caveats, not blanks), RESOLVED (kept so nobody reopens them), and "Curriculum entries to ADD once facts land".
  • Table columns (CRITICAL and HIGH): #, Artifact, Missing (the field letters and what is missing), Best lead (where the fact can be recovered). A resolved row is struck through and annotated RESOLVED with the date and the evidence.
  • Closing a gap. The fact is filed in the vault; check_curriculum_vault.py then picks it up.

At HEAD the register has five CRITICAL rows (one resolved: the BioClinical-ModernBERT weights were shown to be the stock published weights), five HIGH rows, four known defects (for example "V4 pretrain: 39.62% exact-duplicate text"; "V6 SFT/RL mix: contamination unchecked"), four resolved items, and one completed addition (the KOS-V6 base curriculum, 2026-10-14).

docs.title: RDF vocabulary and SPARQL stores
docs.text:
RDF is panAtlas's canonical graph form (owner decision 2026-09-26, recorded in GRAPH_STANDARDS.md). This page documents how the served property graph becomes RDF: the namespaces, classes and predicates, the named graph, the mapping rules, and the SPARQL stores that serve panAtlas together with mirrored external graphs. Code: web/rdf/build_rdf.py (export), web/rdf/qlever_build.py, qlever_serve.py, qlever_fold.py, qlever_export.py, nt_canon.py, sparql_client.py (stores), and web/acquisition/okn/ (mirrors).

Item Status Export of the served graph to N-Quads Built (build_rdf.py) SPARQL store panatlas-okn (panAtlas + NSF OKN mirrors) Built and served inside the HPC cluster (vault, 2026-10-16) SPARQL store wikidata Built, held back in verification (vault, 2026-10-16) SPARQL store panatlas-restricted (licensed vocabularies, per-project access) Designed only (PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md) Public SPARQL endpoint None. The stores answer only inside the cluster network

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Prefix IRI Use pa: https://panatlas.net/ontology# panAtlas classes and properties (nodes) https://panatlas.net/id/{id} One IRI per graph node; {id} is the node id, percent-encoded with no safe characters (statements) https://panatlas.net/id/edge%2F{edge id} Reified edges; the / after edge is percent-encoded because the whole string goes through the same encoder (graph) https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas The named graph panAtlas curates (graph) https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/{shortname} A mirrored NSF OKN graph (graph) http://www.wikidata.org/ The Wikidata mirror (source of record: Wikimedia) rdf: http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns# rdf:type, reification, rdf:JSON literals rdfs: http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema# rdfs:label, rdfs:Class, rdfs:subPropertyOf skos: http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core# skos:Concept, skos:prefLabel, skos:exactMatch, skos:broader, skos:related dct: http://purl.org/dc/terms/ dct:description, dct:identifier, dct:title, dct:license, dct:publisher dcat: http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat# dcat:Dataset foaf: http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/ foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf (Wikipedia pages) void: http://rdfs.org/ns/void# Named-graph descriptions prov: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# prov:Entity, prov:generatedAtTime pav: http://purl.org/pav/ pav:version (upstream version of a mirrored graph) xsd: http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema# Literal datatypes

Code IRIs are built from the rdf_iri_stem of each system in web/codesystems.json (see Controlled vocabularies):

Node field Stem Predicate mesh_dui http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/ skos:exactMatch snomed http://snomed.info/id/ skos:exactMatch loinc http://loinc.org/rdf/ skos:exactMatch rxnorm http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/RXNORM/ skos:exactMatch cui the UMLS identifier stem registered in codesystems.json skos:exactMatch icd11 http://id.who.int/icd/entity/ skos:exactMatch go http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_ (the GO: prefix is stripped) skos:exactMatch icd10cm none registered literal pa:icd10cmCode wiki_title https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf wp_url (the URL itself) foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf mesh_url (the URL itself) pa:meshUrl

The MeSH stem is http, not https, because NLM mints http IRIs and only redirects https (vault project-panatlas, 2026-09-26). Site browser links in mesh_url stay https.

docs.title: Mapping rules (build_rdf.py)
docs.text: Inputs: the served graph (web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/graph.json), the dataset registry (web/datasets.json) and web/codesystems.json. Optional: --okn-agents <dir> with each mirror agent's state.json, sor.json and provenance.json. Output: rdf/panatlas.nq and rdf/panatlas.stats.json. Every quad is in the named graph https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas and is written once; repeats (for example wp_url and wiki_title naming the same page) are counted as duplicates_suppressed.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
Graph content RDF Every node <id> rdf:type pa:{Kind}, where {Kind} is the kind in upper camel case (llm-benchmark → pa:LlmBenchmark, fhir → pa:Fhir) Concept-like kinds: concept, disease, specialty, food, food-category, domain, capability, capability-group, eval-domain, gen-category, artifact-type, testing-type, register, training-stage, group, root, atlas-root Also rdf:type skos:Concept; label also as skos:prefLabel dataset Also rdf:type dcat:Dataset benchmark, llm-benchmark Also rdf:type dcat:Dataset and rdf:type pa:Benchmark model rdf:type pa:Model label rdfs:label desc dct:description Codes and links The table above Code-system nodes (onto-*) iri_stem, rdf_iri_basis and fhir_system are taken from codesystems.json, not from the graph, because the graph copy may predate an edit Any other field pa:{camelCase(field)}; a list of scalars repeats the predicate once per value

Literal typing: booleans are xsd:boolean, integers xsd:integer, floats xsd:double; objects and lists of objects are serialised as sorted JSON with datatype rdf:JSON; strings are plain literals. Empty values (null, "", [], {}) are skipped, as are id, kind and label (already expressed).

Kinds typed as skos:Concept

training-stage, capability, testing-type and register nodes are typed skos:Concept because they are in the script's CONCEPT_KINDS. model, dataset, fhir, authority, codebase, system, guideline, kg, eval-suite, modality, measurement and method nodes are not. The last three are MeSH-grounded concepts whose kind is not in the list.

docs.title: Edges
docs.text:
Every edge whose two ends exist becomes <from> pa:{camelCase(rel)} <to>. An edge with attributes is also reified:

<https://panatlas.net/id/edge%2Fe-ca547f136f6d8d89b80f>
    a rdf:Statement ;
    rdf:subject   <https://panatlas.net/id/mesh-D000089323> ;
    rdf:predicate pa:partOf ;
    rdf:object    <https://panatlas.net/id/concept-geriatrics> ;
    pa:src        "mesh_tree" .

The 36 relation predicates, with the number of triples at HEAD: pa:binds 15, pa:builtWith 14, pa:classifiedAs 1,756, pa:covers 3,607, pa:coversTopic 2,209, pa:defines 1, pa:derivedFrom 3, pa:evaluatedBy 2, pa:evaluatedOn 8, pa:executedOn 14, pa:follows 9, pa:groundedIn 239, pa:grounds 13, pa:groups 35, pa:hasArtifactType 816, pa:hasRegister 162, pa:hasResource 18, pa:hasTrainingStage 14, pa:hasType 21, pa:inCollection 83, pa:inDomain 97, pa:instantiates 36, pa:isType 106, pa:measuredOn 104, pa:partOf 5,430, pa:prereq 6, pa:related 44, pa:resolvesTo 251, pa:scored 85, pa:sftTrainedOn 2, pa:stageTrainedOn 45, pa:structuredAs 1,592, pa:testSetOf 14, pa:tests 247, pa:trainedOn 20, pa:uses 1. Their meaning is on Graph schema.

The only alignment axioms asserted are:

pa:partOf  rdfs:subPropertyOf skos:broader .
pa:related rdfs:subPropertyOf skos:related .

Nothing else is asserted about the vocabulary. In particular there is no skos:narrower, no domain or range, and no class hierarchy.

docs.title: Dataset registry
docs.text:
Each entry of datasets.json is written to <https://panatlas.net/id/dataset-{slug}>:

Registry field RDF (entry) rdf:type dcat:Dataset urn dct:identifier name dct:title modality[] pa:modality license dct:license <IRI> when it is a URL, else pa:licenseStatement license_status, license_scope, status, role, host, access, used_in_training pa:licenseStatus, pa:licenseScope, pa:status, pa:role, pa:host, pa:access, pa:usedInTraining manifest.manifest_hash, manifest.file_count, manifest.total_bytes pa:manifestHash, pa:fileCount, pa:totalBytes maintained_externally pa:maintainedExternally true source_of_record.graph pa:sourceOfRecord <external graph IRI>, plus pa:agent, pa:upstreamVersion, pa:heldVersion, pa:upstreamLastUpdatedOn, pa:registryCommit (no external source of record) pa:sourceOfRecord <https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas>

Registry fields are documented on Dataset registry and Manifests.

docs.title: Named-graph descriptions
docs.text:
With --okn-agents, each mirrored graph is described (not copied) inside the panAtlas graph:

Triple Source <graph> rdf:type void:Dataset, prov:Entity always <graph> pa:mirroredBy <…/id/dataset-okn-{sn}> always <graph> pa:agent "okn-agent:{sn}" sor.json <graph> pav:version upstream version, provenance.json <graph> pa:heldVersion held version, state.json <graph> prov:generatedAtTime fetch time, state.json <graph> void:triples endpoint count, state.json <graph> void:sparqlEndpoint upstream endpoint, provenance.json <graph> dct:license, dct:publisher provenance.json <graph> pa:authoritativeNamespace <ns> (repeated) sor.json <graph> pa:authoritativeDeclared whether the publisher declared its namespaces or panAtlas inferred them

The panAtlas graph describes itself as void:Dataset with dct:title "panAtlas (source of record: panAtlas)" and prov:generatedAtTime (the export time).

Every pa: class used is declared rdf:type rdfs:Class with an rdfs:label, and every pa: property rdf:type rdf:Property with an rdfs:label.

docs.title: panatlas-okn
docs.text:
A read-only SPARQL 1.1 endpoint (QLever) holding panAtlas's own graph and every deployed NSF Open Knowledge Network graph that has been proven exact, each in the named graph of its source of record.

Fact Value Source Build panatlas-okn-20261003T0039 web/rdf/README.md; vault reference-panatlas-sparql-endpoint Named graphs 44: panAtlas plus 43 OKN graphs same Triples 6,994,341,217 same; re-checked 2026-10-16 Served 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-08 (Slurm job 226412), and since 2026-10-16 08:06 (job 237423) same Where A CPU-only Slurm job on a cluster compute node; reachable only inside the cluster network same Every graph Passed the exact round trip before the store went live (2026-10-03 07:43) vault

The host and port change whenever a new build is switched live, so clients read them from the endpoint record stores/<name>.endpoint (host, port, url, job, started) under the store directory in <cluster project storage>/panatlas/qlever/. Queries run inside a Slurm job, never on a login node. A served query is stopped after one hour; whole-store scans take minutes.

Agents query through the query_knowledge_graph tool of the Astral agent, which runs sparql_client.py over a forced-command key: parameters query, store (panatlas-okn or wikidata), describe=true (the named graphs with versions, sizes and proofs) and max_rows (at most 1,000); requests are base64 JSON ({"action": "describe", "store": …} or {"query": …, "store": …, "max_rows": …}); SPARQL Update is refused; timeout 120 s.

docs.title: wikidata
docs.text: A separate store from the Wikidata agent's md5-verified Wikimedia dump, in the named graph http://www.wikidata.org/. 21,350,107,674 triples, indexed 2026-10-02. It is held back: its first smoke test assumed English labels, but Wikidata stores a name shared by every language once under the language code mul (vault defect-wikidata-store-test-assumed-english-label). A verification rerun was submitted 2026-10-16 (job 237432). For English labels use FILTER(LANG(?l) IN ('en', 'mul')) and prefer en. The two stores are joined at query time with SERVICE.

docs.title: panatlas-restricted (designed)
docs.text: PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md designs a third QLever store for licensed vocabularies, never merged into panatlas-okn, with one named graph per source restriction level under https://panatlas.net/graph/restricted/…, panAtlas-derived relations in a separate derived graph, and per-user, per-project entitlements enforced in sparql_client.py (default deny, every call audited). Licensed content is internal and entitlement-gated; none of it enters the public graph or this documentation. At HEAD only acquisition (phase P1) has passed; the store is not built.

docs.title: Mirrors: one agent per graph
docs.text:
Each OKN graph has its own agent (okn-agent:{shortname}, web/acquisition/okn/okn_agent.py) with its own state, provenance, source-of-record file, lock and update job. A six-hourly tick snapshots the OKN registry and VoID records (pav:version, lastUpdatedOn, void:triples per graph) and submits an independent sync job for each changed graph. Held copies live as raw/<sn>/<version>/part_*.nt with DONE and PROOF.json, and raw/<sn>/current points at the adopted version. A sync proves its new version and falls back to the previous one if any proof fails. Mirrored graphs are read-only and replaced wholesale; panAtlas never edits an externally maintained node or edge, it only links to it from its own graph.

The source-of-record rule for nodes: a node IRI is maintained by whichever source's authoritative namespace covers it, by longest prefix (sor_index.json). Where a graph declares no namespaces, its own base IRI is taken as authoritative and marked inferred. An IRI no source claims belongs to its external authority (OBO, Wikidata, identifiers.org, NCBI).

docs.title: Proof levels (okn_prove.py, PROOF.json)
docs.text:
Level Check fingerprint sha256 of the sorted distinct triples; per-predicate counts; blank-node count upstream Per-predicate counts equal the endpoint's; 20 random slices byte-identical at their offsets; 2,000 random triples byte-identical among the endpoint's objects for their subject and predicate reextract A second full extraction at page size 999,983 hashes identically store The triples exported back out of the local store equal the source (qlever_build.py)

A graph is admitted to a store build only if its extraction verified and PROOF.json shows fingerprint, upstream and reextract ok.

docs.title: The store round trip
docs.text:
A store is a query view, proven before it is served. qlever_build.py builds into stores/<name>-<stamp>/, then requires: every graph's triple count equals its verified count; no graph appears that was not admitted; the panAtlas MeSH joins hold; and the exact round trip passes. Only then does stores/<name> switch to the new build. A failed build writes stores/<name>.last_failure and is not resubmitted until fixed and re-verified.

The round trip exports every graph back out of the store and requires that the sorted distinct non-blank triples of canon(export) hash identically to canon(fold(source)), that blank-node triple counts are equal (the store assigns its own labels), and that COUNT(*) equals the source's distinct stored values. nt_canon.py writes one spelling per RDF term; qlever_fold.py applies QLever's literal folding to the source. QLever cannot keep literals verbatim and has no setting to stop it (vault reference-qlever-literal-folding):

Rule Effect integer xsd:integer becomes xsd:int (60-bit range) decimal / double Stored as a double minus its 4 lowest mantissa bits; printed %.1f or %.13g as xsd:decimal (lossy past 13 significant digits) point WKT POINT quantized to a 30-bit grid per coordinate, printed %f (sub-metre loss) dateTime A year beyond 4 digits loses its Z unparseable A folded-type literal QLever cannot parse loses its datatype spelling \uXXXX escapes, ^^xsd:string, language-tag case (same RDF term)

Exact recreation therefore always comes from the verified raw files, never from a store.

docs.title: Joins the store enables
docs.text:
Measured in the store and recorded in the vault (project-panatlas, 2026-09-26):

  • 3,373 of 3,377 panAtlas MeSH IRIs exist in NLM's MeSH RDF (OKN graph biobricks-mesh).
  • 3,310 panAtlas concepts reach 3,313 Wikidata entities through the OKN identifier-mappings graph.
  • 137 MeSH IRIs join the OKN graph spoke-okn only through their https variant.
  • panAtlas concepts carry no Wikidata identifiers of their own.

Example (from web/rdf/README.md, run against the live store 2026-10-08, 1.2 s):

PREFIX skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?c ?m ?label WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas>              { ?c skos:exactMatch ?m }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/biobricks-mesh>     { ?m rdfs:label ?label } } LIMIT 3
# -> panatlas:fa-dis-C531609  mesh:C531609  "Diffuse alopecia"@en

PREFIX skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#>
SELECT ?c ?w WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas>                 { ?c skos:exactMatch ?m }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/identifier-mappings>   { ?w skos:exactMatch ?m } } LIMIT 3
# -> panatlas:fa-dis-C531609  wd:Q9394945   (7.2 s)

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Agent (Cresco). A leaf node of the Cresco mesh: a JVM running the OSGi host and plugins, attached as a client to its region's broker. Messages address it as region_agent; its identity is its certificate subject (CN=<agent>, OU=<region>, O=<tenant>). See Cresco's glossary.

Agent (panAtlas). Anything that contributes to the atlas under its own identity: a participating Cresco node, a dataset manager, or a knowledge-graph agent that mirrors one external graph.

Agent profile. The panAtlas overlay on a Cresco identity: display name, owner, institution, purpose, tier and status, with a private contact block. See Wire contract.

Anchors. One vector per grounded concept in one model's embedding space, used to attach new embeddings to concepts. Only valid for that exact model@version.

Attach. Relating a new embedding to concepts by cosine similarity to the anchors, at or above the model's cutoff. It produces classified_as connectivity edges and never creates new identities.

Canonical identifier (canonical_id). An ontology identifier such as mesh:D051436. The join key of federation.

Connectivity. Relationships (edges), recorded as attributed claims. Contrast with substrate.

content_hash. SHA-256 over a report's nodes and edges, used for change detection. Not comparable across producers; see Participating agents.

Cresco. The hierarchical, secure, multi-tenant distributed agent mesh (global → region → agent) that panAtlas runs on. Secure by default since its 1.3 hardening. Documentation.

Curriculum. A model's ordered training stages, each answering: what data, when, which system, which configuration, which codebase. See Models and curriculum.

Dataset manager. The cresco-panatlas plugin instance responsible for one dataset, running on the agent at the dataset's site.

doc_uid. blake2b(raw_text, 16 bytes): the unkeyed content identity of a document.

Domain. A field of knowledge the atlas maps, such as medicine, food and nutrition, or general knowledge. panAtlas covers every domain; medicine is where its holdings run deepest today. In the served graph the top-level domains are domain nodes under atlas-root. Not the same as an evaluation domain (eval-domain), which classifies benchmarks. See Purpose and principles.

Federation status. visible (merged and shown) or pending (held for a curator), set by the reporting agent's tier.

GaiaKeep. A global file system built for agents, running on the same Cresco mesh: versioned datasets, kept durable and streamed wherever they are needed. The intended durable backend for panAtlas. Documentation; see Storage on GaiaKeep.

Global controller. The root of the panAtlas Cresco region, where inventories roll up and through which the hub's calls to managers are routed. In panAtlas's configuration the hub's client connects to the web host agent's wsapi, not to the global's.

Grounding. Tying a node to a canonical vocabulary identifier. Ungrounded nodes stay private to their agent.

Hub. The panatlas.net side of federation: it pulls reports, merges permitted contributions and serves the graph.

Join secret. Cresco's per-tier discovery secret (discovery_secret_agent, _region, _global) that admits a node to the mesh in the standard security profile; the production profile uses the operator's PKI instead. See Discovery.

manifest_hash. SHA-256 over a dataset's canonical sorted inventory of (relpath, size, mtime). It detects moves, growth and edits. It does not hash content.

Mesh view. The site's live view of Cresco nodes, links and the datasets each node hosts, drawn from mesh.json.

Model space. One registered (modality, model, version). Embeddings compare only within one space.

MsgEvent. Cresco's control-plane message. Under Cresco 1.3's secure defaults each one is authenticated end to end by its origin and bound to its recipient. Manager calls (getgraphmanifest, getgraphinventory) are MsgEvent EXEC messages. See MsgEvent.

pycrescolib. Cresco's Python client library, used by the hub to list, deploy and call managers.

Source of record. The graph that maintains a node or triple. panAtlas curates only what it is the source of record for.

Status (agent). pending, active, suspended or revoked. Only active agents contribute.

Structure-only. The federation rule that payloads carry identifiers, counts, edges, model stamps and hashes, never content. Enforced by rejecting text, body, raw, content, document, excerpt and abstract at any depth.

Substrate. Entity identity, keyed by canonical identifier. It merges by identity. Contrast with connectivity.

Tier. trusted (merged visibly on arrival) or provisional (held as pending claims).

URN. A dataset's global identifier, panatlas:dataset:<slug>.

docs.title: Repository map
docs.text:
A map of the panAtlas repository at commit 57505c6. The repository has three directories (atlas/, docs/, web/) and a set of design and operations documents at the root. Almost all code is under web/. Paths are relative to the repository root.

The Cresco plugin (cresco-panatlas) and the operator kit for connecting a site (agent-deployment) are separate repositories; see Distributed.

docs.title: Data acquisition
docs.text: Every dataset panAtlas holds or mirrors arrives through an acquisition tool in web/acquisition/<source>/. The scripts there are mirrors of what runs on the HPC cluster; on the cluster they are deployed to a downloads area in project storage, and the data lands in a staging area beside it. This page describes the shared pattern, then each tool. What the registry records about a dataset's origin and licence is in Acquisition and licence; manifest fields are in Manifests.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  F["fetch<br/>(resumable, pinned)"] --> V["verify<br/>every file"]
  V --> D["completion record<br/>DONE · completion_summary.json · PROOF.json"]
  D --> M["manifest<br/>dataset_manifest.py"]
  M --> FO["fold<br/>fold_*.py → web/datasets.json"]
  FO --> R["register + link<br/>register_*.py · link_*.py"]
  R --> C["sync_catalog.py →<br/>served catalog"]
  C --> MG["dataset manager<br/>on the mesh"]

The tools differ by source, but they share these rules:

  • Pin the version. A Hugging Face dataset is fetched at a fixed revision; an OKN graph at its published pav:version; a Wikimedia or NLM release by its date or release name.
  • Resume, never restart. Fetchers keep what is already valid and fetch only what is missing.
  • Verify every file against what the publisher states (hashes, CRCs, row counts, an independent second extraction), and delete or refetch anything that does not match.
  • Write the completion record last, and only when every file is present and verified with nothing partial or extra. Downstream steps read the record, not the directory.
  • Run in Slurm on a CPU partition, not on the login node (Rules for the cluster).
  • Use the provider's own tool and settings. Never raise a service's concurrency.
  • Record the licence per dataset, and per document where documents carry different licences.

docs.title: Completion records
docs.text: Record Written by Meaning DONE Each fetcher's finish step The copy is complete and verified completion_summary.json (or completion_summary_partial.json) Finalizers {finished, datasets: [{slug, file_count, total_bytes, missing, hash}]}, or a whole-download summary {checked, n_missing_or_unverified, partial_files, extra_files} PROOF.json okn_prove.py The levels of exactness proof an OKN mirror passed agents/<sn>/state.json okn_agent.py The version, counts and last sync result an OKN agent holds

docs.title: Manifests and folding
docs.text:
web/dataset_manifest.py builds a canonical, sorted inventory of a dataset's files over its registered locations[] as (relpath, size, mtime), with counts and one manifest_hash (sha256 over the inventory). Its audit mode recomputes the hash and exits 0 on a match and 3 on drift. File content is not hashed (datasets reach hundreds of gigabytes); size and modification time are the per-file signature, which detects moves, growth and edits but does not prove two files in different stores hold the same bytes.

For large trees, web/dataset_manifest_parallel.py shards the walk at depth 3 across a process pool and produces a byte-identical canonical hash. web/derive_source_manifests.py cuts per-source manifests from one full-walk inventory when a corpus is an exact partition by sub-collection, so the tree is not walked twice.

web/fold_manifests.py <dir> [summary] [summary path] is the general folder: for each dataset with a manifest it copies the manifest into web/manifests/, sets the entry's manifest block (URN, file count, total bytes, missing locations, hash, time), moves status from acquiring to active when nothing is missing, and sets acquisition.status to complete. A whole-download summary is accepted only when it reports nothing missing, partial or extra. fold_renal_manifests.py and fold_tcga_manifests.py are its source-specific predecessors. web/manifests/ held 161 files at 57505c6.

docs.title: NSF Open Knowledge Network mirrors
docs.text:
web/acquisition/okn/ mirrors every deployed graph of the NSF Open Knowledge Network as an independent agent, and proves each copy recreates its upstream exactly. One graph counts as deployed only if its own endpoint answers. Measured: 42 graphs on 2026-09-26, 43 from 2026-10-02.

Script Role okn_fetch.py Extracts a graph from its public SPARQL endpoint in 1,000,000-triple N-Triples pages, four in parallel, and verifies it okn_prove.py Proves a held copy is exactly upstream's okn_agent.py The agents: upstream snapshots and versions, adoption, independent syncs, the six-hourly tick, store refresh deploy/panatlas-okn-tick.{service,timer} Runs the tick every 6 hours (00:17, 06:17, 12:17, 18:17)

Extraction. A page is accepted only if it has exactly the expected line count, every line is one statement, and the file ends in a newline. The public endpoints stop a query at about 30 s and append their error text to a truncated stream with HTTP 200, so a short or junk-carrying page is refetched and then split into ten sub-slices, recursively, down to 1,000 triples. A graph is DONE only if its lines equal the endpoint's COUNT(*), nothing is malformed and every line is distinct, or every repeated line is confirmed by the endpoint itself (the endpoints print some distinct values identically).

Proof (PROOF.json):

Level Check fingerprint sha256 of the sorted distinct triples; per-predicate counts; blank-node count upstream Per-predicate counts equal the endpoint's; 20 random slices byte-identical at their offsets; 2,000 random triples byte-identical among the endpoint's objects for their subject and predicate reextract A second full extraction at a different page size (999,983) hashes identically store The triples exported back out of the local SPARQL store equal the source (Knowledge store)

Agents. okn_agent.py snapshot | check [SN..] | sync SN | adopt SN | describe [SN..] | tick | store. Each agent records its held version, provenance and source-of-record declaration under agents/<sn>/. Every triple extracted from a graph has that graph as its source of record; panAtlas curates only nodes and edges whose source of record is panAtlas, and replaces a mirror wholesale when its agent syncs a new upstream version. The tick snapshots upstream, registers external dumps, and submits one independent okn_sync_<sn> Slurm job per changed graph; a sync that fails any proof returns current to the previous version. When no OKN job is active and the held versions differ from the served store, the tick submits a store build. web/register_okn.py upserts one registry entry per agent from the entry its agent writes.

Layout (data/sources_staging/okn/ in project storage): upstream/ snapshots; agents/<sn>/ state; raw/<sn>/<version>/part_*.nt with DONE and PROOF.json, and raw/<sn>/current pointing at the held version; raw/wikidata/<dump date>/ for the Wikimedia dump (its source of record is Wikimedia, not OKN); sor_index.json mapping authoritative namespaces to graphs.

Tests: python3 -m unittest test_okn_fetch test_okn_prove test_okn_agent. Fake endpoints reproduce truncation with appended text, confirmed repeats, paging errors, a single altered literal, the memory cap and over-long argument lists.
