docs.title: Renal biomarker datasets
docs.text:
web/acquisition/renal/ mirrors the tooling that pulled the raw data for a renal-biomarker project from GEO, GDC, PDC, KiTS23, TCIA and PRIDE.

File Role renal_fetch.py Resumable downloader with one subcommand per source and tier; logs every file to a JSONL manifest run_renal.sh Launches streams A, B and C launch_d.sh Smoke-tests two repaired stages, then opens stream D and restarts the finalizer finalize_renal.sh Waits for STREAM_{A,B,C,D}_DONE, runs one idempotent sweep of every stage, builds the manifests and writes completion_summary.json probe_dgx.py Pre-launch environment probe completion_summary.json The finalizer's record: 10 manifests, 48,281 files, 6.86 TB, 0 missing locations (finished 2026-09-06)

The registry entries are in web/datasets_renal.json, folded by web/fold_renal_manifests.py and linked by web/link_renal.py.

Renal ran on the login node

renal_fetch.py says it runs on the login node, and run_renal.sh and launch_d.sh start the streams in tmux and the finalizer with nohup there. This predates the 2026-10-08 rule. New acquisitions follow the OpenH and UMLS pattern: an sbatch script on a CPU partition.

docs.title: arXiv
docs.text:
web/acquisition/arxiv/ has no README. Its scripts acquire and align the Hugging Face snapshot secemp9/arxiv-complete (3,148,796 papers):

Script Role arxiv_fetch.py Resumable acquisition in priority order, so atlas-relevant text lands first arxiv_doc_index.py One row per paper for the document estate, with the licence per document arxiv_lexalign.py Aligns every paper to Wikipedia and MeSH nodes with the estate's own lexical linkers (no embeddings) arxiv_embed_align.py, arxiv_embed_align.sbatch Embeds arXiv with the estate's recipe and aligns it exactly as the estate is aligned arxiv_align_summary.py, arxiv_embed_summary.py Roll the alignments up into what the served graph and catalog show

web/register_arxiv.py, web/fold_arxiv_alignment.py and web/link_arxiv.py bring it into the registry and graph. The corpus node carries no concept edges by design: arXiv's own categories are not MeSH-grounded.

docs.title: UMLS (licensed, internal only)
docs.text:
web/acquisition/umls/ acquires the UMLS Metathesaurus as panAtlas's first project-restricted dataset, under a personal licence held by the project owner. It is used only to relate things internally.

  • The release is stored owner-only (mode 0700). The fetch fails if any path is group- or world-readable.
  • Nothing from it is published, committed or logged. The licence key is read from a private file, never from a command line or a log.
  • umls_fetch.sbatch runs as a Slurm job, never on the login node. It downloads the release archives through NLM's download API, checks every archive member's CRC and every published checksum, unpacks the Metathesaurus, and checks every RRF file against NLM's own MRFILES.RRF (rows exactly; size in bytes or characters as NLM counted them) before writing DONE.
  • Release 2026AA passed this phase (P1) on 2026-10-16 (job 237451).

The next phases, a separate restricted SPARQL store and per-user entitlements, are planned in PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md and not built. The restricted release is never served; the public graph carries only cross-code identifiers and their IRI forms (Code systems).

docs.title: Document licences
docs.text:
web/licence/ records a licence for every document in the estate, applying the policy that panAtlas ingests everything and treats licence as a per-document attribute consulted when documents are shared or used for training:

Script Role licence_registry.py, licence_registry.json The upstream licence table and the route from each estate source to its upstream estate_licence_build.py One licence, one Wikipedia primary link and one MeSH concept per estate document pmc_licence_scan.py, pmc_licence_scan.sbatch Per-document PMC licence group medrxiv_licence.py Per-preprint licence from the medRxiv API sft_label_extract.py, sft_components.py Upstream labels and duplicate trails for fine-tuning data apply_registry_licences.py Writes each text dataset's verified licence onto its registry entry

Measured 2026-09-23/24: the estate index holds 93,056,465 rows (89,907,669 embedded documents plus 3,148,796 arXiv papers), with a licence on every row and 85,128,342 verified.

docs.title: After acquisition
docs.text: Once folded and registered, a dataset is linked into the served graph, synced into the catalog, and deployed (Build pipeline). If it lives on a mesh node, a dataset manager is deployed for it and its manifest is re-audited on a schedule (Dataset managers).

docs.title: Astral: the agent interface
docs.text:
The Astral agent (web/astral/) registers panAtlas with the Astral agent platform, so that Astral users can query the atlas from chat and Astral's model can call panAtlas as tools. It is read-only and a bolt-on: it adds files under web/astral/ and changes nothing about the site. It does not call the WordPress REST API, and it writes nothing to the database or to the plugin.

Property Value Code agent.py (service, handshake, identity), skills.py (tool definitions), tools.py (handlers), atlas_store.py (in-memory index) Runs on The web host, as a systemd service bound to loopback; Apache forwards two paths to it over the existing TLS virtual host Reads The plugin's data/ directory: graph.json, datasets.json, benchmarks_llm.json, mm_evals.json, models.json Reaches The SPARQL store and the coverage service on the HPC cluster, over restricted SSH keys Scopes tools:read and tools:search only Tests web/astral/tests/ (agent, authorised identities, SPARQL tool, WordPress link contract)

docs.title: How it connects
docs.text:
The Astral orchestrator dials out to agents; it never accepts inbound agent connections. The web host accepts only the standard web and SSH ports at the network edge, so the agent cannot listen on a port of its own. It binds a loopback port and Apache forwards exactly two paths:

Astral orchestrator ──HTTPS──> https://panatlas.net/.well-known/agent-card.json
                    ──WSS────> wss://panatlas.net/agent ──> agent on loopback
  1. The orchestrator requests the agent card without a credential. panAtlas answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: AstralAgentKey.
  2. An explicitly trusted orchestrator retries with X-Astral-Agent-Key. The agent validates it before returning the card or accepting the socket.
  3. The orchestrator opens the WebSocket at /agent; the agent sends register_agent with its card.

The WebSocket is required. If it fails, the orchestrator's fallback registers the agent without a socket, which looks like success but leaves every tool invisible to the model. The agent deliberately does not serve the fallback card path, so that degraded mode cannot happen; the 404 for it in the logs is expected.

The agent key is defended three ways, and none may be relaxed without an equivalent replacement:

  1. the application compares exactly one X-Astral-Agent-Key header in constant time;
  2. Apache restricts both paths to the orchestrator's address;
  3. the agent enforces its own peer allowlist (PANATLAS_ALLOWED_PEERS), reading the real client from an Apache-overwritten forwarding header only when the direct peer is loopback.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
skills.py defines fifteen tools:

Tool What it returns search_atlas_graph Keyword search across the graph nodes get_atlas_node One node in full, bulky blocks omitted by default traverse_atlas_relations Neighbours, filterable by relation type search_datasets Search the audited dataset catalog get_dataset_provenance The full reproducibility record for one dataset search_benchmarks Search the language-model evaluation register get_benchmark_detail One benchmark plus every model score held for it compare_models_on_benchmarks Head-to-head across benchmarks get_model_profile Architecture, training corpus, evaluation summary list_imaging_evaluations Pathology and radiology foundation-model results lookup_concept_grounding Concept to MeSH descriptor and tree numbers get_concept_coverage Which datasets cover a concept and which benchmarks test it get_area_coverage How well the atlas's documents cover a free-text area, against the Wikipedia layer query_knowledge_graph Read-only SPARQL over the knowledge store summarize_atlas_state Counts and coverage, for orientation

Tool count

web/astral/README.md says "Fourteen tools" and then lists fifteen; the vault recorded fourteen on 2026-09-16, before query_knowledge_graph was added. The code defines fifteen.

Tool names avoid the prefixes Astral's high-risk gate refuses outright (send_, post_, fetch_, upload_, http_, delete_, drop_, wipe_, purge_, transfer_, pay_, deploy_); a test enforces this. When a sibling Astral checkout is present, the tests also validate every tool schema with Astral's own validator, which is what closes the socket on a bad schema.

Deliberately not exposed: the propose write path; navigate and model-lens (both spend a server-side LLM key, and wrapping an LLM in a tool called by an LLM is redundant); the federation registry (token hashes and contact details); the mesh snapshot (internal topology); whoami (identity); and the audit table (per-user browsing history).

Restricted datasets are catalogued, never served. Records whose access tier is restricted or credentialed* carry a fixed note that panAtlas holds metadata only.

docs.title: How the data is held
docs.text: atlas_store.py loads the five JSON files into an in-memory index and re-reads a file only when its modification time or size changes, so a site rebuild is picked up without a restart. After a WordPress plugin update, check that the data directory still exists, because an update replaces the plugin directory.

docs.title: query_knowledge_graph: how Astral reaches the store
docs.text:
The SPARQL store runs on the HPC cluster and answers only inside the cluster network (Knowledge store). The agent reaches it without an inbound port:

sequenceDiagram
  participant M as Astral model
  participant A as Astral agent (web host)
  participant C as sparql_client.py (cluster)
  participant E as endpoint record
  participant Q as QLever server (Slurm job)
  M->>A: query_knowledge_graph {query, store, max_rows}
  A->>C: ssh (restricted key), base64 JSON request
  C->>C: refuse SPARQL Update
  C->>E: read stores/STORE.endpoint
  C->>Q: POST query (timeout 120 s)
  Q-->>C: results
  C-->>A: JSON {vars, rows, truncated, seconds}
  A-->>M: rows + notes
  • The key is restricted. In authorized_keys the key may run only sparql_client.py, with no port forwarding, agent forwarding, X11 or terminal. The client accepts only a base64-encoded JSON object, never a shell command.
  • Requests. {"action": "describe", "store": …} lists the named graphs with versions, sizes and proofs; {"query": …, "store": …, "max_rows": …} runs a query.
  • Read-only. Any INSERT, DELETE, LOAD, CLEAR, DROP, CREATE, ADD, MOVE, COPY or WITH operation is refused, and the store has no update token.
  • Limits. Rows are capped at 1,000 (default 200). The client waits at most 120 s for the store (SPARQL_TIMEOUT); the agent's SSH call times out at 150 s by default (PANATLAS_SPARQL_TIMEOUT). Queries up to 20,000 characters are accepted.
  • Stores. store is panatlas-okn (default) or wikidata. The client also knows a wikidata-sample store name.

Tool input:

Field Type Notes query string SPARQL, 1 to 20,000 characters store enum panatlas-okn or wikidata describe boolean true lists the named graphs instead of running a query max_rows integer 1 to 1,000, default 200

Tool output: store, vars[], rows[], n_rows, truncated, boolean (for ASK), graphs[] (for describe), seconds, and notes[]. The notes always restate three facts a model needs: each named graph is a source of record (panAtlas's own graph, the OKN mirrors, Wikidata), panAtlas concepts link out by skos:exactMatch to MeSH and UMLS IRIs, and the store prints numbers and points as folded values. Configuration comes from PANATLAS_SPARQL_SSH_KEY, PANATLAS_SPARQL_HOST and PANATLAS_SPARQL_KNOWN_HOSTS; without them the tool answers "SPARQL store not configured".

Open decision: the SPARQL client runs on the login node

The forced-command key runs sparql_client.py on the cluster's login node. That conflicts with the rule that nothing but squeue, sacct and sbatch runs there. Whether the client should move into a Slurm job was left as an owner decision on 2026-10-17.

docs.title: get_area_coverage: the coverage service
docs.text:
get_area_coverage answers "how well does the atlas cover this area, and what nearby do we lack". It calls the W10 coverage service (web/coverage/w10_coverage_service.py) on the cluster over its own forced-command key (w10_client.py), with the same base64-JSON pattern.

  • Input: text (up to 2,000 characters) or a Wikipedia page_id; k (1 to 200, default 30); space (auto, name for title-only vectors, desc for title plus lead; auto picks by query length); centre (none or own); uncovered (0 to 50, default 10).
  • Output: verdict (well covered, partly covered, thin, unknown territory), summary, matches[] with each article's evidence class from the Wikipedia layer (strong, medium, bridge, weak, none), nearest_uncovered[], nearest_covered[], recipe, seconds, notes[].
  • Method: embed the text with the estate encoder and rank by exact cosine against all 6,748,358 article vectors. The notes say it measures topical proximity, not truth.
  • Measured 2026-09-16: identity recall@1 of 1.000 in both vector spaces (100 queries each); 1.2 s median latency; 3.7 s end to end from the agent, 1.3 s of it in the service.

The coverage service also runs on the login node

It runs as a user service on the login node, loopback only, because it holds about 33 GB in memory and the web host does not have that. The 2026-10-17 restore record lists it among the login-node services disabled on 2026-10-08.

docs.title: Identity: ORCID allowlist and the link flow
docs.text:
The agent does not call the plugin's access gate, because it reads the files directly. It enforces its own ORCID allowlist (PANATLAS_ALLOWED_ORCIDS) on every tools/call. The list must carry the same iDs as the plugin's gate; tests/test_authorized_identities.py fails if either side loses one.

An Astral user proves their ORCID iD through panAtlas:

  1. In Astral's panAtlas detail, Connect ORCID opens https://panatlas.net/?panatlas_astral_orcid_link=1 with a signed state from Astral.
  2. The plugin checks the state, sends the user straight to the ORCID authorisation URL, and receives them back through the OIDC plugin's public callback. This avoids WordPress's restricted login and admin paths.
  3. If the signed-in iD is on the allowlist, the plugin returns a short-lived signed handoff bound to that Astral user (provider orcid, issuer https://orcid.org) and writes link_astral_orcid to the audit log.
  4. Astral stores the link and passes only that verified iD to the agent in caller_info.verified_identity.

Missing configuration, an invalid or replayed handoff, a missing or malformed identity and an unlisted iD all fail closed. Tool arguments and unverified caller metadata never authorise a request. The agent card states the claim requirement and the link URL but never publishes the allowlist or the link secret. The link secret is a separate high-entropy value shared with Astral and held outside the repository.

The link was lost from the plugin when an older branch was merged on 2026-09-12 and restored on 2026-10-07.

docs.title: Making the tools available to every Astral user
docs.text: Registration alone does not make tools callable. With Astral's safe-agents setting on, a tool is allowed for all users only when the agent is both public and marked safe. The second flag is set from Astral's agent UI by the agent's owner or a realm administrator who has already saved their own LLM credentials; otherwise the action reports success and does nothing. Confirm the trust row exists afterwards (web/astral/README.md §4.4). Once both are set, a new user resolves to tools:read and tools:search with no per-user grant; explicit per-user decisions are kept.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
systemctl status panatlas-astral
journalctl -u panatlas-astral -f
curl -s localhost:<agent port>/healthz | python3 -m json.tool
Symptom Cause /healthz 503 Data unavailable, the agent key unusable, or the ORCID allowlist empty Card fetched, tools absent in chat The WebSocket did not connect Socket closed with 1008 Access control unconfigured, key mismatch, or a schema the orchestrator rejected Tool call returns -32001 The Astral account has not connected ORCID, or the iD is not on the allowlist Connect ORCID returns 403 before WordPress The card still advertises a legacy admin URL; set PANATLAS_ORCID_LINK_URL to the front-controller form and restart Tools visible but refused The agent is not yet public and safe

For local development the agent runs standalone against the committed data files (PANATLAS_DATA_DIR=../wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data), and web/astral/local/README.md describes an end-to-end test against a local Astral orchestrator in Docker with mock authentication.

docs.title: Build pipeline
docs.text:
The served atlas is a set of JSON files compiled from registries and from analysis outputs. The work happens in three places:

Place What is built there Entry points HPC cluster, inside Slurm jobs Everything heavy: acquisition, manifests, the document index, concept mapping, embeddings, evaluation ingest, the universe projection, the Wikipedia layer, RDF and SPARQL stores web/dgx/, web/acquisition/, web/wikipedia_layer/, web/rdf/ A workstation with the repository (web/) The served property graph and catalogs, the curation layers, the evaluation index, verification The graph builders, web/build_all.sh, web/deploy.sh The web host The nightly literature feed web/pipeline/literature/server/ 
flowchart TB
  C["Cluster outputs<br/>(full_eval.json, mm_evals, doc_concept_agg,<br/>record typing, manifests, classification)"] --> U
  R["Registries<br/>datasets.json · models.json · codesystems.json"] --> U
  A["atlas/20-concepts/*.md"] --> U
  U["Stage 1: upstream graph builders<br/>(build_graph … apply_bench_taxonomy)"] --> D["plugin data/<br/>graph.json · datasets.json · benchmarks_llm.json"]
  D --> B["Stage 2: build_all.sh<br/>curation layers + verification"]
  B --> P["Stage 3: register / link / fold /<br/>sync_catalog / build_evals_index"]
  P --> T["Verify: ui_harness.js,<br/>test_public_api.py --stage"]
  T --> DEP["deploy.sh → web host"]
  DEP --> L["Verify live:<br/>test_public_api.py --live"]

There is no single end-to-end build script

build_all.sh is the ordered entry point for the curation layers only. It assumes the upstream graph builders have already produced graph.json, datasets.json and benchmarks_llm.json (its header says so), and it does not run the post-build register, link and fold steps or build_evals_index.py. Those are run by hand in the order given below. Most scripts declare themselves idempotent (nodes updated in place, edges de-duplicated), so re-running a step is safe.

docs.title: Stage 1: upstream graph builders
docs.text:
These produce the three files build_all.sh starts from. build_all.sh names them, in this order, as its precondition. All write into web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/ unless noted.

Script What it does build_graph.py Compiles the first-interface inventory graph (web/graph.json) from the curated dataset catalog page in the knowledge vault. An intermediate, not the served graph. build_layered.py The core compiler. Builds the layered graph (concept, dataset and ontology layers, with modality as a facet) from the MeSH-grounded concept spine (atlas/20-concepts/*.md plus concept_mesh_grounded.json), code systems, FHIR, NACC, nutrition, FoodAtlas, FNDDS, the imaging registry, domains, measured corpus sources (dgx_sources.json), the document rollup and footprint, and merged federation output. Writes data/graph.json. build_all_datasets.py Exhaustive corpus-source accounting: every data source on disk, used or not, tagged with modality, status, location and scale. build_train_sources.py Wires the authoritative per-model training manifests (v4_train_sources.json, v5_train_sources.json) as trained_on edges, replacing partial ones. build_source_topics.py Propagates each training source's content domain (a clinical specialty or other content area, from the V4/V5 source manifests) onto the catalog entries. sft_wiring.py Wires the measured supervised fine-tuning inventory into the graph. build_corpus_structure.py Fixes the dataset model: a model has a few datasets (pretraining corpus, SFT set), each composed of sources. model_wiring.py Restores full graph stats and wires model to dataset and benchmark edges. build_benchmark_nodes.py Promotes benchmarks to first-class nodes: dataset test_set_of benchmark tests concept. build_concept_remap.py Wires the judge-gated item-to-concept mapping (pipeline/qconcept2/*.jsonl), including 120 general Wikipedia-grounded concepts. apply_bench_taxonomy.py Replaces arm groupings with two axes, testing type and domain, from bench_taxonomy.json.

build_layered.py is not portable as written

It reads vault metadata from a hard-coded absolute path on one workstation, reads benchmark centroids from a temporary file, and writes a second copy of graph.json to a temporary preview directory. Running it on another machine needs those paths changed. build_graph.py and pipeline/check_curriculum_vault.py also read the knowledge vault, which is not part of this repository.

docs.title: Stage 2: build_all.sh
docs.text:
web/build_all.sh runs from web/ under set -euo pipefail, so any failing step stops the build, except the one step marked below. Graph paths are wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/data/….

# Command Reads Writes 1 python3 build_artifact_types.py pipeline/artifact_types.json (33-type vocabulary, each grounded to a verified Wikipedia article and, where faithful, a MeSH descriptor), the v4/v5 training manifests, benchmark facets Artifact-type nodes; has_artifact_type and covers_topic edges on pretraining sources, SFT sources and benchmarks; stamps graph.json, datasets.json, benchmarks_llm.json; pipeline/corpus_type_profile.json 2 python3 build_curriculum.py pipeline/model_curriculum.json (schema panatlas-model-curriculum/1) training-stage nodes with data, dates and jobs, system, config and codebase; edges has_training_stage, stage_trained_on, follows, executed_on, built_with; curriculum_disclosed on every model node 3 python3 build_record_level.py pipeline/doc_concept_agg.json (per-document concepts, 89.9M documents across 136 sources), pipeline/record_level/record_typing_results.json (every SFT record typed on the cluster), training manifests Corpus-level type × topic matrices with stated coverage; per-record type and register on SFT mix and source nodes; pipeline/record_level/record_level_wired.json 4 python3 pipeline/existing_meta/merge_gap.py \|\| true Gap-classification worker shards pipeline/existing_meta/gap_classification.json (26 sampled sources). Failure is tolerated (\|\| true): when labels are absent the build continues 5 python3 build_existing_meta.py pipeline/existing_meta/pretrain_classification.json, pretrain_holes_classification.json, gap_classification.json, grounding verdicts Per-source domain, data-type and register distributions wired to existing concept nodes; existing_classification_wired.json. Generates nothing new 6 python3 build_native_meta.py pipeline/existing_meta/source_native_meta.json and the classification files native_fields, has_embeddings and doc_classification_status (full-population or source-level only) on pretraining source nodes 7 python3 build_field_values.py pipeline/existing_meta/native_field_values.json Categorical counts, numeric summaries and identifier distinct-counts on pretraining source nodes 8 python3 build_patho_evals.py pipeline/patho_evals/*.json (BACH, CRC and neuropathology results) Pathology results reconciled into mm_evals.json; pathology benchmarks wired into the concept graph 9 python3 build_eval_map.py benchmark_ontology_facets.json, benchmark_audit.json, benchmark_suite_fit.json The audit block, including audit.map (a 2-D UMAP projection of each benchmark's facet vector, with a PCA fallback) in data/benchmarks_llm.json. Without it the Benchmarks map view is empty 10 python3 pipeline/check_curriculum_vault.py pipeline/model_curriculum.json, the knowledge vault Nothing. Exits 1 if any hard curriculum fact (SLURM job ids, config paths, codebase paths) is missing from the vault 11 node pipeline/ui_harness.js assets/app.js, data/graph.json, data/datasets.json, data/benchmarks_llm.json Nothing. Loads the front end against a stubbed DOM and drives every render path over the real data; exits 1 on any failure

The script ends with BUILD+VERIFY COMPLETE. Deploy with: ./deploy.sh. Measured harness runs: 18,941 renders with 0 failures (2026-09-12) and 19,238 renders with 0 failures (2026-10-16).

web/guard_eval_map.sh is a separate guard for step 9: it detects a live benchmarks endpoint without audit.map, a missing coverage grid, or a changed map source, and rebuilds and redeploys that one file.

docs.title: Stage 3: register, link, fold, and the evaluation index
docs.text:
New data enters the served graph through small idempotent scripts, each named for its step:

Step Scripts Effect Register register_fragment.py (any panatlas.datasets/1 fragment), register_okn.py, register_openh.py, register_arxiv.py, register_neuropath.py, register_tcga.py, register_predictors.py, renal_sbir_registry.py Upsert entries into web/datasets.json (by URN) or web/models.json Fold fold_manifests.py, fold_renal_manifests.py, fold_tcga_manifests.py, fold_arxiv_alignment.py Write cluster-built manifests and completion records into the registry entries Link link_renal.py, link_neuropath.py, link_openh.py, link_arxiv.py, link_predictors.py, link_datasets_to_nodes.py Add dataset, concept and model nodes and edges to the served graph.json Catalog sync_catalog.py Upsert web/datasets.json into the served catalog data/datasets.json, keyed by URN Evaluations attach_full_eval.py, reconcile_benchmarks.py, build_evals_index.py Attach model batteries to model nodes; reconcile the benchmark catalog with what was run; build data/evals_index.json, the one index behind the public API

The order recorded for the predictor-model suite (web/fm_suite/README.md) is a worked example:

# from web/
FM_SUITE_ROOT=<working copy> python3 fm_suite/suite/export_panatlas.py predictor_evals.json
python3 register_fragment.py datasets_fm_suite.json
python3 register_predictors.py
python3 sync_catalog.py
python3 link_predictors.py
python3 build_evals_index.py
node pipeline/ui_harness.js

build_evals_index.py is outside build_all.sh

deploy.sh ships data/evals_index.json, but build_all.sh never rebuilds it. After any change to benchmarks_llm.json, full_eval.json, mm_evals.json, predictor_evals.json or models.json, run build_evals_index.py before deploying, or the public API serves stale scores.

docs.title: Cluster-side builds (web/dgx/)
docs.text:
web/dgx/ is a mirror, taken 2026-09-13, of every *.py, *.sh and *.sbatch in the panAtlas directory on the cluster: the registry, label, universe and manifest side of the build. Twenty of these files also exist under web/ or web/pipeline/; where the cluster copy differs, the cluster copy produced the current artifacts (web/dgx/README.md). The mirror is a snapshot, so check the cluster copy before relying on a detail.

Group Scripts Output Registry and manifests dataset_manifest.py, build_dataset_reports.py, inventory.py, classify_splits.py, count_docs.sh Manifests (manifest_hash), each dataset manager's structure-only report, corpus inventory, split classification. An hourly user timer re-audits the cluster registry and regenerates the manager reports Document index and concepts build_master_index.py, agg_doc_concept.py, dup.py, uniq.py, verify_uniq.py, map_concepts.py, map_concepts2.py, map_concepts3.py, map_mesh.py, map_mesh2.py, map_final.py, mesh_expand.py, expand_clean.py, llm_label_cells.py, llm_judge_cells.py, validate_build.py, recount.py, validate_footprint*.py Every embedded document mapped to a MeSH concept through its cell, with duplicate-id checks on the index; MeSH grounding confirmed per descriptor; cell labels and medical/general judgments; the footprint validation Anchors and embeddings assemble_text.py, generate_concept_text.py, normalize_node_text.py, embed_concepts*.py, build_text_anchors.py, build_image_anchors.py, precompute_pooled.py, exp_anchor_study.py, embed_attach.py, pa_local_agent.py Concept anchors in the registered text space (BioClinical-ModernBERT-large, 1024-d) and image space (RAD-DINO, 768-d); the attach process that relates new embeddings to concepts Evaluation ingest_full_eval.py, build_mm_evals.py, build_concept_accuracy.py, extract_questions.py, build_question_concept_map.py, remap_general.py, remap_gated.py, precompute_cellmap.py full_eval.json (every model's battery), mm_evals.json (imaging and multi-modal results, with the evaluation type inferred from the result-file structure), per-concept accuracy, question-to-concept maps Contamination decontam_exact.py, ledger_by_source.py Exact-document contamination check against the training ledgers (blake2b, 16-byte digest over raw text); per-source ledger counts Universe build_universe.py, build_universe_export.py, build_universe_export_full.py (and web/pipeline/universe/build_backbone.py) A 2-D coordinate for every document, exported in resolution tiers for the browser, with the graph overlaid as a backbone Literature identity build_pmc_map.py Per-article PMCID/PMID for the trained PMC corpora, recovered by content anchor

Other cluster-side chains have their own directories: the Wikipedia world-view layer (web/wikipedia_layer/, steps W0 to W9 for the pinned run 20260901), the OKN mirrors and other acquisitions (Acquisition), document licences (web/licence/), and the RDF export and SPARQL stores (Knowledge store).

Getting results to the workstation. Cluster outputs are copied into web/ (for example full_eval.json after ingest_full_eval.py) and the workstation steps are re-run. web/finish_v2.sh is a recorded one-shot of this pattern for one classifier pass: pull worker shards, merge, rebuild the record-level layer, verify, deploy.

docs.title: Deploy: deploy.sh
docs.text:
web/deploy.sh runs after build_all.sh passes. It copies, from web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/ to the plugin directory on the web host:

Files Destination assets/app.js, assets/style.css assets/ data/graph.json, data/datasets.json, data/benchmarks_llm.json, data/mm_evals.json, data/evals_index.json data/ includes/public-evals.php, then includes/public-api.php includes/ (in that order, because public-api.php requires public-evals.php)

It then sets ownership of the copied files to the web server user. It never touches data/mesh.json, which the mesh daemon on the web host rewrites live.

What deploy.sh does not deploy

The main plugin file panatlas-explorer.php, the other includes (federation-admin.php, mesh.php, wikimap.php), universe.js, wikimap.js, data/models.json and data/kg_graphs.json are not in the script. The universe and world-map assets live outside the web root and have their own install paths (web/wikimap/install_wikimap.sh for the map). A change to any of these is deployed separately. Recorded deploys take a dated backup of the plugin's data directory first; deploy.sh does not.

docs.title: Verify after deploying
docs.text:
python3 tests/test_public_api.py --stage DIR   # a staged plugin copy, through tests/public_api_harness.php
python3 tests/test_public_api.py --live        # against panatlas.net; exit status = number of failures
python3 tests/test_explore_e2e.py              # asks a real external LLM client the questions the atlas must answer

The public API contract test also fails a response that contains an internal path or host string, or a tool result over 24,000 characters (Public API).

docs.title: Rules for the cluster
docs.text:
These are standing rules for anything that runs on the HPC cluster (owner rule of 2026-10-08, recorded in web/rdf/README.md and the acquisition READMEs):

  • Compute runs in Slurm jobs, never on the login node. On the login node only squeue, sacct and sbatch run. Inspect a running job with srun --overlap --jobid <id> -n1 -c1 --mem=1G … (-n1, or the command runs once per task).
  • CPU jobs go to a CPU partition so they never hold a GPU node. The serving job for the SPARQL store, the OpenH download and the UMLS fetch all follow this.
  • Third-party services use their own tools and settings. Never raise a provider's concurrency (the OpenH-RF download uses the official hf download with its own adaptive concurrency).
  • Large walks are parallel jobs. A single-threaded walk of the CT corpus on the login node did not finish in 25 minutes; dataset_manifest_parallel.py shards the tree and produces a byte-identical canonical hash.

Known exceptions in the current code

Several components predate the rule or still run on the login node. They are listed so nobody copies the pattern:

Component What it does on the login node web/acquisition/renal/run_renal.sh, launch_d.sh, finalize_renal.sh Launched the renal download streams in tmux and the finalizer with nohup (finished 2026-09-06, before the rule) web/acquisition/okn/deploy/panatlas-okn-tick.timer Runs the OKN tick as a user systemd timer every 6 hours; the tick submits the real work as Slurm jobs web/coverage/w10_coverage_service.py The coverage service for Astral runs as a user service on the login node, loopback only web/rdf/sparql_client.py Astral's SPARQL tool runs this client on the login node over its forced-command key. Whether it should move into a Slurm job is an open owner decision (2026-10-17) Hourly registry refresh and agent supervision timers User systemd timers on the login node (Operations) web/pipeline/wiki_prep.py; precompute_cellmap.py and extract_questions.py The first's docstring and web/BENCHMARK-QUESTION-MAPPING.md for the other two say they run on the login node

The 2026-10-17 restore record says the panAtlas user services on the login node (agent, watchdog, coverage, refresh, CT re-walk, OKN tick) were disabled on 2026-10-08 and not re-enabled in that session.

docs.title: Knowledge store (SPARQL)
docs.text:
panAtlas keeps its graph in RDF as well as in the served JSON, and loads it, together with mirrored public knowledge graphs, into local QLever SPARQL stores on the HPC cluster. A store is a query view: it lets agents and jobs join panAtlas to other graphs. It is not the record. Exact recreation always comes from the verified raw files, because QLever cannot keep every literal verbatim (see Exactness).

This page is operational: what the stores hold, how they are built, proven, served and queried. The vocabulary of panAtlas's own graph (classes, properties, IRIs) is in RDF vocabulary.

docs.title: The stores
docs.text:
Store Contents Size State panatlas-okn panAtlas's own graph plus every NSF Open Knowledge Network graph whose mirror is proven exact, each in its own named graph Build panatlas-okn-20261003T0039: 44 named graphs, 6,994,341,217 triples Every graph round-tripped exactly; live since 2026-10-03 07:43. Served by job 226412 until 2026-10-08 (cancelled when all jobs were stopped), and again by job 237423 since 2026-10-16 08:06, checked at the same count wikidata The Wikimedia Wikidata dump (md5-verified), one graph 21,350,107,674 triples, indexed 2026-10-02 Not served as of the last record. The first build failed a smoke test that assumed English labels; a verify-only rerun (job 237432) passed all six tests and was in the last stage of the exact round trip on 2026-10-17. It switches live only if the round trip is exact

Code: web/rdf/ (build_rdf.py, qlever_build.py, qlever_serve.py, sparql_client.py, nt_canon.py, qlever_fold.py, qlever_export.py). Stores live under <cluster project storage>/panatlas/qlever/stores/.

docs.title: Named graph = source of record
docs.text:
Each source keeps its own named graph, so a query can always say where a fact comes from (GRAPH ?g { … }):

https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas         panAtlas's own graph (the only one panAtlas curates)
https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/<shortname>   read-only mirror of an OKN graph
http://www.wikidata.org/                    Wikidata (store `wikidata`)

panAtlas concepts link out with skos:exactMatch to the IRIs other graphs use: MeSH as http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/… (NLM mints http; https only redirects) and UMLS as http://linkedlifedata.com/resource/umls/id/… (the form the OKN graphs use). The stems are registered in web/codesystems.json (Code systems).

Joins this enables, tested in the store on 2026-09-26: 3,373 of 3,377 panAtlas MeSH IRIs exist in NLM's MeSH RDF; 3,310 panAtlas concepts reach 3,313 Wikidata entities through the OKN identifier-mappings graph; 137 MeSH IRIs join one OKN graph only through its https variant.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Produced by Admission rule panatlas.nq build_rdf.py from the served graph Each quad written once. Build of 2026-09-26: 213,647 quads (6,088 nodes, 16,891 edges; 361 duplicates suppressed), validated with rdflib OKN mirrors okn/raw/<sn>/current/part_*.nt web/acquisition/okn/okn_agent.py Admitted only if the extraction is proven clean (lines = distinct = endpoint COUNT(*), nothing malformed, or a strict re-check passes) and PROOF.json shows fingerprint, upstream and re-extraction checks all passed (Acquisition) Wikidata dump The Wikidata agent md5-verified; streamed through lbzip2 into the indexer while the same pass counts lines

python3 qlever_build.py plan prints what would be built, which graphs are admitted, and why the others are left out. It is the one subcommand that may run without a job.

docs.title: Lifecycle: build, test, prove, switch, serve
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  P["plan<br/>(proven inputs)"] --> B["build<br/>(Slurm job: index)"]
  B --> T{"tests<br/>pass?"}
  T -- no --> F["stores/NAME.last_failure<br/>(not resubmitted)"]
  F -. "fix cause" .-> V["verify<br/>(re-test existing index)"]
  V --> T
  T -- yes --> R{"exact<br/>round trip?"}
  R -- no --> F
  R -- yes --> S["switch stores/NAME<br/>to the new build"]
  S --> SV["serve<br/>(Slurm job writes<br/>stores/NAME.endpoint)"]
  1. Build. Inside a Slurm job, qlever_build.py build writes stores/<name>-<stamp>/ (index, manifest.json, tests.json) and serves it on a private port inside the job.
  2. Test. Every graph's triple count must equal its verified count exactly; no graph may appear that was not admitted; the panAtlas MeSH joins must hold. For Wikidata the triple count must lie within 0.1 % below the dump's line count (QLever drops exact duplicate triples) and known facts must answer (Q42 "Douglas Adams" in en or mul, Q5 "human", Q42 P31 Q5, items with a MeSH ID).
  3. Round trip (below).
  4. Switch. Only when every test passes and the round trip is exact does the stores/<name> link move to the new build.
  5. Serve. qlever_serve.py start submits the serving job; the job writes an endpoint record once the server answers a real query.

A failed build writes stores/<name>.last_failure and is not resubmitted automatically. After fixing the cause, qlever_build.py verify <store dir> re-runs the tests and round trip on the index already built (no re-index) and removes the failure record when it passes. Builds are submitted with SERVE_AFTER=1 to start serving on success.

Automation. The six-hourly OKN tick (okn_agent.py tick) submits a panatlas-okn build when no OKN job is active and the held graph versions differ from the served store, and a Wikidata build when the Wikidata agent holds a newer verified dump. Both serve only after an exact round trip.

# placeholders: <cluster project storage>, Slurm options omitted
STORE=panatlas-okn python3 qlever_build.py plan
sbatch ... --export=ALL,STORE=panatlas-okn,SERVE_AFTER=1 --wrap 'python3 qlever_build.py build'
sbatch ... --export=ALL,STORE=<name>,SERVE_AFTER=1 --wrap 'python3 qlever_build.py verify <store dir>'
python3 qlever_build.py roundtrip <store dir> [graph ...]      # inside a job
python3 qlever_serve.py start|status|query|stop [store]

docs.title: Exactness: the round trip
docs.text:
QLever folds literals into value identifiers and prints the value on export, and has no setting to stop it. Six folding rules, each read from QLever's source and confirmed on data:

Rule Effect integer xsd:integer becomes xsd:int (60-bit range) decimal / double Stored as a double minus its 4 lowest mantissa bits; printed %.1f or %.13g as xsd:decimal (lossy past 13 significant digits) point WKT POINT quantised to a 30-bit grid per coordinate, printed %f (sub-metre loss; two stored points can print alike) dateTime A year beyond four digits loses its Z unparseable A folded-type literal QLever cannot parse (a leap second, a point out of range) loses its datatype spelling \uXXXX escapes, ^^xsd:string, language-tag case (same RDF term)

The round trip exports every graph back out of the store (a CONSTRUCT over its named graph) and requires:

  • the sorted, distinct, non-blank triples of canon(export) hash identically (sha256) to canon(fold(source)), where nt_canon.py gives one spelling per RDF term and qlever_fold.py applies the rules above to the source;
  • blank-node triple counts are equal (the store assigns its own blank-node labels);
  • COUNT(*) equals the distinct stored values of the source (nt_canon.py --qlever-fold-ids).

Anything a rule does not explain blocks the switch, and the differing lines are written to roundtrip/<graph>.diff. The round trip is recorded per graph in roundtrip/roundtrip.json, which the describe action reports as round_trip_exact and lossy_folds.

docs.title: Serving
docs.text:
qlever_serve.py start submits a CPU-only Slurm job named qlever_serve_<store> with no time limit, on a CPU partition so it never holds a GPU node. Inside the job the server runs from a container image of QLever (commit d5b7eb2), bound to a free port, with a one-hour limit on any single query. Once a real query answers, the job writes stores/<store>.endpoint:

{"store": "...", "store_dir": "...", "host": "<cluster node>", "port": "<port>", "job": "<job id>",
 "started": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", "url": "http://<cluster node>:<port>/"}

The record is removed when the job ends. The address moves whenever a new build is switched live or the server restarts, so always read it from the record. status reports a record whose server no longer answers as STALE. The endpoint is reachable only inside the cluster network; nothing is exposed outside it.

docs.title: Querying
docs.text:
From inside a Slurm job only. Never run queries, tests or scripts on the login node. Attach to the serving job and query from there:

srun --overlap --jobid <serve job> -n1 -c1 --mem=1G bash
cd <cluster project storage>/panatlas/qlever
python3 qlever_serve.py status panatlas-okn                 # endpoint record + live total triple count (~140 s)
python3 qlever_serve.py query panatlas-okn 'SELECT ...'     # TSV
curl -s "$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.load(open("stores/panatlas-okn.endpoint"))["url"])')" \
     --data-urlencode 'query=SELECT ...' -H 'Accept: application/sparql-results+json'

From an agent: Astral's query_knowledge_graph tool (Astral).

From the public site: only the store manifest, through GET /kg/graphs on the public API. The public API accepts no SPARQL.

Examples, run against the live store on 2026-10-08:

# panAtlas concepts with their NLM MeSH labels (1.2 s)
PREFIX skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?c ?m ?label WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas> { ?c skos:exactMatch ?m }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/biobricks-mesh> { ?m rdfs:label ?label } } LIMIT 3
# -> panatlas:fa-dis-C531609  mesh:C531609  "Diffuse alopecia"@en

# panAtlas concepts to Wikidata entities through OKN identifier-mappings (7.2 s)
PREFIX skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#>
SELECT ?c ?w WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://panatlas.net/graph/panatlas> { ?c skos:exactMatch ?m }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/identifier-mappings> { ?w skos:exactMatch ?m } } LIMIT 3
# -> panatlas:fa-dis-C531609  wd:Q9394945

docs.title: Know before you query
docs.text:
• Folded literals. Decimals print at 13 significant digits; WKT points are quantised. Take exact values from the raw files.
  • Slow scans. A count over every graph, or a GROUP BY over all triples, takes minutes on 7 billion triples; the server stops any query at one hour.
  • Wikidata labels. A name shared by every language is stored once under the language code mul (Q42 has 75 labels and none @en). For English use FILTER(LANG(?l) IN ('en', 'mul')) and prefer en.
  • Two stores. panatlas-okn and wikidata are separate stores, joined at query time with SERVICE.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
python3 -m unittest test_nt_canon test_qlever_fold test_qlever_build   # in web/rdf; run on the cluster

The cases come from the observed round trips and the Wikidata store. The digest step uses GNU sort and sha256sum, so the tests are meant to run on the cluster.

docs.title: Planned
docs.text: A separate restricted store for licensed data, built with the same exact round trip and kept apart from panatlas-okn, is planned (PLAN-restricted-data-umls.md, phase P2). It is not built.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
The public API is a read-only HTTP interface to everything panAtlas indexes: statistics, graph search and lookup, the dataset registry, every measured evaluation score for every model type, the literature feed, and the list of knowledge graphs in the SPARQL store. It needs no key. It is separate from the gated panatlas/v1 routes that the explorer uses (Web site).

Property Value Base URL https://panatlas.net/wp-json/panatlas/public/v1 Version 1.1.1 (2026-10-31) Methods GET only Auth None Rate limit 240 requests per client address per minute; requests from the web host itself are exempt. Over the limit: HTTP 429, code rate_limited CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, methods GET, OPTIONS Caching Cache-Control: public with max-age 300 s by default, 3,600 s for /stats, /literature and /kg/graphs, 86,400 s for /teaser Description /openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1.0) and /tools.json (the same routes as LLM tool definitions); human-readable docs at panatlas.net/api/ Code web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/includes/public-api.php (statistics, search, node, dataset, literature, spec), includes/public-evals.php (evaluations) Contract test web/tests/test_public_api.py (--stage DIR or --live)

docs.title: Rules the API keeps
docs.text:
From docs/public-api.md and the code:

  • Additive only. Existing routes and tools keep their names and shapes; new behaviour is added.
  • Nothing internal leaves. Fields are served from whitelists, and every string passes a scrubber that removes server paths, cluster host names and job numbers. Data itself is never served, only records about it. No raw SPARQL is accepted.
  • Fit an LLM's tool budget. Results stay under 24,000 characters at default limits, because the first external client truncates there.
  • Say what is covered. Every evaluation response carries a coverage block, so a search that misses cannot be read as missing data.
  • One metric per benchmark. Values are compared only within one benchmark; cross-benchmark rankings are mean positions and say so.

docs.title: Response envelope
docs.text:
Every data route returns:

{
  "as_of": "<ISO 8601 time or null>",
  "source": "snapshot",
  "data": { }
}
  • as_of is the newest modification time of the snapshot files behind the answer (ISO 8601), or the store's build time for /kg/graphs. It is null when not applicable.
  • source is snapshot for answers from the served files, nightly PubMed feed for /literature, and SPARQL store manifest for /kg/graphs.
  • Errors use the standard WordPress REST error body {"code", "message", "data": {"status"}} with codes not_found (404), bad_request (400) and rate_limited (429). Not-found messages for models suggest the closest names.

Links into the explorer are returned as https://panatlas.net/#node=<id>.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Route Tool name Purpose GET /best best_models Which model is best for a task, data type or domain. Start here GET /overview atlas_overview What has been evaluated, by model type, with the leader of every scored benchmark GET /tasks task_scores Rank models on one task inside a suite GET /scores query_scores Filter every measured score GET /stats stats Headline counts of everything indexed GET /search search_atlas Search graph nodes by words GET /node/{id} get_node One node with public fields and links grouped by relation GET /neighborhood get_neighborhood Nodes and links around up to 12 ids GET /datasets search_datasets Search the dataset registry GET /datasets/{slug} get_dataset One dataset record GET /benchmarks search_benchmarks Search benchmarks and suites of every model type GET /benchmarks/{id} get_benchmark One benchmark: what it measures, full ranking, baselines, held-out models GET /models list_models Every evaluated model of every type GET /models/{name} get_model_scores Every score for one model GET /compare compare_models One benchmark's ranking, or a head-to-head between named models GET /literature/{node} get_literature Recent PubMed articles for a MeSH-grounded node GET /kg/graphs list_knowledge_graphs Named graphs in the SPARQL store with triple counts GET /teaser/{part} (none) Public binary geometry of the document universe GET /openapi.json (none) The OpenAPI description GET /tools.json (none) {instructions, tools[]} for LLM clients

The model types are language, vision, multimodal, tabular and forecasting. Type and domain parameters accept everyday words ("time series", "structured"), which the server maps to a type through a vocabulary in evals_index.json.

docs.title: GET /best
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes task (required) string The task in plain words: "tabular data", "forecasting hospital admissions", "pathology encoders". q and question are accepted as aliases type string Optional model type domain string Optional domain: medical, pathology, radiology, … limit integer Models per benchmark, default 5, at most 25

Returns question, interpreted_as {type, domain, words}, coverage, matched, count, and results[] (up to six benchmarks of one type, or two per type when several match, at most ten). Each result is a suite record: id, name, type, domain, metric, how_to_read, headline, ranking[] (rank, name, value, optional mean_rank, beats_best_baseline, flags ours, published, verified), best_baseline, held_out[] and url. Also, when they apply: answer_from: "matching_tasks" with matching_tasks[] when a single task holds every specific word of the question; overall (per type, with three or more matched benchmarks) with overall_method explaining avg_position; listed_not_run; listed_not_yet_scored; more_benchmarks; note; and advice, a sentence telling an LLM how to state the answer. When nothing matches, matched: false with advice to retry with a type or call atlas_overview.

docs.title: GET /overview
docs.text: No parameters. Returns types, keyed by model type, each with label, evaluated_models, evaluated_baselines, scored_benchmarks, listed_not_run, benchmarks[] (id, name, domain, metric, n_models, leader, leader_value, leader_mean_rank) and not_run[] (name, reason), plus how_to_use. Parts of a benchmark (such as one MMLU subject) are not listed as benchmarks of their own.

docs.title: GET /tasks
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes q string Words describing the task ("hospital admission", "diabetes") benchmark string Suite id or name; alone, lists that suite's tasks with their leaders task string Exact task name; returns that task's ranking type string tabular or forecasting limit integer Models per task, default 10, at most 40

Give at least one of q, benchmark or task, or the route returns 400. A benchmark without per-task tables returns 404 listing the suites that have them.

docs.title: GET /scores
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes model string Model name or part of one type, domain string Model type; domain benchmark string Benchmark id or name metric string Part of a metric name: acc, F1, AUC, Elo min, max number Value range max_rank integer Only rows at this rank or better; 1 lists benchmark leaders limit integer Default 40, at most 200

Returns count, a note that values compare only within one benchmark, and results[] rows with rank, of, name, value, benchmark, benchmark_id, type, domain, metric, sorted by rank.

docs.title: GET /benchmarks and GET /benchmarks/{id}
docs.text:
/benchmarks takes q, type, domain, capability (a capability id such as cap-clinical-knowledge) and limit (default 25, at most 150). It returns count, interpreted_as, coverage, capabilities[] and results[] with id, name, type, domain, metric, testing_type, measures, run_status, n_models_scored and the leader where models were scored.

/benchmarks/{id} accepts an id or a name and limit (default 40, at most 120). It returns the suite record (above) merged with the benchmark's public catalog fields (measures, composition, testing_type, arm, tests, tier, gated, higher_better, verified_published, provenance, …), project and eval_type for imaging and multi-modal benchmarks, and tasks_available when per-task tables exist.

docs.title: GET /models and GET /models/{name}
docs.text:
/models takes q (name filter), type, role (foundation-model, baseline or model), include_not_run (boolean) and limit (default 60, at most 300). It returns count, evaluated_models, evaluated_baselines, how_to_count, coverage and results[] with name, type, role, status, n_benchmarks, modalities and best_result {benchmark, rank, of, value}. Baselines sort last.

/models/{name} accepts partial names. It returns name, type, types, role, status, n_benchmarks, where present family, source, open_weights, runs, note, not_run_reason and url, then scores[] (each score with its rank on that benchmark) and published_leaderboard rows for methods panAtlas did not run itself.

docs.title: GET /compare
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes benchmark string One benchmark's full ranking models string Two or more model names, comma-separated, for a head-to-head limit integer Maximum rows (head-to-head default 30, at most 60)

A head-to-head returns models[], shared_benchmarks, ahead_on and results[] (benchmark, benchmark_id, metric, how_to_read, scores {model: {value, rank}}, ahead). Rows from a published leaderboard are kept apart from scores and from every count. Fewer than two distinct models returns 400. Without benchmark or models the route returns 400.

Undocumented parameters

/compare also accepts task: with no benchmark, it answers as /best for that task. This parameter is not in openapi.json or tools.json.

docs.title: GET /stats
docs.text: No parameters. Returns counts grouped as documents (mapped, by_role, sources), imaging (CT volumes and slices, MRI and chest X-ray studies), graph (nodes, edges, kinds), concepts, food_atlas, datasets (total, by_modality, by_access, by_status), benchmarks (language, language_scored, imaging_multimodal, tabular, forecasting, capabilities), models (with_scores, baselines_scored, by_type, evaluated, how_to_count), literature (concepts, articles) and knowledge_graphs (graphs, triples, subjects, objects, predicates, built). Cached for an hour per snapshot.

docs.title: GET /search, GET /node/{id}, GET /neighborhood
docs.text:
/search takes q (required), kind (one of concept, disease, food, dataset, llm-benchmark, model, specialty, capability) and limit (default 20, at most 100). Matching scores label hits above description hits; terms of three characters or fewer must match a whole word; with several terms, at least half must match. Returns query, count and results[] of {id, label, kind, summary, modality, url}.

/node/{id} returns the node's public fields (from a fixed whitelist: grounding, MeSH and Wikipedia identifiers, description, modality, domain, metric, origin, stage, tokens, documents, access, contamination, training use, and so on), url, links grouped by relation (incoming relations suffixed (in), at most 25 per relation, numeric edge values such as value and metric kept), link_count, and an evaluation block for models and evaluated benchmarks. Unknown id: 404.

/neighborhood takes ids (comma-separated, at most 12). It returns nodes[] (each with role: seed or link, up to 14 links per seed) and edges[] of {from, to, rel}, at most 400.

docs.title: GET /datasets and GET /datasets/{slug}
docs.text:
/datasets takes q, modality (for example text, imaging-ct, knowledge-graph, structured), access (open, public, internal, restricted, credentialed), status (listed, active, measured, on-disk, acquiring, building), limit (default 25, at most 200) and offset. Returns count and results[] with slug, name, desc (trimmed), modality, license, access, status, dtype, owner, url.

/datasets/{slug} matches a slug or a URN and returns the public record: urn, slug, name, desc, modality fields, licence fields, access, status, citation, owner, scale, documents, split_role, stage, domain_mix, corpus_membership, grounding, models_trained, artifact_types, linked_nodes, used_in_training, caveats, url, and evaluation when the dataset is a scored benchmark. Field meanings are in Dataset registry.

docs.title: GET /literature/{node}
docs.text: limit default 10, at most 50. Returns node, count (all stored articles) and articles[] with pmid, title, journal, date, pubdate, authors, doi. See the literature feed.

docs.title: GET /kg/graphs
docs.text: No parameters. Returns the store manifest kg_graphs.json: store, built, totals (triples, subjects, objects, predicates), note, and graphs[] (name, graph IRI, triples, version, family). The served copy at the repository's HEAD describes 44 graphs and 6,994,341,217 triples, built 2026-10-03. See Knowledge store.

docs.title: GET /teaser/{part}
docs.text: part is one of xy, color, nodes, edges. Returns the public low-resolution universe geometry as application/octet-stream. This route is registered but not listed in openapi.json or tools.json.

docs.title: Using the API from a language model
docs.text:
A client needs only tools.json. Load the tools, call each tool's path with the model's arguments as query parameters (substituting path parameters such as {id}), and return the result to the model. Each tool is {"type": "function", "path": "/best", "function": {"name", "description", "parameters"}}. The file also carries suggested system text:

PanAtlas has measured scores for language, vision, multimodal, tabular and forecasting models. For "which model is best" questions call best_models first. Answer only from tool results. Name the benchmark, the score and the best baseline. Compare values only within one benchmark. Before saying PanAtlas has nothing on a topic, check atlas_overview.

Because clients load tools from tools.json at run time, a new tool reaches them without a change on their side. The first external client works this way, with a one-hour cache (docs/public-api.md).

curl -s 'https://panatlas.net/wp-json/panatlas/public/v1/best?task=pathology%20encoders&limit=3'
curl -s 'https://panatlas.net/wp-json/panatlas/public/v1/search?q=cardiology&kind=specialty'
curl -s 'https://panatlas.net/wp-json/panatlas/public/v1/overview'

docs.title: Where the data comes from
docs.text:
The API reads the snapshot files in the plugin's data/ directory, rebuilt by the build pipeline:

File Built by Feeds evals_index.json web/build_evals_index.py from benchmarks_llm.json, full_eval.json, mm_evals.json, predictor_evals.json, models.json Every evaluation route, the evaluation blocks on nodes and datasets, /stats model counts graph.json Graph builders and build_all.sh /search, /node, /neighborhood, /stats datasets.json sync_catalog.py /datasets, /stats benchmarks_llm.json, mm_evals.json Benchmark builders, build_patho_evals.py, cluster ingest /benchmarks/{id} catalog fields, /stats kg_graphs.json The SPARQL store build /kg/graphs, /stats Literature files Nightly feed on the web host /literature, /stats

The evaluation records themselves are described in Evaluation records and Benchmarks.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
• 1.1.1 (2026-10-31). best_models leads with a task that holds every specific word of the question (answer_from); a word in a task's name outranks one in its description; pathology and radiology foundation models read as image encoders. compare_models covers held-out models, adds head_to_head on tasks both finished, and uses published_leaderboard rows for methods without a run of panAtlas's own, kept apart from scores and counts. /models and /stats explain their counts. /best accepts q or question.
  • 1.1.0 (2026-10-31). Every evaluation for every model type through one set of routes. New tools best_models, atlas_overview, task_scores, query_scores. Corrected scores that a substring join had attached to the wrong language benchmarks since 2026-08-05.
  • 1.0.0 (2026-10-25). First public release.

docs.title: The site: panatlas.net
docs.text:
panatlas.net is a WordPress site on the web host. Almost all of panAtlas's behaviour lives in one custom plugin, panatlas-explorer (version 0.2.2, web/wp-plugin/panatlas-explorer/), with a small custom theme (web/wp-theme/panatlas/). The plugin reads static JSON files and streams large assets; it does not keep the atlas in the database.

Part Files Plugin core: roles, audit, access gate, explorer and universe shortcodes, gated REST routes, Navigator, model lens panatlas-explorer.php Public read-only API includes/public-api.php, includes/public-evals.php World map includes/wikimap.php, assets/wikimap.js Agent-network panel includes/mesh.php Federation admin portal includes/federation-admin.php Front end assets/app.js (Cytoscape.js 3.30.2 from a CDN), assets/style.css, assets/universe.js, assets/universe-bg.js with assets/cosmos.bundle.mjs Served data data/graph.json, datasets.json, benchmarks_llm.json, mm_evals.json, evals_index.json, models.json, kg_graphs.json; data/mesh.json is written live on the server

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page Shortcode What it shows Front page [panatlas_explorer] (the theme's front-page.php emits only this) The explorer, or the teaser for visitors without access /universe/ [panatlas_universe] Every document placed by concept, with the graph overlaid /world-map/ [panatlas_wikimap] The known-world map from the Wikipedia layer /agent-network [panatlas_mesh] The live Cresco mesh (also rendered inside the explorer's Mesh view) /api/ [panatlas_api_docs] Generated documentation of the public API

docs.title: The explorer
docs.text:
The explorer is a single-page app (assets/app.js) inside the [panatlas_explorer] shortcode. Its header has these views:

View What it is Home What panAtlas is and where to start; headline counts and entry cards Map The ontology-grounded concept hierarchy, as a tree or an interactive graph. Clicking a node re-centres on its neighbourhood (focus plus context; never the whole graph) Datasets The audited data catalog: every dataset with modality, scale, embedding model, host and audit manifest Models Each model with what it was trained on and evaluated on, per-concept accuracy, a modality filter, and the model lens Coverage & Gaps Per-concept training exposure set against model scores, artifact-type gaps, decontamination status Benchmarks Every benchmark as an audited list or a similarity map (the audit.map projection from the build) Universe Opens /universe/ Mesh The live Cresco agent mesh

Alongside the views are a search box, a context bar, a detail panel for the selected node, and the Navigator panel. A deep link of the form /#node=<id> opens a node's detail panel; the public API returns links in that form.

docs.title: Node detail and the literature feed
docs.text:
A node's detail panel shows its grounding, provenance and links. For concepts, specialties and diseases that carry a MeSH descriptor, the panel loads a Recent literature block from GET /panatlas/v1/literature?node=<id>.

The feed is built nightly on the web host by web/pipeline/literature/fetch_literature.py (standard library only, run from cron with a lock). For every MeSH-grounded node it searches PubMed by MeSH term, sorted by date, diffs the PMIDs against what it already stores, and fetches only new ones. It stores verified NCBI metadata only: PMID, title, journal, date, authors and DOI; no model output. A partial failure skips that concept and never kills the run. Measured on the full run of 2026-08-15: 3,368 nodes, 31,634 articles, 0 failures. An "in training corpus" badge is shown only from the exact PMC identity map (web/pipeline/literature/attach_pmc_identity.py), never from an approximation.

docs.title: Navigator: ask where to go
docs.text:
The Navigator turns a question into a focused view of the graph. POST /panatlas/v1/navigate with {query} (at most 2,000 characters) does this in panatlas_navigate():

  1. Retrieve. Score every node by term overlap: label hits weigh more than hits in descriptions, audit fields, domains or capabilities. Keep the top 24 seeds.
  2. Expand. Add the seeds' neighbours, up to 220 nodes, and collect the edges among them (at most 600).
  3. Ground. Add a modality census from mm_evals.json, so a question about multi-modal or vision models is never answered with a text model.
  4. Ask. Send the subgraph and the question to the hosted LLM endpoint with temperature 0 and a JSON-schema response format {answer, focus[], intent} (constrained decoding).
  5. Validate. Drop any focus id not in the subgraph, default the intent, and supply a fallback answer if the model returned none. The UI then re-centres the map on the focus nodes.

Every call is written to the audit log. Without a configured key the route answers "Navigator offline".

A debug path exists

A query that begins with DEBUG returns diagnostics (HTTP status from the LLM endpoint, seed, node and edge counts, finish reason, and the start of the raw body) instead of an answer. It is reachable by any user who passes the access gate.

docs.title: Model lens
docs.text:
In the Models view, POST /panatlas/v1/model-lens with {query} (at most 500 characters) asks the same endpoint which benchmarks measure what the user cares about: an evaluation type, a medical topic, or a combination ("cardiology QA", "reading reports, not multiple-choice"). The lens prompt is written for today's holdings, where medicine runs deepest. The catalog it chooses from is the union of benchmarks in the model batteries plus the imaging and multi-modal benchmarks. The reply is constrained to {explanation, benchmarks[]}; names not in the catalog are dropped, and an empty selection falls back to the medical knowledge core. The ranking then re-scores models over just that subset. The route releases the PHP session lock first, so a second lens call from the same browser does not queue behind the first.

Navigator model: documentation and code differ

web/README.md and docs/panatlas-system-and-interface.md name a Gemma model as the Navigator. The code sets PANATLAS_NAV_MODEL to the WordPress option panatlas_nav_model, defaulting to zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, with a comment that the Gemma model was retired on the endpoint. The code is authoritative.

docs.title: Universe
docs.text:
The universe page draws every document as a point placed by concept, with the knowledge graph overlaid as a backbone. Its assets are built on the cluster (web/dgx/build_universe*.py, web/pipeline/universe/), stored outside the web root, and streamed through GET /panatlas/v1/universe-asset?f=<part>&tier=<tier>:

f Content xy Point positions, uint16 pairs (per tier) color Point colours, uint8 (per tier) meta universe_meta.json nodes, edges The backbone overlay

Tiers, measured on the 2026-09-24 rebuild that added arXiv: xs 250,107 points, s 1,500,021, m 5,998,856, full 93,056,465. The page then fetches the graph to link points back to the explorer.

Default tier

A code comment says s (1.5M) is the light default. The code falls back to xs when no tier is given.

The teaser shown to visitors without access uses a separate, public, low-resolution version of the same cloud (assets/teaser_*.bin, drawn by assets/universe-bg.js).

docs.title: World map
docs.text: /world-map/ renders the known-world map from the Wikipedia world-view layer: the pinned English Wikipedia run 20260901 (7,234,748 articles) laid out by topic, with each article coloured by how strongly the atlas's documents cover it. The layer gives every document one primary Wikipedia link with an evidence class (strong, medium, lexical agreement, curated bridge, weak). Assets stream from outside the web root through GET /panatlas/v1/wikimap-asset?f=<part>, where f is one of lod_top, lod_links, lod_covered, mesh, categories, art_xy, art_cov, manifest. The page is installed by web/wikimap/install_wikimap.sh; the chain that builds the layer is in web/wikipedia_layer/.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: Sign-in is ORCID through OpenID Connect, using the OpenID Connect Generic plugin with the openid scope (README.md §5). The ORCID iD (the OIDC sub) becomes the WordPress username. ORCID does not release email under that scope, so each account gets a synthetic, non-delivering address. Any ORCID holder can create an account; new accounts get the WordPress subscriber role, which the plugin grants pa_read and pa_suggest.

docs.title: Roles and capabilities
docs.text: Role Capabilities pa_member_viewer pa_read pa_domain_editor pa_read, pa_suggest, pa_edit pa_reviewer pa_read, pa_suggest, pa_verify pa_super_curator all five, including pa_admin WordPress administrator all five (the fallback account)

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
Having an account is not enough to see the atlas. Every atlas view and every gated route goes through panatlas_may_access(), which allows:

  1. the site administrator (manage_options), or
  2. a signed-in user whose username contains an ORCID iD on an allowlist held as a constant in the plugin.

Everyone else gets the teaser: anonymous visitors see "Sign in with ORCID", and signed-in users who are not on the list see "Your account is not authorized to view the atlas" with a switch-account link. The same allowlist is configured in the Astral agent, and web/astral/tests/test_authorized_identities.py asserts that the required iDs are present in both places, so a change to one cannot silently drop a curator from the other.

Why the sign-in link points straight at ORCID. On 2026-08-06 the shared web host restricted WordPress's login and admin paths to internal networks after an incident. Both sign-in links (the theme header and the teaser) were changed on 2026-08-24 to render the plugin-generated ORCID authorisation URL, and the restriction gained a narrow exemption for the OIDC authorise action only. The OIDC callback goes through a public endpoint. Password login and the admin area stay restricted. The server-side rule is kept in the repository as web/infra/lockdown-wp-admin.conf.

Hardening. For anonymous visitors the plugin removes the WordPress users REST endpoints and redirects author archives and ?author= probes to the home page, so usernames cannot be enumerated.

Older text says viewing is public

docs/panatlas-system-and-interface.md (written 2026-08-01) lists /graph, /datasets, /benchmarks, /navigate and /mesh as public, a comment in the plugin still says "Public read endpoints (viewing is open to everyone)", and the Navigator's hint text says "Anyone can explore". In the code every one of these routes checks panatlas_may_access; anonymous requests get 401 (confirmed live on 2026-09-12 for graph and datasets). The open, read-only surface is the public API.

docs.title: The audit log
docs.text: The plugin creates a table panatlas_audit (with the WordPress prefix) holding the time, user id, ORCID iD, the roles held at that moment, the action, a detail string and the client address. Actions written by the code are view_explorer, view_universe, view_wikimap, navigate, navigate_error, model_lens, propose_change and link_astral_orcid; the federation portal also writes its actions here. Site administrators see the latest 200 rows under the PanAtlas Audit admin menu.

docs.title: Gated private assets
docs.text:
Large or sensitive files live in a private directory beside, not inside, the web document root, and reach the browser only through gated routes:

Asset Route Notes Universe tiers and backbone universe-asset Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600; streamed in 1 MB chunks World-map layout wikimap-asset Same pattern Literature feed (lit_<node>.json) literature Rebuilt nightly

Each request carries the WordPress REST nonce and the session cookie. An unknown part returns 404 unknown asset; a part not built yet returns 404 not built yet.

docs.title: REST routes (panatlas/v1, gated)
docs.text:
All paths are under https://panatlas.net/wp-json/panatlas/v1. Responses are raw JSON, not wrapped.

Method Path Permission Returns GET /graph access gate graph.json: {stats, roots, nodes[], edges[]} GET /datasets access gate {datasets[], meta, models} from datasets.json and models.json GET /benchmarks access gate benchmarks_llm.json GET /mm-evals access gate mm_evals.json POST /navigate access gate {answer, focus[], intent} POST /model-lens access gate {explanation, benchmarks[], task_types[], catalog[]} GET /literature?node=<id> access gate The stored feed for that node, or {articles: []} GET /universe-asset?f=&tier= access gate Binary or JSON stream GET /wikimap-asset?f= access gate Binary or JSON stream GET /mesh access gate (since 2026-10-25, because the snapshot carries internal node addresses) The mesh snapshot from data/mesh.json GET /whoami open {orcid, name, roles[], rights[]}; a guest gets name: "guest" and empty lists POST /propose signed in with pa_suggest Records {target, change} (change ≤ 4,000 characters) in the audit log; returns {ok, status, by, rights}. Never publishes GET /federate/agents open (redacted); full profiles for pa_admin The federation agent directory, never token hashes POST /federate/agents/register pa_admin Registers an agent and mints a one-time token POST /federate/agents/update pa_admin Changes tier or status, rotates a token

The federation routes and the admin portal are described in Federation and Contract.

No agent submission route

web/federation/pa_agent.py posts reports to POST /panatlas/v1/federate. The plugin registers no such route; contributions arrive over the Cresco control plane instead. See Distributed.

The Astral identity link has its own entry point on the front controller, /?panatlas_astral_orcid_link=1, so it works from outside the restricted login paths (Astral).

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The front-end assets, the served data and the public API includes are deployed by web/deploy.sh; other plugin files, the world map and the universe assets are deployed separately. See Build pipeline. A repository audit on 2026-09-13 found the live plugin identical to the repository for all 28 shared files, with data/mesh.json the only file that exists only on the server by design.
